September 2022 |title=Bolsonarista é preso após atirar contra carro de deputado durante comício em Minas Gerais |url=https://horadopovo.com.br/bolsonarista-e-preso-apos-atirar-contra-carro-de-deputado-durante-comicio-em-minas-gerais/ |access-date=29 September 2022 |website=Hora do Povo |language=pt |archive-date=2 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221002005552/https://horadopovo.com.br/bolsonarista-e-preso-apos-atirar-contra-carro-de-deputado-durante-comicio-em-minas-gerais/ |url-status=live}} On 4 October, José Roberto Gomes Mendes, a 59-year-old Bolsonaro supporter, was murdered after an argument over politics with Luiz Antonio Ferreira da Silva, a 42-year-old Workers' Party supporter, inside their home in the city of [[Itanhaém]], in the state of [[São Paulo (state)|São Paulo]]. During the argument, Mendes allegedly attacked Silva with a knife, and during the fight, Silva used the same knife to stab Mendes. The police later arrived at the scene and found that Mendes had died of his wounds. Silva confessed the crime to the police.{{cite news | url=https://www.bbc.com/portuguese/brasil-63152266 | title=Petista mata amigo bolsonarista a facadas em discussão política; veja outros casos | work=BBC News Brasil |date=5 October 2022 |language=pt|access-date=1 November 2022}} On 12 October, Bolsonaro visited the [[Basilica of Our Lady of Aparecida]] in São Paulo to accompany the religious celebrations. Supporters of the president promoted riots outside the time and attacked journalists who were covering the ceremony including those of the ''TV Aparecida'', which is owned by the church, and the ''TV Vanguarda'', which is affiliated to the [[TV Globo]]. They also attacked a man with a red shirt and booed an [[archbishop]] who spoke out against hunger.{{cite web |last=Varella|first=Thiago|date=12 October 2022|title=Imagens de bolsonaristas hostilizando imprensa em Aparecida viralizam |url=https://noticias.uol.com.br/eleicoes/2022/10/12/imagens-de-bolsonaristas-hostilizando-imprensa-em-aparecida-viralizam.htm |access-date=30 October 2022 |publisher=Universo Online |language=pt}} On 13 August 2021, former lawmaker and Bolsonaro ally [[Roberto Jefferson]] was arrested due to his verbal threats to government officials and institutions. In January 2022, he was allowed to be moved to [[house arrest]] for health reasons under the conditions that he would not maintain external communication or receive visits other than by family members.{{cite news |date=24 October 2022|title=A cronologia da prisão de Roberto Jefferson |language=pt |work=BBC News Brasil |url=https://www.bbc.com/portuguese/brasil-63375361 |access-date=1 November 2022}} Jefferson violated these conditions multiple times, and he attempted to be a presidential candidate in the 2022 election under the [[Brazilian Labour Party (current)|Brazilian Labour Party]] but was ruled ineligible due to a previous criminal conviction and was replaced by Kelmon Souza as his party's candidate. On 21 October, Jefferson released a video, through his daughter [[Cristiane Brasil]], where he insulted Supreme Federal Court judge [[Cármen Lúcia]] due to rulings that she issued in the 2022 presidential election.{{cite news | last=Albuquerque|first=Mariana|url=https://www.correiobraziliense.com.br/politica/2022/10/5046543-tse-manda-apagar-video-em-que-roberto-jefferson-xinga-ministra-carmen-lucia.html |title=TSE manda apagar vídeo em que Roberto Jefferson xinga ministra Cármen Lúcia |work=Correio Braziliense |date=24 October 2022 |language=pt|access-date=1 November 2022}} Due to Jefferson's multiple violations of his house arrest conditions, Supreme Federal Court judge [[Alexandre de Moraes]] ordered his return to prison. On 23 October, Jefferson violently resisted the [[arrest warrant]] being carried out by Federal Police agents, who were met with gunfire and two [[grenade]]s thrown by him. Some of the agents were injured during the [[siege]], subsequently hospitalized, and later released. Hours after negotiating his surrender terms along with other Bolsonaro allies present in his house, Jefferson turned himself in to the police and was later indicted for four attempted homicides of the agents that he had attacked earlier.{{cite news |last1=Brito |first1=Ricardo|last2=Gaier |first2=Rodrigo Viga |last3=Paraguassu |first3=Lisandra |date=23 October 2022 |title=Brazilian politician surrenders after injuring policemen while resisting arrest |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/brazilian-politician-resists-arrest-fires-police-2022-10-23/ |access-date=24 October 2022}}{{cite news |last1=Prado |first1=Bruna |last2=Savarese |first2=Mauricio |title=Brazil pol and Bolsonaro ally refuses arrest, injures police |newspaper=The Washington Post |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/brazil-pol-and-bolsonaro-ally-refuses-arrest-injures-police/2022/10/23/f8551cdc-5321-11ed-ac8b-08bbfab1c5a5_story.html |access-date=24 October 2022 |issn=0190-8286}} === Disinformation === [[File:Lula ladrão roubou meu coração (cropped).jpg|thumb|Graffiti in Rio de Janeiro which says, "''Thief Lula'' (in brown), ''stole my heart!'' (in black)." This graffiti was likely originally from a Bolsonaro supporter, whose meaning was changed by a Lula supporter.]] [[Disinformation]] became a major topic in the 2022 elections, since experiences from previous elections, especially in 2018, led to new approaches by individuals, including electoral officials, as well as private and public [[institution]]s amid a surge in the use of fake news to discredit political opponents and the electoral system itself.{{Cite web |date=7 July 2022 |title=Missão brasileira discute estratégias de combate à desinformação com a União Europeia |url=https://www.tse.jus.br/comunicacao/noticias/2022/Julho/missao-brasileira-discute-estrategias-de-combate-a-desinformacao-com-a-uniao-europeia |access-date=25 September 2022 |website=Tribunal Superior Eleitoral |archive-date=2 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221002010055/https://www.tse.jus.br/comunicacao/noticias/2022/Julho/missao-brasileira-discute-estrategias-de-combate-a-desinformacao-com-a-uniao-europeia |url-status=live}} In that context, the Superior Electoral Court issued several law-like guidances regarding disinformation, such as further banning [[political ads]] on the internet, and tightening penalties for online breaches of the electoral law. In October 2021, after an investigation by the police and prosecutors, the Superior Electoral Court ruled that [[Fernando Francischini]], a hard-liner lawmaker in the southern state of [[Paraná (state)|Paraná]] and ally of Bolsonaro, had violated electoral law by making false claims about the electronic voting system in 2018. The court removed him from his seat in the state legislature and banned him from elected office for the next eight years.{{Cite web |title=TSE cassa por 6 votos a 1 deputado do PR acusado de divulgar 'fake news' sobre urnas eletrônicas |url=https://g1.globo.com/politica/noticia/2021/10/28/tse-tem-maioria-para-cassar-politico-que-divulgou-fake-news-contra-urnas-eletronicas.ghtml |access-date=25 September 2022 |website=G1 |date=28 October 2021 |language=pt |archive-date=28 October 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211028152712/https://g1.globo.com/politica/noticia/2021/10/28/tse-tem-maioria-para-cassar-politico-que-divulgou-fake-news-contra-urnas-eletronicas.ghtml |url-status=live}} Francischini filed an appeal against the ruling but it was later dismissed by the Supreme Federal Court.{{Cite web |date=8 June 2022 |title=STF mantém cassação do deputado estadual do PR Fernando Francischini |url=https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/radioagencia-nacional/justica/audio/2022-06/stf-mantem-cassacao-do-deputado-estadual-do-pr-fernando-francischini |access-date=25 September 2022 |website=Agência Brasil |language=pt |archive-date=30 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220830233712/https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/radioagencia-nacional/justica/audio/2022-06/stf-mantem-cassacao-do-deputado-estadual-do-pr-fernando-francischini |url-status=live}} On 20 September 2022, the Superior Electoral Court reported that it had received more than 15,500 election-related disinformation complaints over the prior four months.{{Cite web |last=Rocha |first=Lucas |title=TSE recebeu 15,5 mil denúncias de fake news em quatro meses |url=https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/politica/tse-recebeu-155-mil-denuncias-de-fake-news-em-quatro-meses/ |access-date=6 October 2022 |website=CNN Brasil |language=pt}} On 24 September, an incident of [[bulk messaging]] was reported in the state of [[Paraná (state)|Paraná]], which was governed by an ally of Bolsonaro. Several phone users said that they had received a message from the official state alert-messaging service,{{Cite web |date=24 September 2022 |title=Disparo em massa com ameaças a favor de Bolsonaro vira alvo de investigação no Paraná |url=https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/poder/2022/09/disparo-em-massa-com-ameacas-a-favor-de-bolsonaro-vira-alvo-de-investigacao-no-parana.shtml |access-date=25 September 2022 |website=Folha de S.Paulo |language=pt |archive-date=25 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220925225106/https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/poder/2022/09/disparo-em-massa-com-ameacas-a-favor-de-bolsonaro-vira-alvo-de-investigacao-no-parana.shtml |url-status=live}} which read: "Bolsonaro is gonna win the elections in the first round! Otherwise, we are going to the streets to protest! We're gonna storm the Supreme Court and the Congress buildings! President Bolsonaro counts on us all!!" The Superior Electoral Court referred the alleged breach to prosecutors so they could investigate if any electoral crime was committed, and if so, to identify its perpetrators.{{Cite web |title=TSE comunica Ministério Público sobre disparos com mensagem golpista pró-Bolsonaro no Paraná |url=https://www.folhape.com.br/politica/tse-comunica-ministerio-publico-sobre-disparos-com-mensagem-golpista/241326/ |access-date=25 September 2022 |website=Folha PE |language=pt |archive-date=25 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220925225107/https://www.folhape.com.br/politica/tse-comunica-ministerio-publico-sobre-disparos-com-mensagem-golpista/241326/ |url-status=live}} === Electoral fraud allegations === {{See also|Planning for a coup d'état after the 2022 Brazilian presidential elections}} Bolsonaro alleged that [[electronic voting in Brazil]] was prone to [[vote rigging]] since at least 2015, when he was a member of the [[Chamber of Deputies (Brazil)|Chamber of Deputies]], and successfully pushed for a bill requiring voting machines to also print vote records. Brazil's [[Public Prosecutor's Office (Brazil)|Public Prosecutor's Office]] challenged the law citing [[secret ballot]] concerns,{{cite web |title=Raquel Dodge pede ao STF para derrubar exigência de impressão dos votos pelas urnas eletrônicas |url=https://g1.globo.com/politica/noticia/raquel-dodge-pede-ao-stf-para-derrubar-obrigatoriedade-de-impressao-dos-votos-pelas-urnas-eletronicas.ghtml Noticias |language=pt |archive-date=2 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221002010054/https://br.noticias.yahoo.com/a-4-dias-das-eleicoes-partido-de-bolsonaro-diz-que-encontrou-falhas-no-tse-203041976.html |url-status=live}} ==== Reactions to potential coup ==== On 26 July, the [[faculty of law]] of the [[University of São Paulo]] launched a pro-democracy petition as a response to Bolsonaro's criticism of the electronic ballots and the Brazilian voting system in general with over 3,000 signatures, among intellectuals, artists, law experts including retired justices of the Supreme Federal Court, businesspeople, and others.{{cite news|last=Freire|first=Marcelo |date=26 July 2022|title=Faculdade de Direito da USP organiza manifesto em defesa da democracia; leia íntegra |url=https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/politica/faculdade-de-direito-da-usp-organiza-manifesto-em-defesa-da-democracia-leia-integra/ |access-date=2 November 2022 |work=CNN Brasil |language=pt}} On 30 July, the petition topped 540,000 signatures, and four days later reached 700,000 endorsements.{{cite news |date=30 July 2022 |title=Pro-democracy petition garners 500,000 signatures in Brazil |url=https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20220730-pro-democracy-petition-garners-500-000-signatures-in-brazil |access-date=2 November 2022 |work=France 24 |publisher=Agence France-Presse}}{{cite magazine |date=3 August 2022 |title=Carta pela democracia supera 700 mil adesões |url=https://exame.com/brasil/carta-pela-democracia-supera-700-mil-adesoes/ |access-date=2 November 2022 |magazine=Exame |language=pt}} On 17 August, a report by Brazilian newspaper ''Metrópoles'' leaked an online conversation by a group of pro-Bolsonaro businessmen who expressed their preference for a [[coup d'état]] rather than a return of [[Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva]] to the presidency. The businessmen stated that the Supreme Federal Court and the Superior Electoral Court were suspected of election fraud, and proposed that a separate commission recount the votes. The messages also showed that business leader José Koury floated the idea of paying a bonus to employees who voted according to their employers' interests, if it were legal, and that malls chain businessman {{ill|José Isaac Peres|pt}} ordered "thousands of little flags" to be distributed to shopkeepers and customers in Barra World Shopping, one of his company's malls. In response to the report, the businessmen declared their support for democracy and denied any encouragement of illegal activity.{{cite web |last1=Amado|first1=Guilherme|last2=Ghirotto|first2=Edoardo|last3=Lima|first3=Bruna|date=17 August 2022 |title=Exclusivo. Empresários bolsonaristas defendem golpe de Estado caso Lula seja eleito; veja zaps |url=https://www.metropoles.com/colunas/guilherme-amado/exclusivo-empresarios-bolsonaristas-defendem-golpe-de-estado-caso-lula-seja-eleito-veja-zaps |access-date=24 August 2022 |website=Metrópoles |language=pt |archive-date=18 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220818231813/https://www.metropoles.com/colunas/guilherme-amado/exclusivo-empresarios-bolsonaristas-defendem-golpe-de-estado-caso-lula-seja-eleito-veja-zaps |url-status=live}}{{cite web |last1=Amaral |first1=Jordi|last2=Kohan|first2=Arianna |date=18 August 2022|title=Pro-Bolsonaro businessmen show support for coup |url=https://latinamericadailybriefing.substack.com/p/pro-bolsonaro-businessmen-show-support |access-date=19 August 2022 |website=Latin America Daily Briefing |archive-date=18 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220818151319/https://latinamericadailybriefing.substack.com/p/pro-bolsonaro-businessmen-show-support |url-status=live}} On 23 August, by order of the Supreme Federal Court, the Federal Police carried out [[search and seizure]] warrants on the homes, offices, and other properties of the businessmen who allegedly supported a potential coup, including Koury, Peres, and billionaire [[Luciano Hang]], among others.{{Cite news |last1=Brito |first1=Ricardo |last2=Gaier |first2=Rodrigo Viga |last3=Romani |first3=Andre |date=23 August 2022 |title=Brazilian police raid pro-Bolsonaro businessmen accused of coup talk, sources say |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/brazil-police-raid-pro-bolsonaro-businessmen-accused-coup-talk-sources-say-2022-08-23/ |access-date=2 November 2022}} The court also ordered a freeze in their bank and social media accounts, their testimonies, and access to their [[financial records]]. The businessmen stated that this order constituted political persecution and an attack on their freedom of speech.{{cite web |last=Bomfim|first=Camila|date=23 August 2022| title=Moraes determina buscas em endereços de empresários por supostas mensagens golpistas |url=https://g1.globo.com/politica/noticia/2022/08/23/moraes-determina-buscas-em-enderecos-de-empresarios-por-supostas-mensagens-golpistas.ghtml |access-date=23 August 2022 |website=G1 |language=pt |archive-date=23 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220823200304/https://g1.globo.com/politica/noticia/2022/08/23/moraes-determina-buscas-em-enderecos-de-empresarios-por-supostas-mensagens-golpistas.ghtml |url-status=live}} ===== International reactions ===== On 9 June, Bolsonaro and U.S. president [[Joe Biden]] met during the [[Summit of the Americas]] in Los Angeles. Anonymous sources reported to [[Bloomberg News]] that Bolsonaro asked for Biden's help with the elections, saying that a possible administration of former president Lula would be against U.S. interests. Biden changed the subject when approached but emphasized the importance of keeping the integrity of Brazil's elections.{{cite web|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-06-11/brazil-s-bolsonaro-asked-biden-for-re-election-help-against-lula|title=Brazil's Bolsonaro Asked Biden for Re-Election Help Against Lula|website=Bloomberg|first=Eric|last=Martin|date=11 June 2022|access-date=6 September 2022|archive-date=11 July 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220711230832/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-06-11/brazil-s-bolsonaro-asked-biden-for-re-election-help-against-lula|url-status=live}} Bolsonaro answered that he respected democracy and would respect the election results. Biden's response echoed the comments made by [[Elizabeth Frawley Bagley]], the U.S. ambassador to Brazil nominated by Biden. Portuguese/Spanish-language spokesperson of the [[U.S. Department of State]], Kristina Rosales, argued that the elections needed to be transparent and monitored by international observers. Brazil's justice minister [[Anderson Torres]] responded that international observers were of little help and favored the participation of the Federal Police, the [[Brazilian Armed Forces]], and civil society in the elections.{{cite web|url=https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/mundo/2022/06/biden-disse-a-bolsonaro-que-confia-no-sistema-eleitoral-do-brasil-afirma-porta-voz.shtml|title=Biden disse a Bolsonaro que confia no sistema eleitoral do Brasil, afirma porta-voz|website=Folha de S. |archive-date=2 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221002010614/https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20220929-us-senator-sanders-urges-respect-for-brazil-presidential-vote |url-status=live}} === Voter suppression attempts === On 27 September, it was reported that some public transportation companies, most of them bus companies, as well as city administrations whose mayors were Bolsonaro allies, could either suspend some buses operations, claim a lack of funding for [[free travel pass]]es that were usually granted to voters on election day, or order the vehicles sabotaged and engage in [[voter suppression]]. Poor and extremely poor voters, among whom Lula had been leading in the polls, were supposed to be the main target of this strategy, since they could only resort to [[public transportation]] on their way to the [[polling stations]] and back home.{{Cite web |title=PT teme que donos de empresas de ônibus pró-Bolsonaro reduzam frotas para sabotar eleitor de baixa renda |url=https://theintercept.com/notas/pt-teme-que-empresas-de-onibus-pro-bolsonaro-reduzam-frotas/ |access-date=1 October 2022 |website=The Intercept Brasil |date=27 September 2022 |language=pt |archive-date=27 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220927183419/https://theintercept.com/notas/pt-teme-que-empresas-de-onibus-pro-bolsonaro-reduzam-frotas/ |url-status=live}} ==== In the first round ==== Despite some city administrations and Senator [[Randolfe Rodrigues]] asking the Supreme Federal Court to grant free rides for voters on election day,{{Cite web |date=29 September 2022 |title=Painel S.A.: Prefeitos reforçam ação no STF por transporte de graça na eleição |url=https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/colunas/painelsa/2022/09/prefeitos-reforcam-acao-no-stf-por-transporte-de-graca-na-eleicao.shtml |access-date=1 October 2022 |website=Folha de S.Paulo |language=pt}}{{Cite web |title=Chico Alves – Após suspensões, STF é acionado para manter passe livre no dia da eleição |url=https://noticias.uol.com.br/colunas/chico-alves/2022/09/28/randolfe-vai-ao-stf-para-garantir-passe-livre-em-todo-o-brasil-na-eleicao.htm |access-date=1 October 2022 |website=noticias.uol.com.br |language=pt |archive-date=2 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221002010056/https://noticias.uol.com.br/colunas/chico-alves/2022/09/28/randolfe-vai-ao-stf-para-garantir-passe-livre-em-todo-o-brasil-na-eleicao.htm |url-status=live}} [[Porto Alegre]], a major city in southern Brazil whose mayor was a Bolsonaro supporter, announced that it was going to cut free travel passes because of "budgetary costs" for the first time in 25 years;{{Cite web |date=28 September 2022 |title=Porto Alegre terá primeira eleição sem passe livre nos ônibus em 27 anos |url=https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/cotidiano/2022/09/porto-alegre-tera-primeira-eleicao-sem-passe-livre-nos-onibus-em-27-anos.shtml |access-date=1 October 2022 |website=Folha de S.Paulo |language=pt |archive-date=2 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221002010614/https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/cotidiano/2022/09/porto-alegre-tera-primeira-eleicao-sem-passe-livre-nos-onibus-em-27-anos.shtml |url-status=live}} after intense scrutiny by critics and politicians, it gave up on the plan. On 29 September, the Supreme Federal Court issued an injunction blocking public transportation operations from being reduced on election day.{{Cite web |last=Audi |first=Amanda |date=29 September 2022 |title=Brazilian state capitals announce free bus fares on Election Day |url=https://brazilian.report/liveblog/2022/09/29/election-day-bus-fares/ |access-date=1 October 2022 |website=The Brazilian Report |archive-date=2 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221002010622/https://brazilian.report/liveblog/2022/09/29/election-day-bus-fares/ |url-status=live}}{{Cite web |title=Ministro do STF determina transporte público em nível normal no dia 2 |url=https://esportes.yahoo.com/ministro-stf-determina-transporte-p%C3%BAblico-134600021.html |access-date=1 October 2022 |website=Yahoo Esportes |language=pt |archive-date=2 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221002010614/https://esportes.yahoo.com/ministro-stf-determina-transporte-p%C3%BAblico-134600021.html |url-status=live}} On 1 October, the Bolsonaro campaign asked the Superior Electoral Court to immediately block free travel passes in the public transportation system, arguing that the Supreme Federal Court's previous decision would hurt the cities' finances since the costs of free rides on election day were allegedly not anticipated and previously agreed upon by their legislatures. The Superior Electoral Court rejected the request, saying that no additional costs were created for the cities.{{Cite web |title=TSE rejeita pedido de Bolsonaro contra transporte em nível normal no domingo |url=https://noticias.uol.com.br/ultimas-noticias/agencia-estado/2022/10/01/tse-rejeita-pedido-de-bolsonaro-contra-transporte-em-nivel-normal-no-domingo.htm |access-date=2 October 2022 |website=noticias.uol.com.br |language=pt |archive-date=1 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221001232257/https://noticias.uol.com.br/ultimas-noticias/agencia-estado/2022/10/01/tse-rejeita-pedido-de-bolsonaro-contra-transporte-em-nivel-normal-no-domingo.htm |url-status=live}}{{Cite web |title=Ministro do TSE chama de absurdo pedido da campanha de Bolsonaro de limitar transporte nas eleições |url=https://g1.globo.com/politica/eleicoes/2022/noticia/2022/10/01/ministro-do-tse-chama-de-absurdo-pedido-da-campanha-de-bolsonaro-de-limitar-transporte-nas-eleicoes.ghtml |access-date=2 October 2022 |website=G1 |date=October 2022 |language=pt |archive-date=2 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221002005655/https://g1.globo.com/politica/eleicoes/2022/noticia/2022/10/01/ministro-do-tse-chama-de-absurdo-pedido-da-campanha-de-bolsonaro-de-limitar-transporte-nas-eleicoes.ghtml |url-status=live}} ===== Intimidation of voters ===== Voter intimidation, which includes coercion, threats of retaliation, [[workplace harassment]], or a [[Promotion (rank)|promotion]] at work, is both an electoral and a labor crime in Brazil.{{Cite web |url=https://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/leis/l4737.htm |title=Electoral Code of Brazil, article 301 |publisher=Presidency of Brazil |language=pt}}{{Cite web |title=Assédio eleitoral: coagir funcionário por votos é crime e pode levar a indenização; saiba como denunciar |url=https://g1.globo.com/podcast/o-assunto/noticia/2022/10/10/assedio-eleitoral-coagir-funcionario-por-votos-e-crime-e-pode-levar-a-indenizacao-saiba-como-denunciar.ghtml |date=10 October 2022 |website=G1 |language=pt}} It can also be considered a form of [[electoral fraud]], voter suppression and [[workplace bullying]]. Reports of such crime, of which the main targets are employees, contractors and suppliers, have grown in the country since at least early 2022.{{Cite web |title=Crescem denúncias de empresários chantageando empregados e fornecedores a votar em Bolsonaro |url=https://piaui.folha.uol.com.br/eleicoes-2022/crescem-denuncias-de-empresarios-chantageando-empregados-e-fornecedores-votar-em-bolsonaro |archive-url=https://archive.today/20221004230658/https://piaui.folha.uol.com.br/eleicoes-2022/crescem-denuncias-de-empresarios-chantageando-empregados-e-fornecedores-votar-em-bolsonaro |url-status=dead |archive-date=2022-10-04 |date=4 October 2022 |publisher=Folha de S.Paulo |language=pt}} On 19 May, Havan, a retail chain, and its owner, billionaire [[Luciano Hang]], were both ordered to pay damages to a former employee of the company after a court found that she had suffered workplace harassment as a way to force her to vote for Bolsonaro.{{Cite web |last=Patriolino |first=Luana |date=19 May 2022 |title=Hang é condenado a indenizar funcionária coagida a votar em Bolsonaro |url=https://www.correiobraziliense.com.br/politica/2022/05/5009183-hang-e-condenado-a-indenizar-funcionaria-coagida-a-votar-em-bolsonaro.html |publisher=Correio Braziliense |language=pt}}{{Cite web |title=Havan é condenada em R$ 30 mil por coagir funcionária a votar em Bolsonaro |url=https://oglobo.globo.com/politica/havan-condenada-em-30-mil-por-coagir-funcionaria-votar-em-bolsonaro-1-25513977 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20220525005928/https://oglobo.globo.com/politica/havan-condenada-em-30-mil-por-coagir-funcionaria-votar-em-bolsonaro-1-25513977 |url-status=dead |archive-date=2022-05-25 |date=19 May 2022 |publisher=O Globo |language=pt}} On 5 October, the Public Prosecutor's Office and a labor court issued a joint statement warning employers against voter intimidation in the workplace after Stara and Extrusor, two companies based in southern Brazil, had sent their suppliers a memorandum threatening to cut their production and funds from 2023 on in the event that former president Lula were elected in 2022. There were also reports of a [[brickworks]] in northern Brazil that publicly offered each of its employees cash if Jair Bolsonaro were re-elected, and of an agriculture businesswoman in northeastern Brazil who was charged with asking farmers to "have no mercy" in firing employees who voted for Lula.{{Cite web |title=MPT-RS pede condenação de empresa por assédio pró-Bolsonaro |url=https://oglobo.globo.com/economia/noticia/2022/10/mpt-rs-pede-condenacao-de-empresa-por-assedio-pro-bolsonaro.ghtml |date=11 October 2022 |publisher=O Globo |language=pt}}{{Cite web |title=Empresas que ameaçam trabalhadores para votar em candidato cometem crime, alertam MPT e TRT |url=https://valor.globo.com/politica/eleicoes-2022/noticia/2022/10/05/empresas-que-ameacam-trabalhadores-para-votar-em-candidato-cometem-crime-alertam-mpt-e-trt.ghtml |archive-url=https://archive.today/20221011222636/https://valor.globo.com/politica/eleicoes-2022/noticia/2022/10/05/empresas-que-ameacam-trabalhadores-para-votar-em-candidato-cometem-crime-alertam-mpt-e-trt.ghtml |url-status=dead |archive-date=2022-10-11 |access-date=5 October 2022 |publisher=Valor Econômico |language=pt}} On 10 October, an agribusiness leader and husband of a mayor in the state of [[Goiás]] sent farmers a voicenote threatening to shut his business if former president Lula were elected president, and saying that his employees "were desperate" to get people to change their minds not to vote for Lula in order to keep their jobs.{{Cite web |date=10 October 2022 |title=Marido da prefeita em GO ameaça fechar sua empresa caso Lula ganhe a eleição; ouça áudio |url=https://extra.globo.com/noticias/politica/marido-da-prefeita-em-go-ameaca-fechar-sua-empresa-caso-lula-ganhe-eleicao-ouca-audio-25587961.html |access-date=12 October 2022 |publisher=Extra Online |language=pt}} On 11 October, the Labor Prosecutor's Office reported that it had received nearly 200 complaints of voter intimidation since the beginning of the election campaign in August 2022.{{Cite web |title=MPT recebeu quase 200 denúncias de assédio eleitoral nas eleições de 2022 até agora |url=https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/politica/mpt-recebeu-169-denuncias-de-assedio-eleitoral-nas-eleicoes-2022-ate-agora/ |date=11 October 2022 |publisher=CNN Brasil |language=pt}} As of 21 October, there had been 1,112 reports of voter intimidation in 2022, far higher than a total of 212 reports in the 2018 elections, which made many prosecutors open joint tasks forces to investigate the cases.{{Cite web |date=21 October 2022 |title=Denúncias de assédio eleitoral chegam a 1.112, diz MPT |url=https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/mercado/2022/10/denuncias-de-assedio-eleitoral-chegam-a-1112-diz-mpt.shtml |access-date=22 October 2022 |website=Folha de S.Paulo |language=pt}} On 22 October, employees of a [[meatpacking]] company based in southeastern Brazil denounced that they were forced among other things to wear pro-Bolsonaro shirts while at work, reportedly violating several [[food safety]] rules, besides the electoral law.{{Cite web |title=Funcionários de frigorífico de Betim denunciam assédio eleitoral em evento da empresa; VÍDEO |url=https://g1.globo.com/mg/minas-gerais/eleicoes/2022/noticia/2022/10/22/funcionarios-de-frigorifico-de-betim-denunciam-assedio-eleitoral-em-evento-da-empresa-video.ghtml |access-date=22 October 2022 |website=G1 |date=22 October 2022 |language=pt}} ==== In the second round ==== {{Main|Police operations in the 2022 Brazilian general election}} On 30 October, reports spread on social media of [[Federal Highway Police (Brazil)|Federal Highway Police]] (PRF) engaging in unusual patterns of stops in poorer areas of the country that were expected to favour Lula,{{cite news | url=https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/brazil-highway-police-blockades-fan-voter-suppression-fears-2022-10-30/ | title=Brazil highway police blockades fan voter-suppression fears | work=Reuters | date=30 October 2022 | last=Stargardter | first=Gabriel|access-date=31 October 2022}} leading to calls for the close-of-polling hour to be pushed back. The number of police searches of vehicles was 80 percent higher than had been recorded on 2 October, the day of the first round of voting, and directly violated an order from [[Superior Electoral Court]] president [[Alexandre de Moraes]] to suspend such activities on Election Day.{{cite web| last=Audi| first=Amanda| url=https://brazilian.report/liveblog/2022/10/30/alleged-voter-suppression-brazil/| title=More details on alleged voter suppression case emerge| website=The Brazilian Report| date=30 October 2022| access-date=31 October 2022| archive-date=30 October 2022| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221030181443/https://brazilian.report/liveblog/2022/10/30/alleged-voter-suppression-brazil/| url-status=dead}} Stops disproportionately took place in the [[Northeast Region, Brazil|Northeast Region]], which has historically recorded the strongest vote for the Workers' Party.{{cite web |url=https://twitter.com/aagencia_info/status/1586784093324328960 |title=G1/TV Globo: quase metade das operações da PRF hoje são no Nordeste |access-date=31 October 2022 |archive-date=31 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221031105820/https://twitter.com/aagencia_info/status/1586784093324328960 |url-status=live}} Police roadblocks also created a traffic jam on the [[Rio–Niterói Bridge]].{{cite news |last1=Downie|first1=Andrew|last2=Phillips|first2=Tom|date=30 October 2022|title=Brazil election: Lula's challenge hangs in balance amid voter suppression claims |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2022/oct/30/brazil-election-lula-da-silva-jair-bolsonaro-voting-polls-president |access-date=31 October 2022 |work=The Guardian}}{{cite news |date=30 October 2022 |title=Brazil election hit by outcry over roadblocks |url=https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20221030-brazil-election-hit-by-outcry-over-roadblocks |access-date=31 October 2022 |website=France 24 |publisher=Agence France-Presse}} Workers' Party supporters immediately called the actions an attempt of electoral subversion. ''[[O Globo]]'' reported that the director of the PRF, [[Silvinei Vasques]], had posted and then deleted a video on [[Instagram]] endorsing Bolsonaro the previous night.{{cite news | date=30 October 2022|last1=Abbud|first1=Bruno|last2=Rocha|first2= Rayane|url=https://oglobo.globo.com/politica/eleicoes-2022/noticia/2022/10/diretor-geral-da-prf-posta-pedido-de-voto-em-bolsonaro-vote-22.ghtml | title=Diretor-geral da PRF posta pedido de voto em Bolsonaro, mas apaga publicação |work=O Globo|language=pt|access-date=31 October 2022}} ''O Globo'' additionally reported that the operation had been discussed in the office of President Bolsonaro on 19 October, suggesting it was performed at his direction.{{cite news | last=Jardim|first=Lauro|date=30 October 2022|url=https://oglobo.globo.com/blogs/lauro-jardim/post/2022/10/operacao-de-hoje-da-prf-foi-tracada-em-reuniao-no-alvorada.ghtml | title=Operação de hoje da PRF foi traçada em reunião no Alvorada|work=O Globo|language=pt|access-date=31 October 2022}} Activists made an appeal to Moraes, who ordered an immediate halt to the operations and subpoenad Vasques; however, Moraes claimed the operations did not stop anyone from voting and rejected a request from the PT to extend voting hours beyond the 5 pm deadline.{{cite web |last=Winter|first=Brian|url=https://twitter.com/BrazilBrian/status/1586791475009961985 |date=30 October 2022|title=Brazil election chief says extraordinarily high number of police roadblocks today did not stop 'anyone' from voting, thus he declines to extend voting past scheduled 5 pm. Sounds confident. I guess time will tell |access-date=31 October 2022 |archive-date=31 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221031105107/https://twitter.com/BrazilBrian/status/1586791475009961985 |url-status=live|via=Twitter}} Vasques was then arrested on 10 August 2023.{{Cite web |date=2023-08-10 |title=Former Federal Highway Police Chief in Brazil Arrested on Suspicion of Interfering in the Election |url=https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/internacional/en/brazil/2023/08/former-federal-highway-police-chief-in-brazil-arrested-on-suspicion-of-interfering-in-the-election.shtml |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230813184245/https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/internacional/en/brazil/2023/08/former-federal-highway-police-chief-in-brazil-arrested-on-suspicion-of-interfering-in-the-election.shtml |archive-date=2023-08-13 |access-date=2023-08-13 |website=Folha de S.Paulo}} === Environmental issues === Some commentators noted the importance of this election for the [[Amazon rainforest]],{{Cite web |date=31 August 2022 |title=The future of Amazon rainforest is on the line in Brazil election |url=https://www.channel4.com/news/the-future-of-amazon-rainforest-is-on-the-line-in-brazil-election |first=Krishnan |last=Guru-Murthy |access-date=9 September 2022 |website=Channel 4 News |archive-date=9 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220909143225/https://www.channel4.com/news/the-future-of-amazon-rainforest-is-on-the-line-in-brazil-election |url-status=live}} as well as [[climate change]].{{Cite news |date=15 April 2022 |title=Brazil's climate politics are shifting. That matters for the whole planet. |work=The New York Times |first=Manuela |last=Andreoni |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/04/15/climate/brazil-elections-lula-climate.html |access-date=9 September 2022 |issn=0362-4331 |archive-date=29 July 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220729201507/https://www.nytimes.com/2022/04/15/climate/brazil-elections-lula-climate.html |url-status=live}} On 23 September, the British environmental-focused website [[Carbon Brief]] released a report made by researchers at the [[University of Oxford]], the [[International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis]] and the Brazilian [[National Institute for Space Research]] showing that deforestation in the [[Brazilian Amazon]] could be reduced by 89% if Lula were elected in 2022 and his environmental policy continued until 2030. The report said that Lula's enforcement of the [[Brazilian Forest Code]], the country's flagship legislation for tackling deforestation in the Amazon and other ecosystems, would curb forest clearings and could also reduce [[greenhouse gas emissions]]. Instead, a re-election of Bolsonaro would likely see the pace of deforestation accelerate in the coming years, including what one of the report authors described as huge areas beyond the scope of the Forest Code.{{Cite web |last=Gabbatiss |first=Josh |date=23 September 2022 |title=Analysis: Bolsonaro election loss could cut Brazilian Amazon deforestation by 89% |url=https://www.carbonbrief.org/analysis-bolsonaro-election-loss-could-cut-brazilian-amazon-deforestation-by-89/ |access-date=24 October 2022 |website=Carbon Brief}} === Views and endorsements === On 3 September, medical journal ''[[The Lancet]]'' published an [[editorial]] calling the stakes in the Brazilian elections high and highlighting among other things that Bolsonaro, described as someone "who is known for his volatility and indirect incitement of violence, will not go quietly" if he were not re-elected as predictions pointed to, and that "he has already criticised Brazil's electronic voting system in the presence of foreign ambassadors". It concluded by saying "there is an unprecedented chance for new beginnings in Latin America; an opportunity to make positive changes to alleviate deep neglect, inequality, and violence. Let us hope that Brazil chooses to seize this opportunity."{{cite journal |date=3 September 2022 |title=New beginnings for Latin America? |journal=The Lancet |volume=400 |issue=10354 |pages=707 |doi=10.1016/S0140-6736(22)01662-2 |issn=0140-6736 |pmid=36058210|last1=The Lancet |pmc=9448301}} On 25 October, ahead of the second round, British weekly scientific journal ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'' published an editorial in which it said that a second term for incumbent Bolsonaro would "represent a threat to science, democracy, and the environment", and cited Bolsonaro's similarities to former U.S. president [[Donald Trump]], both of whom it said "have sought to undermine the [[rule of law]] and slash the powers of regulators", and "ignored scientists' warnings about [[COVID-19]] and denied the dangers of the disease". It concluded by stating that "Brazil's voters have a valuable opportunity to start to rebuild what Bolsonaro has torn down. If Bolsonaro gets four more years, the damage could be irreparable."{{cite journal |date=25 October 2022 |title=There's only one choice in Brazil's election — for the country and the world |journal=Nature |volume=610 |issue=7933 |pages=606 |doi=10.1038/d41586-022-03388-y|pmid=36284189 |s2cid=253111053|doi-access=free |bibcode=2022Natur.610..606. }} == Opinion polls == === Presidential Instead, Bolsonaro outperformed almost all published opinion polling. This was partly attributed to a significant number of supporters of minor candidates deciding to vote for Bolsonaro shortly before the election, along with a number of Bolsonaro supporters refusing to respond to pollsters in the view that pollsters were part of a "fake news establishment".{{cite news|last=Henley|first=Jon|date=3 October 2022|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2022/oct/03/why-did-the-brazil-election-pollsters-get-bolsonaros-vote-so-wrong|title=Why did the Brazil election pollsters get Bolsonaro's vote so wrong?|work=The Guardian|access-date=31 October 2022}} Additionally, Brazil had last conducted a [[census]] in 2010, and a number of pollsters oversampled poorer voters who generally backed Lula. At the same time, this was the first time that the incumbent president attempting re-election did not receive the highest number of votes in the first round.{{cite news| leaders congratulate Lula on election victory|url=https://www.dw.com/en/brazil-presidential-election-lula-set-to-become-new-president-live-updates/a-63596512 |access-date=31 October 2022|work=Deutsche 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240919222915/https://time.com/6226302/lula-wins-brazil-election-defeats-bolsonaro/|url-status=dead}} Lula became the first person to be elected president for a third term in Brazil,{{cite news |last1=Faiola|first1=Anthony|last2=Sá Pessoa|first2=Gabriela|last3=Villegas|first3=Paulina |date=30 October 2022 |title=Lula defeats Bolsonaro to win third term person to assume the post at age 77 on his inauguration scheduled for 1 January 2023.{{cite news|last=Middleton|first=Joe|date=30 October 2022|title=Brazil election: Lula defeats Bolsonaro in presidential race|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/brazil-election-lula-victory-bolsonaro-b2213960.html|access-date=31 October 2022|work=The Independent}}{{cite 2022}} Lula's 60 million votes surpassed his own 2006 record as the largest number of votes in a Brazilian election.{{cite web|last=Alencar|first=Caíque|url=https://noticias.uol.com.br/eleicoes/2022/10/31/putin-parabeniza-lula.htm|title=Putin e Zelensky, adversários em guerra na Ucrânia, parabenizam Lula|publisher=Universo Online|language=pt|date=31 October 2022|access-date=31 October 2022}} It was the closest presidential election in Brazil to date.{{cite news |last=Gielow|first=Igor|date=30 October 2022 |title=Lula é eleito presidente pela 3ª vez |url=https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/poder/2022/10/lula-e-eleito-presidente-pela-3a-vez-projeta-datafolha.shtml |access-date=7 November 2022 |work=Folha de S.Paulo |language=pt}} In both rounds, Lula was the most voted candidate in the state of [[Amazonas (Brazilian state)|Amazonas]] and the country's [[Bellwether (politics)|bellwether]], [[Minas Gerais]], where Bolsonaro had been the most voted in [[2018 Brazilian presidential election|2018]]. A shift was also observed among urban voters in the [[Southeast Region, Brazil|Southeast Region]]. In the city of [[Rio de Janeiro]], Bolsonaro had obtained 66.4% of the vote in 2018, but only 52.7% in 2022.{{cite web |date=30 October 2022 |title=Apuração da Eleição 2022 por estado para Presidente — Rio de Janeiro |url=https://especiaisg1.globo/rj/rio-de-janeiro/eleicoes/2022/mapas/apuracao-estado-presidente/2-turno |access-date=4 November 2022 |website=G1 |language=pt}} In the city of [[São Paulo]], he obtained 60.4% in 2018, but Lula flipped the city in 2022 and received 53.5% of the vote.{{cite web |date=30 October 2022 |title=Apuração da Eleição 2022 por estado para Presidente — São Paulo |url=https://especiaisg1.globo/sp/sao-paulo/eleicoes/2022/mapas/apuracao-estado-presidente/2-turno |access-date=4 November 2022 |website=G1 |language=pt}} [[Steven Levitsky]], author of ''[[How Democracies Die]]'', commented that Bolsonaro's allies acknowledging Lula's victory helped to avoid a 6 January scenario, referencing the [[2021 United States Capitol attack]], and that Brazil managed the election in a better way than the United States did in 2020.{{cite news|last=Sanches|first=Mariana|url=https://www.bbc.com/portuguese/brasil-63453815|title=Reconhecimento da derrota de Bolsonaro por aliados foi grande diferença com eleição nos EUA, diz Levitsky|work=BBC News Brasil|language=pt|date=31 October 2022|access-date=31 October 2022}} Some observers, such as Thomas Traumann, compared the results to [[Joe Biden]]'s victory in 2020, and said that Lula was inheriting a nation that was much divided. Bolsonaro's better-than-expected performance reflected an election year with increased government spending. Political scientist Carlos Melo compared the election to the political climate experienced by the former president [[Dilma Rousseff]]'s reelection bid in the [[2014 Brazilian presidential election]].{{cite news|last1=Jeantet|first1=Diane|last2=Saverese|first2=Mauricio|date=30 October 2022|title=Lula defeats Bolsonaro to again become Brazil's president|url=https://apnews.com/article/jair-bolsonaro-religion-caribbean-voting-ed2130a095ca42ff1be324a3dea9f355|access-date=31 October 2022|work=AP News|publisher=Associated Press}} Both presidential candidates in the second round received a higher percentage of the votes than they did in the first round in every state, and Bolsonaro's increase was greater than Lula's also in every state. [[Amapá]] was the only state where the most voted candidate was different between the first round (Lula) and the second round (Bolsonaro). It was the first presidential election when more people voted in the second round than in the first round, and both rounds had the lowest percentage of invalid votes in a presidential election since the two-round system was introduced in 1989.{{cite web |url=https://politicalivre.com.br/2022/10/bolsonaro-ampliou-votacao-em-todos-os-estados-lula-perdeu-em-quatro |title=Bolsonaro ampliou votação em todos os estados; Lula perdeu em quatro |trans-title=Bolsonaro increased votes in all states; Lula dropped in four |publisher=Política Livre |date=31 October 2022 |language=pt}} The second round was the first time when votes from abroad exceeded those in a Brazilian state ([[Roraima]]). ==== Congressional election results ==== {{Main|57th Legislature of the National Congress}} In the [[National Congress of Brazil]], [[right-wing]] parties expanded their majority, while [[centrist]] and [[left-wing]] parties elected fewer members, despite the Workers' Party-led coalition gaining seats, continuing the trend from the [[2018 Brazilian general election]].{{cite web |date=3 October 2022 |title=Direita mantém crescimento, esquerda oscila negativamente e centro afunda |url=https://www.jota.info/opiniao-e-analise/artigos/direita-mantem-crescimento-esquerda-oscila-negativamente-e-centro-afunda-03102022 |website=Jota |language=pt|access-date=4 November 2022}} Several small parties did not satisfy the minimum number of elected members to obtain access to public funds, broadcast time, and congressional leadership. To satisfy the requirement, these members could choose to individually join larger parties, or their parties could merge. The goal of this requirement, first established in 2018, was to reduce the large number of parties in Congress and facilitate political negotiations between them.{{cite web |date=5 October 2022 |title=Só 13 partidos cumprem cláusula de desempenho em 2022 |url=https://www.poder360.com.br/eleicoes/so-13-partidos-cumprem-clausula-de-desempenho-em-2022/ |website=Poder360 |language=pt|access-date=4 November 2022}} The growth of the right-wing parties in Congress was cited as a potential roadblock to Lula's policy goals upon taking office, while one observer noted that the Congress elected in 2022 would be “far more to the right than the one Lula negotiated with during his previous tenures from 2002 to 2010” while also describing it as “the most centre-right Congress since 1988.”[https://feps-europe.eu/what-a-difference-a-president-makes-lulas-election-in-brazil/ What a difference a president makes: Lula’s election in Brazil by Leany Lemos, "The Progressive Post", 03/11/2022] Despite right-wing shifts in both chambers, a number of [[conservative]] incumbents were not elected for the same or other offices, including [[Douglas Garcia]], [[Janaina Paschoal]], and Fabricio Queiroz. A number of milestones took place in the election for Congress, including two transgender activists, [[Erika Hilton]] and [[Duda Salabert]], who became the first transgender individuals elected to Congress, and five self-declared indigenous Brazilians were elected as deputies (including [[Sônia Guajajara]] and [[Célia Xakriabá]]) and two as senators ([[Wellington Dias (politician)|Wellington Dias]] and [[Hamilton Mourão]]), the largest number of self-declared indigenous candidates elected to Congress to date.{{cite news |last=Downie|first=Andrew|date=3 October 2022 |title=Brazilian left celebrates election wins for trans and Indigenous candidates |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2022/oct/03/brazil-left-election-wins-trans-indigenous-candidates |access-date=4 November 2022 |work=The Guardian }}{{cite web |last=Mendes|first=Carla|date=25 October 2022 |title=Brazil's biggest elected Indigenous caucus to face tough 2023 Congress |url=https://news.mongabay.com/2022/10/brazils-biggest-elected-indigenous-caucus-to-face-tough-2023-congress/ |access-date=4 November 2022 |website=Mongabay Environmental News}} === Reactions === ==== In Brazil ==== {{see also|2022–2023 Brazilian election protests}} After 90% of the votes were counted in the second round, the [[Superior Electoral Court]] declared Lula as mathematically elected.{{cite web |date=30 October 2022 |title=Resultados – TSE |url=https://resultados.tse.jus.br/oficial/app/index.html#/eleicao/resultados/cargo/1 |access-date=30 October 2022 |publisher=Superior Electoral Court |language=pt |archive-date=2 November 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221102121453/https://resultados.tse.jus.br/oficial/app/index.html#/eleicao/resultados/cargo/1 |url-status=dead }} After this result, Lula stated: "Today the only winner is the Brazilian people. This isn't a victory of mine or the Workers' Party, nor the parties that supported me in campaign. It's the victory of a democratic movement that formed above political parties, personal interests and ideologies so that democracy came out victorious." In his victory speech, he also called for "peace and unity" and said: "It is in no one's interest to live in a divided nation in a permanent state of war." Former president [[Fernando Henrique Cardoso]], who was elected against Lula in presidential elections in 1994 and 1998, congratulated Lula by stating that "democracy has won". Journalist [[Fernando Gabeira]], an opponent of the [[military dictatorship in Brazil]], called the election "a victory for Brazil, and a victory for humanity. We can now breathe again."{{cite magazine|last=Passos de Souza|first=Olavo|date=31 October 2022|title=Lula's Victory Over Bolsonaro Has Restored Hope for Brazilian Democracy|url=https://jacobin.com/2022/10/lula-president-election-victory-bolsonaro-democracy|access-date=31 October 2022|magazine=Jacobin}} [[File:01 11 2022 Pronunciamento do Presidente Jair Bolsonaro (52470301702).jpg|thumb|Bolsonaro's first speech after his loss]] Bolsonaro did not immediately publicly concede or comment on the election result,{{cite news |date=31 October 2022|title=Brazil's Bolsonaro yet to concede after Lula's election victory |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/news/picture/lula-wins-brazilian-election-bolsonaro-h-idUSKBN2RQ086 |access-date=31 October 2022}}{{cite news |last1=Boadle |first1=Anthony|last2=Paraguassu |first2=Lisandra |date=31 October 2022 |title=Lula wins Brazil election in political resurrection for leftist |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/lula-wins-brazilian-election-bolsonaro-has-not-conceded-2022-10-31/ |access-date=31 October 2022}} which raised the widely discussed concerns prior to the election that he might reject the result like [[Donald Trump]] did in the United States in [[Attempts to overturn the 2020 United States presidential election|2020]]. Privately, Bolsonaro only acknowledged the result to the president of the Superior Electoral Court [[Alexandre de Moraes]],{{cite web|url=https://www.metropoles.com/brasil/eleicoes-2022/bolsonaro-admite-derrota-nas-urnas-a-moraes-mas-nao-faz-declaracao-publica|title=Bolsonaro admite derrota nas urnas a Moraes, mas não faz declaração pública|website=Metrópoles|language=pt|date=31 October 2022|access-date=31 October 2022}} and he remained silent as transition talks began.{{cite news|last1=Boadle|first1=Anthony|last2=Mano |first2=Ana|date=1 November 2022|title=Brazil's Bolsonaro silent on Lula victory, transition talks begin|work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/lula-wins-brazilian-election-bolsonaro-has-not-conceded-2022-10-31/|access-date=1 November 2022}} On 1 November, [[Ministry of Communications (Brazil)|Minister of Communications]], [[Fábio Faria (politician)|Fabio Faria]], told [[Reuters]] that Bolsonaro would not contest the election result and would address the nation later in the day.{{cite news|last=Buschschlüter|first=Vanessa |title=Brazil's Bolsonaro to break silence after election defeat |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-63451860|work=BBC News|access-date=1 November 2022|date=1 November 2022}} [[Chief of Staff of the Presidency]], [[Ciro Nogueira Lima Filho]], also confirmed that the incumbent government had already begun to establish contact with the future government led by Lula to discuss a transition.{{cite news|last1=Ellsworth|first1=Brian|last2=Brito|first2=Ricardo|date=1 November 2022|title=Brazil's Bolsonaro to accept election loss in speech to nation, says minister|work=Reuters|url=https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/brazilian-court-orders-roadblocks-cleared-bolsonaro-silent-election-loss-2022-11-01/|access-date=1 November 2022}} Vice president-elect [[Geraldo Alckmin]] was named as the representative of the future government. Alckmin confirmed that he would coordinate the transition and aimed to start it on 3 November.{{cite news|date=1 November 2022|title=Lula's running mate Alckmin to manage Brazil's government transition|work=Reuters|url=https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/lulas-running-mate-alckmin-manage-brazils-government-transition-2022-11-01/|access-date=1 November 2022}} Protests broke out in many states of Brazil after the election, as supporters of Bolsonaro alleged fraud and blockaded key roads, while demanding military intervention.{{cite news |last1=Carvalho|first1= Daniel |last2=Rosati|first2= Andrew |date=1 November 2022 |title=Brazil Protesters Block Roads, Airport as Bolsonaro Stays Silent |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-11-01/brazil-protests-grow-with-bolsonaro-silent-after-election-loss |access-date=1 November 2022 |work=Bloomberg News}}{{cite news |date=1 November 2022|title=Bolsonaro supporters block Brazil roads for a 2nd day as president refuses to accept election loss |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/brazil-election-results-2022-protest-lula-bolsonaro-road-blocks/ |access-date=1 November 2022 |work=CBS News}}{{cite news |date=1 November 2022 |title=Brazil election: Bolsonaro supporters block roads after poll defeat |work=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-63467982 |access-date=1 November 2022}} In some cases, police did not intervene. Late on 31 October, Moraes ordered the [[Federal Highway Police (Brazil)|Federal Highway Police]] to clear all the federal highways. Protesters also blockaded roads to the [[São Paulo/Guarulhos International Airport]] on 1 November but were cleared by the Federal Highway Police.{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/11/01/world/americas/bolsonaro-protest-brazil-election.html|title=Bolsonaro Supporters Try to 'Paralyze' Brazil as They Wait for Him to Speak|last1=Martins|first1=Laís|last2=Nicas|first2=Jack Nicas|last3=Spigariol|first3=André|newspaper=The New York Times|date=1 November 2022|access-date=1 November 2022|url-access=subscription}} The blockades disrupted fuel and grain distribution, as well as the meat industry and rail network. The road to the [[Port of Paranaguá]], an important grain export port, was blocked by protestors. The Brazilian Petroleum and Gas Institute stated that the situation regarding fuel distribution had become critical, and called on the federal government to form a crisis committee regarding the protests.{{cite news|date=1 November 2022|title=Brazil government seeks to clear truckers' pro-Bolsonaro blockades|work=Reuters|url=https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/main-road-brazils-paranagua-port-major-grain-export-hub-still-blocked-2022-11-01/|access-date=2 November 2022|last=Mano|first=Ana}} In a press conference at the [[Palácio da Alvorada]] on 1 November, Bolsonaro did not acknowledge the result but stated that he would "comply with the Constitution". Regarding the protests by his supporters, he referred to them as "the fruit of indignation and a sense of injustice of how the electoral process unfolded", while calling on them to remain peaceful and not block roads. Shortly after his speech, the Supreme Federal Court stated that by authorizing the transition of power he had recognized the results,{{cite web|last1=Henrique Gomes|first1=Pedro|last2=Mazui|first2=Guilherme|url=https://g1.globo.com/politica/eleicoes/2022/noticia/2022/11/01/bolsonaro-faz-primeiro-discurso-apos-perder-a-eleicao.ghtml|title=Bolsonaro diz que vai cumprir a Constituição; Ciro Nogueira inicia a transição|date=1 November 2022|access-date=1 November 2022|language=pt}}{{cite news|last=Buschschlüter|first=Vanessa|date=1 November 2022|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-63451860|title=Bolsonaro breaks silence without publicly conceding|work=BBC News|access-date=1 November 2022}} paving the way for the transition two days after Lula was declared elected.{{cite news |last1=Nicas |first1=Jack |last2=Spigariol |first2=André |date=1 November 2022 |title=Bolsonaro Agrees to Transition, Two Days After Losing Brazil Election |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/11/01/world/americas/bolsonaro-protest-brazil-election.html |access-date=2 November 2022 |issn=0362-4331}}{{cite news |last1=Brito |first1=Ricardo |last2=Ellsworth |first2=Brian |last3=Gaier |first3=Rodrigo Viga |date=2 November 2022 |title=Brazil's Bolsonaro does not concede to Lula, but authorizes transition |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/brazilian-court-orders-roadblocks-cleared-bolsonaro-silent-election-loss-2022-11-01/ |access-date=2 November 2022}} Hours before the press conference, Bolsonaro met with the [[Brazilian Armed Forces]] to pitch the possibility of challenging Lula's election judicially, arguing that he would not be eligible due to his convictions in the [[Operation Car Wash]], all of which had been annulled by the Supreme Federal Court in 2021.{{cite news|url=https://abcnews.go.com/International/lula-winner-brazils-presidential-election/story?id=92443979|title=Who is Lula? Winner of Brazil's presidential election|date=2 November 2022|access-date=8 November 2022|work=ABC News|first=Michela|last=Moscufo}} Bolsonaro could not find support for it, and members of the [[Army High Command]] reportedly accepted the results and were against any possibility of a military intervention or coup.{{cite news|url=https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/politica/pouco-antes-de-quebrar-o-silencio-bolsonaro-consultou-exercito-sobre-judicializar-eleicoes-e-nao-teve-apoio-segundo-oficiais-ouvidos-pela-cnn/|title= Pouco antes de quebrar o silêncio, Bolsonaro consultou Exército sobre judicializar eleições e não teve apoio, segundo oficiais ouvidos pela CNN|date=4 November 2022|access-date=4 November 2022|language=pt|work=CNN Brasil|first=Kenzô|last=Machida}} The following day, Bolsonaro directly appealed to his protesting supporters to clear the roadblocks, while welcoming their decision to protest against the election results and asking them to do it through other means. The [[Ministry of Defence (Brazil)|Ministry of Defence]] released the report about the election audit done by the military on 10 November. While it cited some possible vulnerabilities in the electronic voting machines used for the election, it did not find any sign of voter fraud.{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2022/nov/10/brazil-military-finds-no-evidence-of-election-dashing-hopes-of-bolsonaro-supporters|title=Brazil military finds no evidence of election fraud, dashing hopes of Bolsonaro supporters|date=10 November 2022|access-date=12 November 2022|work=The Guardian|first=Andrew|last=Downie}} On the following day, the Brazilian Armed Forces released a letter signed by leaders of all three branches, stating that all electoral disputes must be resolved through peaceful means, while adding that the Constitution permitted peaceful protests.{{cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/brazils-armed-forces-say-disputes-must-be-resolved-through-democratic-rule-law-2022-11-11/|title=Brazil's armed forces say disputes must be resolved through democratic rule of law|date=11 November 2022|access-date=12 November 2022|work=Reuters}} Bolsonaro meanwhile spent weeks after his defeat mostly alone in his presidential residence. They requested that the Superior Electoral Court invalidate the votes recorded by the affected machines, which would result in Bolsonaro being elected with 51% of the remaining valid votes. However, experts claimed that the software error did not affect the election results and pointed out that the identification numbers did appear in the physical vote records printed by the machines.{{Cite web |last1=Biller |first1=David |last2=Bridi |first2=Carla |date=2022-11-23 |title=Bolsonaro Contests Brazil Election, Demands Votes Be Anulled {{sic|hide=y}} |url=https://www.huffpost.com/entry/bolsonaro-contests-brazil-election-demands-votes-be-anulled_n_637d5ecbe4b082d8e6cb2bf8 |access-date=2022-11-23 |website=HuffPost|quote=Bolsonaro has been almost completely secluded in the official residence since his Oct. 30 defeat, inviting widespread speculation as to whether he is dejected or plotting to cling to power.}} On the next day the court rejected the request and fined the party [[Brazilian real|R$]]22.9 million ([[United States dollar|US$]]4.3 million) for what it considered [[bad faith]] litigation.{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2022/nov/24/brazil-judge-fines-bolsonaro-allies-millions-after-bad-faith-election-challenge |title=Brazil judge fines Bolsonaro allies millions after 'bad faith' election challenge |work=The Guardian |date=23 November 2022}} Lula's victory was officially certified on 12 December. The authorization was given on 2 November by the Chief of Staff of the Presidency.{{cite news|url=https://www.correiobraziliense.com.br/politica/2022/11/5048738-apos-mais-de-44-horas-bolsonaro-reconhece-indiretamente-vitoria-de-lula.html|title=Após mais de 44 horas, Bolsonaro reconhece indiretamente vitória de Lula|work=Correio Braziliense|language=pt|first=Ingrid|last=Soares|date=2 November 2022|access-date=2 November 2022}} The transition formally began on 3 November after Lula's transition team arrived in [[Brasília]], meeting first with senator [[Marcelo Castro]], who was overseeing the budget for 2023. Vice president-elect [[Geraldo Alckmin]] later personally met with Bolsonaro.{{cite news|url=https://apnews.com/article/jair-bolsonaro-business-caribbean-brazil-congress-607180be50dabedff22b39434370b06e|title=Lula's team meets Bolsonaro as Brazil's transition kicks off|work=Associated Press|first=Carla|last=Bridi|date=4 November 2022|access-date=4 November 2022}} On 9 December, Lula named five of the members assuming major positions in his incoming cabinet.{{cite news|url=https://www.dw.com/en/brazil-lula-names-ministers-bolsonaro-breaks-silence/a-64053382|title=Brazil: Lula names ministers, Bolsonaro breaks silence|work=Deutsche Welle|date=10 December 2022|access-date=24 December 2022}} On 22 December, he named 16 more members of his cabinet. The transition team of Lula also presented a report stating that the health and education sectors had suffered a setback under the tenure of Bolsonaro. Lula stated that addressing these issues along with poverty will be among his top priorities.{{cite news|url=https://apnews.com/article/caribbean-covid-brazil-964bd56d9446980975690b3dbf8ae2eb|title=Brazil's Lula taps 16 ministers ahead of inauguration|author=Diane Jeantet|work=Associated Press|date=23 December 2022|access-date=24 December 2022}} On 29 December, he named the remaining 16 ministers.{{cite news|url=https://brazilreports.com/lula-announces-final-cabinet-members-highest-number-of-female-ministers-in-brazils-history/3509/|title=Lula announces final cabinet members, highest number of female ministers in Brazil's history|author=Tabata Viapiana|work=Brazil Reports|date=29 December 2022|access-date=29 December 2022}} Lula and his cabinet were sworn in at the [[National Congress of Brazil|National Congress]] on 1 January 2023.{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-64138739|title=Lula sworn in as Brazil president as predecessor Bolsonaro flies to US|author1=Katy Watson|author2=Alys Davies|work=BBC|date=1 January 2023|access-date=2 January 2023}} ==See also== *[[2022 Brazilian attempted coup plot]] *[[Conservative wave]] *[[Pink tide]] == Notes == {{notelist}} == References == {{reflist}} ==External links== *[https://www.bloomberg.com/graphics/2022-brazil-election/ Brazil Election Live Results] at [[Bloomberg News]] {{2022 Brazilian general election}} {{Brazilian elections}} [[Category:2022 elections in Brazil|General]] [[Category:Parliamentary elections in Brazil]] [[Category:October 2022 in Brazil|General]] [[Category:Presidential elections in Brazil]]

the Federal Council]] ==Electoral system== ===National Council=== The 200 members of the National Council are elected from the [[Cantons of Switzerland|26 cantons]], each of which constitutes a constituency. In all multi-member cantons [[Open list|open-list]] [[proportional representation]] is used; with [[apparentment]]s for allied parties and sub-apparentments for lists within parties, where apparented lists are initially counted together for seats allocation. Seats are allocated using the [[Hagenbach-Bischoff system]] with no threshold. Voters may cross out names on party lists or write names twice, split their vote between parties (a system known as [[panachage]]), or draw up their own list on a blank ballot. The six single-member cantons use [[first-past-the-post voting]].{{Cite web |title=Organisation of the National Council election |url=https://www.ch.ch/en/elections2023/how-the-elections-are-organised/national-council-elections/ |access-date=2023-01-07 |website=www.ch.ch |language=en |archive-date=2023-01-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230107202254/https://www.ch.ch/en/elections2023/how-the-elections-are-organised/national-council-elections/ |url-status=live }} Seats in the National Council are apportioned to the cantons based on their respective population size (which includes children and resident foreigners who do not have the right to vote). Based on the official population count recorded at the end of 2020, [[Basel-Stadt]] lost a seat while [[Zürich]] gained one. Zürich is the canton with the most seats (36).{{Cite web |title=Renouvellement intégral du Conseil national en 2023 : modification de la répartition des sièges entre les cantons |url=https://www.admin.ch/gov/fr/accueil/documentation/communiques.msg-id-84941.html |access-date=2023-01-07 |website=www.admin.ch |archive-date=2023-01-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230107202248/https://www.admin.ch/gov/fr/accueil/documentation/communiques.msg-id-84941.html |url-status=live }} The rules regarding who can stand as a candidate and vote in elections to the National Council are uniform across the Confederation. Only [[Swiss nationality law|Swiss citizens]] aged at least 18 can stand or vote and the citizens resident abroad can register to vote in the canton in which they last resided (or their [[Place of origin|canton of citizenship]], otherwise) and be able to vote no matter how long since, or whether they ever have, lived in Switzerland. {| class="wikitable sortable" style="font-size:95%; text-align:right;" |+ Apportionment of National Council seats by canton in 2023{{Cite swiss law|en=Ordinance on the apportionment of seats for the full renewal of the National Council|fr=Ordonnance sur la répartition des sièges lors du renouvellement intégral du Conseil national|link=161_13|sr=161.13|de=Verordnung über die Sitzverteilung bei der Gesamterneuerung des Nationalrates|date=2021-09-01}}{{Cite law|type=Order (arrêté)|date=1 September 2021|title=Arrêté du Conseil fédéral homologuant les chiffres de la population résidante permanente à la fin de 2020|trans-title=Order of the Federal Council accrediting the permanent resident population figures at the end of 2020|url=https://www.newsd.admin.ch/newsd/message/attachments/68031.pdf}} {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221110142419/https://www.newsd.admin.ch/newsd/message/attachments/68031.pdf |date=10 November 2022 }} ! States === The 46 members of the Council of States are elected in 20 two-seat constituencies (representing the 20 'full' cantons) and six single-member constituencies (representing the six [[half-canton]]s). Two 'full' cantons with small populations – [[Canton of Uri|Uri]] and [[Canton of Glarus|Glarus]] – each have two seats in the Council of States but only one seat each in the much larger National Council.{{Cite web |title=IPU PARLINE database: SWITZERLAND (Ständerat – Conseil des États – Consiglio degli Stati), Electoral system |url=http://archive.ipu.org/parline-e/reports/2306_B.htm |access-date=2023-01-07 |website=archive.ipu.org |archive-date=2022-12-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221209025251/http://archive.ipu.org/parline-e/reports/2306_B.htm |url-status=live }} Elections to the Council of States are regulated by the cantons. The cantons of [[Canton of Jura|Jura]] and [[Canton of Neuchâtel|Neuchâtel]] use proportional representation, while all the others use a majoritarian system, often with [[Two-round system|two rounds]] of voting. In the first round voters typically have up to two votes and candidates need an overall majority to be elected; if seats remain to be filled a runoff is held using simple plurality. All cantons, except Appenzell-Innerrhoden, which elects its state councilor during the [[Landsgemeinde]] in April, hold the first round concurrently with the National Council election, but the dates for the runoffs vary.{{Cite web |title=Organisation of the Council of States elections |url=https://www.ch.ch/en/elections2023/how-the-elections-are-organised/council-of-states-elections/ |access-date=2023-01-07 |website=www.ch.ch |language=en |archive-date=2023-01-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230107202250/https://www.ch.ch/en/elections2023/how-the-elections-are-organised/council-of-states-elections/ |url-status=live }} As each canton regulates its election to the Council of States, the rules regarding who can stand as a candidate and vote in these elections vary canton by canton. Jura and Neuchâtel allow certain foreign residents to vote, whilst [[Canton of Glarus|Glarus]] allows 16- and 17-year-olds to vote. Swiss citizens abroad registered to vote in a canton are permitted to vote in that canton's Council of States election only if the canton's law allows it. Only [[Canton of Schaffhausen|Schaffhausen]] has [[compulsory voting]], though limited in implementation by way of only an insignificant fine. {| class="wikitable" |+Apportionment of Council of States seats by canton !Seats !Cantons |- |Cantons with 2 seats |Zürich, Bern, Lucerne, Uri, Schwyz, Glaris, Zug, Fribourg, Solothurn, Schaffhausen, St. Gallen, Grisons, Aargau, Thurgau, Ticino, Vaud, Valais, Neuchâtel, Geneva, Jura |- |Cantons with 1 seat ('half-cantons') |Obwalden, Nidwalden, Basel-Stadt, Basel-Landschaft, Appenzell Innerrhoden, Appenzell Ausserrhoden |} ==Contesting parties== The table below lists contesting parties represented in the [[Federal Assembly (Switzerland)|Federal Assembly]] before the election. {| class="wikitable" ! rowspan="2" colspan="3"| Name ! rowspan="2"| [[Political group]] ! rowspan="2"| Ideology ! rowspan="2"| Leader(s) ! colspan="3"| 2019 result |- !
