Parliamentary elections were held in the [[Czech Republic]] on 8 and 9 October 2021. All 200 members of the [[Chamber of Deputies of the Czech Republic|Chamber of Deputies]] were elected, with the leader of the resulting government to become the [[Prime Minister of the Czech Republic]]. Following the [[2017 Czech parliamentary election|2017 parliamentary elections]], the country had been ruled by a [[minority government]] consisting of [[ANO (political party)|ANO]], led by prime minister [[Andrej Babiš]], and the [[Czech Social Democratic Party]] (ČSSD), led by interior minister [[Jan Hamáček]], with [[confidence and supply]] support from the [[Communist Party of Bohemia and Moravia]] (KSČM) until April 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/world/czech-government-set-survive-no-confidence-vote-2021-06-03/|title=Czech government survives no-confidence vote months before election|date=3 June 2021|agency=Reuters}}</ref> The largest opposition party was the [[Civic Democratic Party (Czech Republic)|Civic Democratic Party]] (ODS), followed by the [[Czech Pirate Party]]. Other parties in the Chamber of Deputies included [[Freedom and Direct Democracy|SPD]], [[TOP 09]], [[Mayors and Independents|STAN]], and [[KDU-ČSL]].

Babiš ran again as leader of ANO, and the main opposition parliamentary parties formed two electoral alliances, [[Spolu (Czech Republic)|SPOLU]] and [[Pirates and Mayors]] (abbreviated to PirStan or PaS). ANO was front runner of the election, as it was polling first ahead of SPOLU and PirStan prior to the election.<ref name="aktualne041021">{{cite web|title=Spolu posiluje, ale ANO neporazí, Piráti už vůbec, říkají autoři posledních průzkumů|url=https://zpravy.aktualne.cz/domaci/volby/volby-pruzkumy/r~92a6f456250911ecb91a0cc47ab5f122/|website=Aktuálně.cz|access-date=13 October 2021|language=cs|date=4 October 2021}}</ref><ref name="Vyhrálo by hnutí ANO, favorité voleb mírně oslabili, říká poslední průzkum">{{cite web|title=Vyhrálo by hnutí ANO, favorité voleb mírně oslabili, říká poslední průzkum|url=https://www.idnes.cz/volby/volby-pruzkum-hnuti-ano-koalice-spolu-pirstan.A211003_202645_volby_lisv|website=Mladá fronta Dnes|access-date=13 October 2021|language=cs|date=4 October 2021}}</ref><ref name="Volby 2021: Favoritem je Babiš před koalicí Spolu a Piráty se Starosty newsbox.cz">{{cite web|title=Volby 2021: Favoritem je Babiš před koalicí Spolu a Piráty se Starosty|url=https://newsbox.cz/zpravy/volby-2021-favoritem-je-babis-pred-koalici-spolu-a-piraty-se-starosty-fmlgs89i|website=newsbox.cz|access-date=13 October 2021|language=sk}}</ref> The result was a [[Upset (competition)|surprise victory]] for the [[liberal conservative]] alliance SPOLU, which received the highest number of votes, while the [[populist]] ANO received the highest number of seats.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kudrnáč|first1=Aleš|last2=Petrúšek|first2=Ivan|year=2022|title=Czech Republic: Political Developments and Data in 2021: Historic Electoral Loss of the Left|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/2047-8852.12358|journal=European Journal of Political Research Political Data Yearbook|volume=61|issue=1|pages=111–126|doi=10.1111/2047-8852.12358|issn=2047-8844|doi-access=free}}</ref> No opinion poll placed Spolu in the first place prior to the vote.<ref name="Proč nikdo neřekl, že vyhraje Fiala? Průzkumy nestihly volební finiš - Seznam Zprávy">{{cite web|title=Proč nikdo neřekl, že vyhraje Fiala? Průzkumy nestihly volební finiš|url=https://www.seznamzpravy.cz/clanek/proc-nikdo-nerekl-ze-vyhraje-fiala-pruzkumy-nestihly-volebni-finis-177617|website=Seznam Zprávy|access-date=13 October 2021|language=cs}}</ref> It was the closest parliamentary election in the history of Czech Republic.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Czech PM's party loses election to liberal-conservative coalition|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/oct/09/czech-pm-set-to-lose-power-after-weak-showing-in-general-election|newspaper=The Guardian|date=9 October 2021|access-date=10 October 2021}}</ref>

The opposition parties won a majority in the Chamber of Deputies and agreed to form a coalition government with SPOLU leader [[Petr Fiala]] as the new prime minister.<ref name="Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babiš's populist party loses grip on power in nail-bitingly close election">{{cite web|first1=John|last1=Mastrini|first2=Sheena|last2=McKenzie|title=Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babiš's populist party loses grip on power in nail-bitingly close election|url=https://edition.cnn.com/2021/10/09/europe/czech-election-andrej-babi-intl/index.html|publisher=[[CNN]]|date=9 October 2021|access-date=9 October 2021}}</ref><ref name="ONLINE: Nečekaný triumf koalice Spolu. V posledním momentu přeskočila ANO a vyhrála sněmovní volby">{{cite web|title=Online: Nečekaný triumf koalice Spolu. V posledním momentu přeskočila ANO a vyhrála sněmovní volby|url=https://www.irozhlas.cz/volby/volby-2021-koalice-spolu-vitez-voleb-fiala-pekarova_2110091832_kno|website=[[Czech Radio]]|date=9 October 2021|access-date=9 October 2021|language=cs}}</ref><ref name="Koalice se dohodly, chtějí pro Fialu pověření od prezidenta - Novinky.cz">{{cite web|title=Koalice se dohodly, chtějí pro Fialu pověření od prezidenta|url=https://www.novinky.cz/volby/do-poslanecke-snemovny/clanek/koalice-se-dohodly-vytvorime-vladu-a-s-nikym-jinym-o-ni-jednat-nebudeme-40374429|website=[[Novinky.cz]]|access-date=9 October 2021|language=cs}}</ref> Traditional [[left-wing]] parties ČSSD and KSČM failed to reach the 5% threshold to win any seats in the Chamber of Deputies for the first time since the [[dissolution of Czechoslovakia]] in 1993.<ref>{{Cite web|date=9 October 2021|title=Populist Czech PM Babis's party narrowly loses election in surprise result|url=https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20211009-populist-czech-pm-babis-s-party-narrowly-loses-czech-election-in-surprise-result|url-status=live|access-date=10 October 2021|publisher=France 24|quote=Both the Social Democrats and the Communists, the country's traditional parliamentary parties, failed to win seats in parliament for the first time since the split of Czechoslovakia in 1993.|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211009190208/https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20211009-populist-czech-pm-babis-s-party-narrowly-loses-czech-election-in-surprise-result|archive-date=9 October 2021}}</ref> The Pirates, which were one of the leading opposition parties, were heavily defeated due to preferential votes and won just 4 seats in the Chamber of Deputies.<ref name="Starostové kroužkováním zmasakrovali Piráty - Novinky.cz">{{cite web|title=Starostové kroužkováním zmasakrovali Piráty|url=https://www.novinky.cz/volby/do-poslanecke-snemovny/clanek/starostove-krouzkovanim-zmasakrovali-piraty-40374403|website=Novinky.cz|access-date=9 October 2021|language=cs}}</ref> Petr Fiala was appointed as the new prime minister on 28 November 2021 while rest of the new cabinet was appointed on 17 December 2021.

== Background ==
{{see also|2017 Czech parliamentary election}}
According to the [[Constitution of the Czech Republic]], an election to the [[Chamber of Deputies of the Czech Republic|Chamber of Deputies]], the lower house of the [[Czech parliament]], must be held every four years. The government is answerable to the Chamber of Deputies and remains in power only with the confidence of the majority of members of parliament. Article 19(1) of the constitution states that any citizen of the Czech Republic who has right to vote and is 21 years old is eligible to serve as an MP.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Czech Republic's Constitution of 1993 with Amendments through 2013|url=https://www.constituteproject.org/constitution/Czech_Republic_2013.pdf?lang=en|url-status=live|quote=Article 19. 1. Any citizen of the Czech Republic who has the right to vote and has attained the age of twenty-one is eligible for election to the Assembly of Deputies.|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210419152817/https://www.constituteproject.org/constitution/Czech_Republic_2013.pdf?lang=en|archive-date=19 April 2021}}</ref>

[[ANO (political party)|ANO]] emerged as the largest party in the 2017 parliamentary election and formed a [[Andrej Babiš' First Cabinet|minority government]], which then lost a vote of confidence on 16 January 2018. The party formed a [[coalition government]] with the [[Czech Social Democratic Party]] (ČSSD), supported by the [[Communist Party of Bohemia and Moravia]] (KSČM), which lasted until April 2021. [[Andrej Babiš]] became the new prime minister. The [[Civic Democratic Party (Czech Republic)|Civic Democratic Party]] (ODS) emerged as the second largest party and main opposition party, narrowly ahead of the [[Czech Pirate Party]].<ref>{{cite web|last1=Zlámalová|first1=Lenka|title=Souboj o přízeň tažných koní. ODS a Piráti se spolu přetahují o voliče všech generací|url=https://www.echo24.cz/a/SypP7/souboj-o-prizen-taznych-koni-ods-a-pirati-se-spolu-pretahuji-o-volice-vsech-generaci|website=Echo24|access-date=26 October 2020|language=cs|date=4 April 2019}}</ref>

=== 2018 Senate and municipal elections ===
{{main|2018 Czech municipal elections|2018 Czech Senate election}}

In 2018, voters elected 27 of 81 members of the [[Senate of the Czech Republic|Senate]] and approximately 61,900 members of local councils. ODS won the Senate election with 10 senators elected.<ref>{{cite web|title=Fiasko vládních stran. Světová média si všímají vítězství ODS i porážky KSČM|url=https://www.lidovky.cz/svet/svetova-media-si-vsimaji-vitezstvi-ods-ve-volbach-a-porazky-komunistu.A181013_185653_ln_zahranici_ele|website=Lidové noviny|access-date=26 October 2020|language=cs|date=13 October 2018}}</ref> ANO won the municipal elections in most regional cities, with ODS finishing first in [[Prague]] and [[Mayors and Independents|STAN]] in [[Liberec]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Hnutí ANO vyhrálo v drtivé většině měst. Výjimkami jsou Praha a Liberec|url=https://echo24.cz/a/Sxguj/hnuti-ano-vyhralo-v-drtive-vetsine-mest-vyjimkami-jsou-praha-a-liberec|website=echo24.cz|access-date=26 October 2020|language=cs|date=6 October 2018}}</ref> ČSSD and KSČM lost over half of their votes and seats in municipal councils.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cz.boell.org/en/2020/11/02/krajske-senatni-volby-2020-horke-vitezstvi-pro-babise-dominance-opozice-v-senatu|title=Czech Senate and regional elections 2020: Bitter victory for the Prime Minister, dominance of the opposition in the Senate|website=Heinrich Böll Stiftung}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/13597566.2021.1948839?journalCode=frfs20|doi=10.1080/13597566.2021.1948839|title=The 2020 Czech regional elections: A story of a winner that lost|year=2021|last1=Kouba|first1=Karel|last2=Lysek|first2=Jakub|journal=Regional & Federal Studies|volume=32|issue=4|pages=1–13|s2cid=237827332|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

=== 2019 European Parliament election ===
{{main|2019 European Parliament election in the Czech Republic}}

In May 2019, voters elected 21 members of the [[European Parliament]]. ANO came first, with ODS and the Pirates close behind in number of seats. As ČSSD failed to achieve more than 5 percent of votes in national elections for the first time since the mid-1990s, it did not get any seat.<ref>{{cite web|date=2 May 2019|title=Results by national party: 2019–2024|url=https://europarl.europa.eu/election-results-2019/en/national-results/czechia/2019-2024/|access-date=12 October 2021|website=European Parliament}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|date=May 2019|title=2019 European Parliament election in the Czech Republic|url=https://www.europeansources.info/record/2019-european-parliament-election-in-the-czech-republic/|access-date=12 October 2021|website=European Sources Online}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Málek|first=Jiří|date=26 May 2019|title=Czechia: Results of EU Elections 2019|url=https://www.transform-network.net/en/focus/overview/article/ep-2019-the-european-left-one-mouth-many-voices/czechia-results-of-eu-elections-2019/|access-date=12 October 2021|website=Transform! Europe|publisher=Party of the European Left}}</ref>

=== 2020 Senate and regional elections ===
{{main|2020 Czech regional elections|2020 Czech Senate election}}

In October 2020, voters elected 675 members of regional assemblies in 13 regions of the nation, except Prague, which then formed regional governments. ANO won the election with 21.8% of votes but opposition parties, especially the Pirates, made gains, while allies of ANO were heavily defeated.<ref>{{cite news|first=Andrea|last=Gričová|title=Krajské volby ovládlo ANO, vyhráno ale nemá. ČSSD a komunisté propadli|url=https://www.denik.cz/z_domova/volby-krajske-senat-vitez-ucast-20201003.html|website=[[Deník]]|publisher=Vltave Labe Media|access-date=26 October 2020|language=cs|date=3 October 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Piráti jsou skokanem voleb. Za každou cenu vládnout nechceme, říká Bartoš|url=https://www.seznamzpravy.cz/clanek/pirati-si-vyzkouseli-svoji-silu-do-predvolebnich-koalic-se-nezenou-122657|website=Seznam Zprávy|access-date=26 October 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Komentář: ANO drží pozice i náskok, ale ztrácí spojence|url=https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/komentar-krajske-volby-vysledky-ano-cssd-kdu-csl-kscm-stan-pirati.A201003_191826_domaci_misl|website=Mladá fronta Dnes|access-date=26 October 2020|date=3 October 2020}}</ref> The governing parties were also heavily defeated in the Senate elections, which were won by [[Mayors and Independents]] ahead of ODS.<ref>{{cite web|title=Volby do Senátu jsou sečteny. Debakl pro ANO a ČSSD, úspěch pro STAN|url=https://tn.nova.cz/clanek/druhe-kolo-senatnich-voleb-cesi-dnes-poznaji-tretinu-novych-senatoru.html|website=[[TV Nova (Czech Republic)|TV Nova Czech Republic]]|access-date=26 October 2020|language=cs|date=10 October 2020}}</ref>

=== Coalitions of political parties ===
Following these elections, opposition parties began negotiations about potential electoral alliances. It was speculated that two electoral blocs would be formed: a [[conservative]] bloc led by ODS, which would also include [[KDU-ČSL]] and [[TOP 09]], with [[Petr Fiala]] as leader, and a [[Liberalism|liberal]] bloc composed of the Pirates and [[Mayors and Independents]], with [[Ivan Bartoš]] as the leader.<ref>{{cite web|title=Námluvy pokročily. Jak se pečou koalice proti Babišovi do velkých voleb?|url=https://cnn.iprima.cz/namluvy-pokrocily-jak-se-pecou-koalice-proti-babisovi-do-velkych-voleb-10635|website=[[CNN Prima News]]|access-date=26 October 2020|language=cs}}</ref>

The ODS leadership agreed to form an alliance on 25 October 2020, with a memorandum to be signed two days later.<ref>{{cite web|title=Pravicové strany směřují k očekávané volební koalici. V úterý mají podepsat memorandum|url=https://www.lidovky.cz/domov/ods-top-09-a-kdu-csl-jdou-do-trojkoalice-v-utery-maji-podepsat-memorandum.A201025_092806_ln_domov_likv|website=Lidové noviny|access-date=26 October 2020|language=cs|date=25 October 2020}}</ref> On 27 October 2020, Fiala, [[Marian Jurečka]], and [[Markéta Pekarová Adamová]] announced that ODS, KDU-ČSL, and TOP 09 would form an electoral alliance for the next parliamentary election, with ODS leader Fiala as the alliance's candidate for prime minister.<ref>{{cite web|title=ODS, TOP 09 a KDU-ČSL půjdou do voleb společně. Chtějí je vyhrát|url=https://ct24.ceskatelevize.cz/domaci/3215797-ods-top-09-a-kdu-csl-pujdou-do-voleb-spolecne-chteji-je-vyhrat|website=[[ČT24]]|publisher=[[Czech Television]]|access-date=28 October 2020|language=cs}}</ref> On 11 November 2020, the parties agreed that ODS would nominate the leaders of the election lists in nine regions, KDU-ČSL in three regions, and TOP 09 in two regions.<ref>{{cite web|title=Trojkoalice si rozdělila lídry. ODS 9, lidovci 3, topka 2|url=https://www.novinky.cz/volby/clanek/trojkoalice-si-rozdelila-lidry-ods-9-lidovci-3-topka-2-40341881#|website=Novinky.cz|access-date=11 November 2020|language=cs}}</ref> The name of the alliance was announced as [[Spolu (Czech Republic)|SPOLU]], meaning "Together" in English.<ref>{{cite web|title=ODS, KDU-ČSL a TOP 09 jdou do voleb jako koalice SPOLU. Daly 17 slibů|url=https://www.seznamzpravy.cz/clanek/ods-kdu-csl-a-top-09-jsou-do-voleb-jako-koalice-spolu-133025|website=Seznam Zprávy|access-date=9 December 2020|language=cs}}</ref> Fiala was confirmed as the alliance's candidate for prime minister on 16 December 2020.<ref>{{cite web|title=Kandidát ODS, TOP 09 a KDU-ČSL na premiéra je Fiala, strany zachovají kluby|url=https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/koalice-ods-top-09-kdu-csl-kandidat-na-premiera-fiala.A201216_112017_domaci_kop|website=Mladá fronta Dnes|access-date=16 December 2020|date=16 December 2020|language=cs}}</ref>

[[File:Vít Rakušan Ivan Bartoš 18 May 2021.jpg|thumb|left|[[Vít Rakušan]] and [[Ivan Bartoš]], leaders of [[Pirates and Mayors]].]]
The leadership of [[Mayors and Independents]] agreed to start negotiations on 8 October 2020.<ref>{{cite web|title=STAN schválil zahájení vyjednávání s Piráty o koalici pro parlamentní volby|url=https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/stn-pirati-koalice-volby-2021.A201008_175326_domaci_kop|website=Mladá fronta Dnes|access-date=26 October 2020|date=8 October 2020|language=cs}}</ref> The Pirates are required to ratify any alliance in a members' referendum. In a poll on 20 October 2020, 51% of Pirate members were opposed to the alliance while 43% supported it. The referendum to starting negotiations for an alliance was originally scheduled for 13 to 16 November 2020<ref>{{cite web|title=Piráti zatím odmítají spolupráci se STAN. Bojí se zneužití|url=https://www.novinky.cz/domaci/clanek/pirati-zatim-odmitaji-spolupraci-se-stan-boji-se-zneuziti-40339863|website=Novinky.cz|access-date=26 October 2020|language=cs}}</ref> but was rescheduled for 20 to 23 November 2020.<ref>{{cite news|title=Piráti o koalici se STAN: Nechceme si konkurovat. Jasno bude koncem listopadu|url=https://www.denik.cz/z_domova/pirati-stan-koalice-volby-2021.html|website=Deník|access-date=19 November 2020|language=cs|date=7 November 2020}}</ref> Among Pirate members, 695 out of 858 voted in favour of negotiations, with a turnout of 80%.<ref>{{cite web|title=Piráti začnou jednat o koalici se STAN. Členové dali zelenou v referendu|url=https://www.seznamzpravy.cz/clanek/pirati-zacnou-jednat-se-starosty-o-koalici-clenove-dali-zelenou-v-referendu-130907|website=Seznam Zprávy|access-date=24 November 2020|language=cs}}</ref> [[Ivan Bartoš]] was nominated to be the Pirate's election leader on 25 November 2020,<ref>{{cite web|title=Bartoš míří na lídra koalice se STAN|url=https://www.novinky.cz/domaci/clanek/bartos-miri-na-lidra-koalice-se-stan-40343219#|website=Novinky.cz|access-date=25 November 2020|language=cs}}</ref> and was confirmed on 2 December 2020. The Pirates also offered the [[Green Party (Czech Republic)|Green Party]] the possibility to join its electoral list.<ref>{{cite web|title=Piráty povede do voleb Bartoš, potvrdili členové v referendu|url=https://www.novinky.cz/domaci/clanek/piraty-povede-do-voleb-bartos-potvrdili-clenove-v-referendu-40343922|website=Novinky.cz|access-date=2 December 2020|language=cs}}</ref> Bartoš was confirmed as the alliance's electoral leader on 14 December 2020.<ref>{{cite web|title=Koalici Pirátů a STAN povede Bartoš. Chtějí spolu do vlády či opozice|url=https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/pirati-stan-koalice-jednani-tiskova-konference.A201214_163230_domaci_ajez|website=Mladá fronta Dnes|access-date=16 December 2020|date=14 December 2020|language=cs}}</ref> Pirate members voted to approve the alliance on 13 January 2021.<ref>{{cite web|title=Piráti potvrdili koalici se STAN. Vyvedeme spolu zemi z krize, slíbil Bartoš|url=https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/pirati-koalice-s-hnutim-stan-volby-do-snemovny-internetove-hlasovani.A210112_060941_domaci_kop|website=Mladá fronta Dnes|access-date=14 January 2021|date=12 January 2021|language=cs}}</ref>

ČSSD started to negotiate the formation of a third electoral bloc in January 2021, negotiating with the [[Green Party (Czech Republic)|Green Party]] and some regional parties about the formation of a left-wing electoral alliance.<ref>{{cite web|title=Formuje se třetí blok proti Babišovi. ČSSD chystá vlastní koalici|url=https://www.seznamzpravy.cz/clanek/formuje-se-treti-blok-proti-babisovi-cssd-chysta-vlastni-koalici-136768#|website=Seznam Zprávy|access-date=8 January 2021|language=cs}}</ref> The Green Party stated as a condition for joining an alliance that the parties would not form a government coalition with ANO after the election.<ref>{{cite web|title=Zelení si dali podmínku pro spolupráci s ČSSD. Nesmí vést k vládě s Babišem|url=https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/zeleni-podminka-pro-spolecny-postup-ve-volbach-s-cssd-ne-s-babisem.A210130_200209_domaci_kop|website=Mladá fronta Dnes|date=30 January 2021|access-date=3 February 2021|language=cs}}</ref>

In early 2021, the [[Tricolour Citizens' Movement]], [[Svobodní]], the [[Freeholder Party of the Czech Republic]], and other minor parties began negotiations about a potential alliance.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Leinert|first1=Ondřej|title=Trikolóra se Svobodnými a Soukromníky? Do voleb teď můžeme jít i s deseti stranami, plánuje Klaus mladší|url=https://archiv.ihned.cz/c1-66879110-trikolora-se-svobodnymi-a-soukromniky-do-voleb-ted-muzeme-jit-i-s-deseti-stranami-planuje-klaus-mladsi|website=[[Hospodářské noviny]]|access-date=16 February 2021|language=cs|date=5 February 2021}}</ref> On 5 March 2021, these three parties confirmed the formation of a coalition, stating that they would run either in a formal electoral alliance or as a single party, depending on the new electoral law.<ref>{{cite web|title=Trikolóra, Soukromníci a Svobodní půjdou do voleb spolu. Jsme otevřeni i pro další subjekty, řekl Klaus mladší|url=https://ct24.ceskatelevize.cz/domaci/3278602-trikolora-soukromnici-a-svobodni-pujdou-do-voleb-spolu-jsme-otevreni-i-pro-dalsi|website=[[ČT24]]|publisher=[[Czech Television]]|access-date=4 March 2021|language=cs}}</ref> The [[Independence Party of the Czech Republic]] declared support for this coalition soon after.<ref>{{cite web|title=Už se to valí. Pravice nebude štěpit síly. Ke Klausovi, Vondráčkovi a Bajerovi se přidávají další|url=https://www.parlamentnilisty.cz/arena/monitor/Uz-se-to-vali-Pravice-nebude-stepit-sily-Ke-Klausovi-Vondrackovi-a-Bajerovi-se-pridavaji-dalsi-656163|website=Parlamentní listy|access-date=6 March 2021|language=cs}}</ref> On 23 March 2021, Tricolour leader [[Václav Klaus Jr.]] resigned from all political functions for personal reasons.<ref>{{cite web|title=Václav Klaus ml. končí v politice|url=https://www.novinky.cz/domaci/clanek/vaclav-klaus-ml-konci-v-politice-40354829|website=Novinky.cz|date=23 March 2021|language=cs}}</ref> [[Zuzana Majerová Zahradníková]] became acting leader of the party.<ref>{{cite web|title=Trikolóru povede Majerová Zahradníková, Klaus ml. rezignoval|url=https://www.novinky.cz/domaci/clanek/trikoloru-povede-majerova-zahradnikova-klaus-ml-rezignoval-40354890|website=Novinky.cz|access-date=23 March 2021|language=cs}}</ref>

On 23 March 2021, a group of minor parties including the [[Alliance for the Future (Czech Republic)|Alliance for the Future]], Agrarian Democratic Party, [[Order of the Nation (political party)|Order of the Nation]], and [[Democratic Green Party]] formed an electoral alliance, the Alliance for the Future, with [[Pavel Sehnal]] as leader.<ref>{{cite web|title=Další koalice. Do voleb jde Aliance pro budoucnost|url=https://www.tyden.cz/rubriky/domaci/dalsi-koalice-do-voleb-jde-aliance-pro-budoucnost_550889.html|website=[[Týden]]|access-date=24 March 2021|language=cs|date=23 March 2021}}</ref> The [[Party of Common Sense]] also subsequently joined the alliance.<ref>{{cite web|title=K Alianci pro budoucnost se připojili Rozumní Petra Hanniga|url=https://www.ceskenoviny.cz/zpravy/k-alianci-pro-budoucnost-se-pripojili-rozumni-petra-hanniga/2062067|website=České Noviny|access-date=27 July 2021|language=cs|date=14 July 2021}}</ref>

Some commentators have described the election as a "hidden referendum" on membership of the [[European Union]] (EU).<ref name="pes1">{{cite news|first=Ondřej|last=Neff|title=Kdopak by se pirátů bál|url=https://neviditelnypes.lidovky.cz/cirkus/kdopak-by-se-piratu-bal.A210930_214531_p_cirkus_nef|access-date=4 October 2021|work=Neviditelný pes|date=1 October 2021|language=cs}}</ref><ref name="pes2">{{cite news|first=František|last=Novotný|title=Volby: Skryté referendum o EU|url=https://neviditelnypes.lidovky.cz/politika/volby-skryte-referendum-o-eu.A211001_164349_p_politika_wag|access-date=4 October 2021|work=Neviditelný pes|date=4 October 2021|language=cs}}</ref><ref name="čt24">{{cite news|title=Volební lídři v Praze se přeli o to, co Česku přináší členství v Evropské unii|url=https://ct24.ceskatelevize.cz/domaci/3378780-volebni-lidri-v-praze-se-preli-o-co-cesku-prinasi-clenstvi-v-evropske-unii|access-date=4 October 2021|website=[[ČT24]]|publisher=[[Czech Television]]|date=1 October 2021|language=cs}}</ref>

== Electoral system ==
{{further|Elections in the Czech Republic|Politics of the Czech Republic}}
[[File:Hlasovací lístky PSP 2021 Praha.jpg|thumb|Set of ballots for the 2021 parliamentary elections for the Prague voting district]]
During the 2017 parliamentary election, the 200 members of the Chamber of Deputies were elected from 14 multi-member constituencies by [[open list]] [[proportional representation]] with an [[electoral threshold]] of 5%. It was raised to 10% for two-party [[political alliance]]s, 15% for three-party alliances, and 20% for alliances of four or more parties. Seats were allocated using the [[D'Hondt method]]. Voters can give preference votes to up to four candidates on a list. Candidates who receive preferential votes from more than 5% of voters are moved to the top of their list; in cases where more than one candidate receives over 5% of the preferential votes, they are ranked in order of votes received.<ref>{{Cite web|title=IPU parline database: Czech Republic (Poslanecka Snemovna), Electoral system|url=http://archive.ipu.org/parline-e/reports/2083_B.htm|access-date=14 February 2021|website=archive.ipu.org}}</ref>

Although it was expected that the 2021 parliamentary election would take place using the same electoral system, the [[Constitutional Court of the Czech Republic|Constitutional Court]] ruled on a complaint submitted by a group of senators from [[Mayors and Independents]], [[KDU-ČSL]], and [[TOP 09]] that the electoral system was unproportional and favoured larger parties. It focused on the [[D'Hondt method]], the division of the country into 14 constituencies, and the increased electoral threshold for alliances.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ústavní soud rozhodl o systému sněmovních voleb. Výsledek oznámí ve středu|url=https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/us-rozhodl-o-systemu-snemovnich-voleb-vysledek-oznami-ve-stredu-zeman-volby.A210202_153024_domaci_lre|website=Mladá fronta Dnes|access-date=3 February 2021|date=2 February 2021|language=cs}}</ref> The Constitutional Court's decision, published on 3 February 2021, set the threshold for alliances at 5% and removed some provisions relating to seat allocation.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ústavní soud zrušil část volebního zákona, ulevil koalicím a zrušil bonus pro vítěze|url=https://www.novinky.cz/domaci/clanek/ustavni-soud-zrusil-cast-volebniho-zakona-40349771#|website=Novinky.cz|access-date=3 February 2021|language=cs}}</ref> New provisions were put into law before the election, establishing a threshold of 5% for single parties, 8% for coalitions of two parties, and 11% for coalitions of three or more parties.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.psp.cz/en/sqw/cms.sqw?z=14710|title=Chamber passes required changes to election law (7.04.2021)|website=PSP.cz|access-date=12 August 2024}}</ref>

===Registration process===
The deadline to submit candidate lists for election was 4 August 2021. As of 2 August 2021, 29 subjects had made an application to the registration bureau.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lhůta k přihlášení do sněmovních voleb se krátí. Zájem má zatím kolem 30 uskupení|url=https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/volby-do-poslanecke-snemovny-2021-kandidatky-snemovni-volby_2108021110_ern|website=Czech Radio|date=2 August 2021|access-date=4 November 2021|language=cs}}</ref> All of them were approved by the bureau and permitted to run.<ref>{{cite web|title=Úřady potvrdily kandidátky do voleb všem 22 přihlášeným uskupením|url=https://www.ceskenoviny.cz/zpravy/urady-potvrdily-kandidatky-do-voleb-vsem-22-prihlasenym-uskupenim/2079033|website=České Noviny|access-date=4 November 2021|language=cs}}</ref>

=== Observers ===
Czech Republic invited experts from [[Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe]] (OSCE) and [[Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights]] (ODIHR) to observe election.<ref name="Česko opět pozve mezinárodní pozorovatele, aby přijeli na sněmovní volby">{{cite web|title=Česko opět pozve mezinárodní pozorovatele, aby přijeli na sněmovní volby|url=https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/cesko-pozve-staty-obse-volby-snemovna-pozorovani.A210711_175810_domaci_pmk|website=Mladá fronta Dnes|access-date=4 November 2021|language=cs|date=11 July 2021}}</ref> OSCE provided four observers.<ref name="Férovost českých voleb budou hlídat čtyři mezinárodní experti. Nevládní organizace plošný dohled nechystají">{{cite web|title=Férovost českých voleb budou hlídat čtyři mezinárodní experti. Nevládní organizace plošný dohled nechystají|url=https://ct24.ceskatelevize.cz/domaci/3373858-ferovost-ceskych-voleb-budou-hlidat-ctyri-mezinarodni-experti-nevladni-organizace|website=ČT24|publisher=Czech Television|access-date=4 November 2021|language=cs}}</ref>

===Covid-19 pandemic===
[[File:Covid-19 testing site - Prague, Náměstí Míru.jpg|thumb|COVID-19 testing site in Prague. COVID-19 affected the election with some changes required to allow quarantined and isolated people to vote.]]
As with the regional elections in 2020, the pandemic emergency, covered by the pandemic law,<ref>{{cite web|title=94/2021 Sb. Zákon o mimořádných opatřeních při epidemii onemocnění COVID-19 a o změně některých souvisejících zá...|url=https://www.zakonyprolidi.cz/cs/2021-94|website=Zákony pro lidi|access-date=12 November 2021|language=cs}}</ref> allowed for the establishment of special polling stations for people in isolation or quarantine, as well as drive-in voting locations. Disinfection and respiratory protection were provided to ensure hygienic conditions in traditional polling stations. Special election dates were announced on 6 and 7 October 2021.<ref>{{cite news|title=Zeman vyhlásil termíny voleb pro lidi v karanténě. Uskuteční se 6. října|url=https://prazsky.denik.cz/volby-ps-2021/cesko-volby-koronavirus-karantena-20210916.html|website=Pražský Deník|access-date=12 November 2021|language=cs|date=16 September 2021}}</ref>

===Local referendums===
Simultaneously with the election, there were local referendums held in 20 cities and towns: [[Blšany u Loun]], [[Blučina]], [[Bzenec]], [[Dačice]], [[Drnholec]], [[Jáchymov]], [[Jezeřany-Maršovice]], [[Katovice]], [[Losiná]], [[Pardubice]], [[Podolí (Brno-Country District)|Podolí]], [[Příkosice]], [[Řevnice]], [[Slavonice]], [[Sušice]], [[Ševětín]], [[Temelín]], [[Třemošnice]], [[Velký Beranov]], [[Zduchovice]] and Stará Bělá (part of [[Ostrava]]).<ref>{{cite web|title=Volby ve 20 obcích doplní místní referenda. Lidé rozhodnou o stavbách nebo osudu nemocnice|url=https://www.irozhlas.cz/volby/parlamentni-volby-2021-obce-mistni-referenda-hlasovani_2110080747_tzr|website=Czech Radio|access-date=27 August 2023|language=cs|date=8 October 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Šimon|last=Rogner|title=Spolu s volbami proběhne šestnáct místních referend. Rozhodnou o Zelené bráně i o chovu jelena|url=https://ct24.ceskatelevize.cz/domaci/3371466-spolu-s-volbami-probehne-sestnact-mistnich-referend-rozhodnou-o-zelene-brane-i-o|website=ČT24|publisher=Czech Television|access-date=27 August 2023|language=cs}}</ref>
