== Campaign ==
[[File:Kampan2021.jpg|thumb|2021 Campaign.]]

===Issues===
The campaign was significantly affected by the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the Czech Republic|COVID-19 pandemic]], with opposition parties criticizing the government for its handling of the pandemic and emphasising the country's high death rate. Some parties also focused their campaigns around opposition to the COVID-19 restrictions. Meanwhile, the government parties defended their handling of the crisis, and some government ministers argued that the situation would have been worse if the opposition had been in government. This issue later lost prominence, with economic issues receiving more attention. Several political scientists, including Daniel Prokop, characterised the election as a referendum on Prime Minister Andrej Babiš.<ref>{{cite web|title=Předvolební kampaň končí a s ní intriky, lži a nekonečné hádky. Třeba se začne i vládnout|url=https://www.e15.cz/nazory/jan-novotny-predvolebni-kampan-konci-treba-se-zacne-i-vladnout-1384206|website=E15.cz|access-date=2 November 2021|language=cs}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Jan|last=Tvrdoň|title=Prokop: Opozice nedokázala využít covid. Koalice Spolu riskuje, že bude muset vládnout v rozporu se svým programem|url=https://denikn.cz/690995/prokop-opozice-nedokazala-vyuzit-covid-koalice-spolu-riskuje-ze-bude-muset-vladnout-v-rozporu-se-svym-programem/|website=Deník N|access-date=2 November 2021|language=cs|date=27 August 2021}}</ref> During the final phase of the campaign, inflation and the increasing prices of groceries became the main issue, reflected in Spolu's campaign slogan: "The cost of Babiš".<ref>{{cite web|title=Komentář: Inflace v kampani. Babišova drahota, nebo opoziční levota?|url=https://www.seznamzpravy.cz/clanek/komentar-inflace-v-kampani-babisova-drahota-nebo-opozicni-levota-176105|website=Seznam Zprávy|access-date=2 November 2021|language=cs}}</ref>

ANO and the far-right parties also focused on immigration during their campaigns, criticising multiculturalism and pledging to prevent "Muslim Europe".<ref>{{cite web|title=Hlavní téma voleb: Daně, kvalita potravin, koronavirus i migrace|url=https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/volby-migrace-verejne-mineni.A210808_200445_domaci_frum|website=Mladá fronta Dnes|access-date=2 November 2021|language=cs|date=9 August 2021}}</ref>

===Party campaigns===
==== Alliance for the Future ====
In March 2021, the Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA) formed an electoral alliance with other minor parties called Alliance for the Future (APB), led by Pavel Sehnal. Parties in the alliance included the Agrarian Democratic Party, [[Order of the Nation (political party)|Order of the Nation]] and the [[Democratic Party of Greens]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Další koalice. Do voleb jde Aliance pro budoucnost|url=https://www.tyden.cz/rubriky/domaci/dalsi-koalice-do-voleb-jde-aliance-pro-budoucnost_550889.html|website=Týden|access-date=9 December 2021|language=cs|date=23 March 2021}}</ref> The same year in July, the [[Party of Common Sense]] joined the alliance.<ref>{{cite web|title=Aliance pro budoucnost se rozrostla o další nové subjekty a známé osobnosti|url=https://www.parlamentnilisty.cz/arena/monitor/Aliance-pro-budoucnost-se-rozrostla-o-dalsi-nove-subjekty-a-zname-osobnosti-670572|website=Parlamentní listy|access-date=9 December 2021}}</ref> ODA formally changed its name to Alliance for the Future to avoid the higher electoral threshold.<ref>{{cite web|title=Menší neparlamentní strany budou kandidovat do Sněmovny v alianci|url=https://www.ceskenoviny.cz/zpravy/mensi-neparlamentni-strany-budou-kandidovat-do-snemovny-v-alianci/2010885|website=České noviny|access-date=9 December 2021|language=cs}}</ref>

The alliance's campaign was launched at a press conference on 16 June 2021, where Sehnal introduced APB's priorities, including support for Czech businesses and lower taxes. He also declared support for transatlantic cooperation and EU membership.<ref>{{cite web|title=Formace dalšího miliardáře jde do voleb. Sehnal nabízí pravicovou politiku|url=https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/aliance-pro-budoucnost-volby-pravicova-politika-sehnal.A210616_135631_domaci_mkop|website=Mladá fronta Dnes|date=16 June 2021|access-date=9 December 2021|language=cs}}</ref>

==== ANO ====
[[File:Volby 10 - 2021 (1).jpg|thumb|ANO billboard]]
After opinion polls in early 2021 showed [[ANO (political party)|ANO]] falling behind the [[Czech Pirate Party]], prime minister [[Andrej Babiš]] reacted by attacking the Pirates for their progressive stances, such as their supposed support for immigration and legalisation of drug use.<ref>{{cite web|title=Proč Babiš útočí jen na Piráty|url=https://www.irozhlas.cz/komentare/hnuti-ano-andrej-babis-pirati-vlada-snemovni-volby-2021-kampan_2106161705_onz|website=Czech Radio|date=16 June 2021|access-date=25 September 2021|language=cs}}</ref> The party's campaign thus focused on criticism of the Pirates in early 2021.<ref>{{cite web|title=Piráti jako veřejný nepřítel číslo 1. Komu fandí dezinformátoři?|url=https://www.e15.cz/volby/volby-do-snemovny/pirati-jako-nepritel-horsi-nez-brusel-s-usa-dohromady-u-dezinformatoru-boduje-babis-1382986|website=E15.cz|access-date=25 September 2021|language=cs}}</ref> On 27 June 2021 President Miloš Zeman endorsed ANO, stating that he would vote for the party.<ref>{{cite web|title=Zeman ve volbách hodí hlas hnutí ANO, volební koalice považuje za podvod. Jen útočí na konkurenci Babiše, míní politologové|url=https://domaci.hn.cz/c1-66945540-zeman-ve-volbach-hodi-hlas-hnuti-ano-volebni-koalice-povazuje-za-podvod|website=Hospodářské noviny|date=27 June 2021|access-date=4 November 2021|language=cs}}</ref>

In July 2021, ANO published a book, ''Share it, before they ban it'', allegedly written by Babiš, who began promoting the book during the campaign with book signings. The book primarily boasted about Babiš record in government.<ref>{{cite web|title=Babiš se v knize chlubí úspěchy firem. Nikdo nám o tom neřekl, říkají rozpačitě podniky|url=https://www.e15.cz/domaci/babis-se-v-knize-chlubi-uspechy-firem-nikdo-nam-o-tom-nerekl-rikaji-rozpacite-podniky-1382354|website=E15.cz|access-date=9 November 2021|language=cs}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title="Je třeba vypláchnout špínu." Po Babišovi v Teplicích šel muž s hadicí, zasáhla ochranka|url=https://www.blesk.cz/clanek/volby-volby-do-snemovny/687145/je-treba-vyplachnout-spinu-po-babisovi-v-teplicich-sel-muz-s-hadici-zasahla-ochranka.html|website=Blesk|access-date=9 November 2021|language=cs}}</ref> Ice cream was also given out at these sessions, in response to the campaign of Pirates and Mayors.<ref>{{cite web|title=Nejdřív křížky, pak hozené vejce. Na autogramiádu Babiše v Průhonicích dorazili i odpůrci opatření|url=https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/volby-2021-andrej-babis-volebni-kampan-krizky-pruhonice_2108070932_zuj|website=Czech Radio|access-date=9 November 2021|language=cs}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|first=Daniela|last=Tauberová|title=Video: Babišovo setkání v Přerově narušil protest odpůrců|url=https://olomoucky.denik.cz/zpravy_region/babis-galerie-prerov-prodvolebni-stetkani-ano-protest-kpv-hucin-21-srpna.html|website=Olomoucký deník|date=21 August 2021|access-date=9 November 2021|language=cs}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Ideová nebo tradiční? Před volbami zuří zmrzlinová válka. Anketa|url=https://tn.nova.cz/zpravodajstvi/clanek/441459-ideova-nebo-tradicni-pred-volbami-zuri-zmrzlinova-valka-anketa|website=TV Nova|access-date=9 November 2021|language=cs}}</ref>

The party officially launched its campaign on 2 September 2021. Babiš promised higher pensions and measures against illegal immigration. He also attacked the opposition alliances, stating that they wanted to destroy the [[Visegrád Group]]. Babiš also talked about the defence of Czech national interests.<ref>{{cite web|title=Babiš v Ústí zahájil kampaň ANO. Slíbil zvýšit důchody a zaútočil na obě koalice|url=https://zpravy.aktualne.cz/domaci/politika/babis-v-usti-zahajil-kampan-ano-slibil-zvysit-duchody-a-zaut/r~b7146a360b6811ec8fa20cc47ab5f122/|website=Aktuálně.cz|date=2 September 2021|access-date=25 September 2021|language=cs}}</ref> In September 2021, ANO released an election advert for Czech television which attacked the Pirates over alleged support for immigration and links to [[Post–World War II anti-fascism|"antifa"]].<ref>{{cite web|last1=Tvrdoň|first1=Jan|title=Volební spoty: Babiš vsadil na negaci, Spolu spojuje a Piráti se STAN vyhánějí pijavice|url=https://denikn.cz/708521/volebni-spoty-babis-vsadil-na-negaci-spolu-spojuje-a-pirati-se-stan-vyhaneji-pijavice/|website=Deník N|date=22 September 2021|access-date=11 October 2021|language=cs}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Babišův spot útočící na Piráty zafungoval, mobilizuje voliče ANO, zjistil výzkum|url=https://zpravy.aktualne.cz/domaci/babisuv-spot-utocici-na-piraty-zafungoval-mobilizuje-volice/r~9cb37efe24ed11ec98380cc47ab5f122/|website=Aktuálně.cz|date=4 November 2021|access-date=11 October 2021|language=cs}}</ref> His campaign used the slogan "I will fight for you until my body falls apart!"<ref>{{cite web|title=Žádní ilegální migranti, průměrný důchod 20 tisíc. Babiš zahájil kampaň|url=https://www.novinky.cz/volby/do-poslanecke-snemovny/clanek/babis-zahajuje-kampan-slibuje-ze-se-bude-rvat-do-roztrhani-tela-40370865|website=Novinky.cz|access-date=12 October 2021|language=cs}}</ref> The launch of the campaign was impacted by the arrival of Babiš' son Andrej Babiš Jr., who was allegedly kidnapped on his father orders leading to the [[2018 Czech political crisis]]. Babiš Jr. confronted his father during the meeting and accused him of deceiving the nation. Babiš later stated that he would not wish any parent to go through such an experience.<ref>{{cite web|title=Babiš mladší se pustil do svého otce. Oblbuješ národ, vyčetl mu|url=https://www.e15.cz/volby/volby-do-snemovny/babis-mladsi-se-pustil-do-sveho-otce-se-svoji-sektou-ano-oblbujes-narod-vycetl-mu-1383259|website=E15.cz|access-date=9 November 2021|language=cs}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Volební kampaně už nectí žádná pravidla|url=https://www.e15.cz/nazory/robert-malecky-proste-to-vytrollime-do-roztrhani-zeme-volebni-kampane-uz-necti-zadna-pravidla-1383326|website=E15.cz|access-date=9 November 2021|language=cs}}</ref>

On 29 September 2021 Hungarian prime minister [[Viktor Orbán]] visited the Czech Republic and formally endorsed ANO at a rally in Ústí nad Labem.<ref>{{cite web|first=Milan|last=Jaroš|title=Orbán podpořil Babiše|url=https://www.respekt.cz/galerie/orban-podporil-babise|website=Týdeník Respekt|access-date=4 November 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Orbán podpoří Babiše v jeho volebním kraji, potká se i se Zemanem|url=https://echo24.cz/a/i6ZxK/orban-podpori-babise-v-jeho-volebnim-kraji-potka-se-i-se-zemanem|website=echo24.cz|date=28 September 2021|access-date=4 November 2021|language=cs}}</ref> Orbán praised Babiš, saying that Hungarians would be glad for a prime minister like Babiš. He also warned about immigration and the European Union during the rally, which was compared to a talkshow of two prime ministers.<ref>{{cite web|title=Maďaři by z premiéra, jako je Babiš, měli radost, řekl Orbán před příznivci hnutí ANO|url=https://zpravy.aktualne.cz/domaci/aplaus-i-straseni-migranty-babis-s-orbanem-se-zucastnili-tal/r~111aef72215411ec8fa20cc47ab5f122/|website=Aktuálně.cz|date=29 September 2021|access-date=4 November 2021|language=cs}}</ref>

Babiš was named in the [[Pandora Papers]] leak around a month later.<ref>{{cite web|first=Tom|last=McEnchroe|title=Pandora Papers: Czech PM Babiš used offshore companies to buy USD 22 million French estate|url=https://english.radio.cz/pandora-papers-czech-pm-babis-used-offshore-companies-buy-usd-22-million-french-8730234|website=Radio Prague International|date=4 October 2021|access-date=11 October 2021}}</ref> According to the leak, Babiš used offshore companies to buy French Mansion in 2009.<ref>{{cite web|title=Revealed: Czech PM used offshore companies to buy £13m French mansion|url=https://www.theguardian.com/news/2021/oct/03/revealed-czech-pm-used-offshore-companies-to-buy-13m-french-mansion|website=The Guardian|access-date=12 October 2021|date=3 October 2021}}</ref>

==== Communist Party of Bohemia and Moravia ====
[[File:Volby 10 - 2021 (7).jpg|thumb|KSČM billboard focusing on housing availability]]
The [[Communist Party of Bohemia and Moravia]] (KSČM) launched its campaign on 4 June 2021. Leader Vojtěch Filip said that a vote for KSČM meant certainty for the future. KSČM named its five priorities as help for children in need, better conditions for life and safety, the right to a dignified life and better environment, a higher minimum wage, and shorter working periods. Filip also stated his party's wish to leave [[North Atlantic Treaty|NATO]] and establish better relationships with China and Russia.<ref>{{cite web|title=KSČM zahájila volební kampaň. Chce odchod z NATO a lepší vztahy s Ruskem a Čínou|url=https://zpravy.aktualne.cz/domaci/kscm-zahajila-volebni-kampan/r~caca07bac53c11eba7d3ac1f6b220ee8/|website=Aktuálně.cz|date=4 June 2021|access-date=7 June 2021|language=cs}}</ref>

==== Czech Crown ====
The monarchist party [[Koruna Česká (party)|Koruna Česká]] launched its campaign on 9 August 2021. The party supported [[TOP 09]] in the [[2017 Czech parliamentary election|2017 elections]]. Chairman Radim Špaček described the program goals, to reform the Czech state from a republic to a parliamentary monarchy, to restore the historical lands of [[Bohemia]], [[Moravia]] and [[Silesia]], and revise the legal order. Deputy Chairman Petr Krátký cited a public opinion polling indicating that almost 10% of Czech citizens, especially younger voters, are in favor of a monarchy. The party's list also includes members of other small parties, such as the [[Conservative Party (Czech Republic)|Conservative Party]] and [[Morava 1918]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Koruna Česká zahájila kampaň, prosazuje návrat krále i zemské zřízení|url=https://www.ceskenoviny.cz/zpravy/koruna-ceska-zahajila-kampan-prosazuje-navrat-krale-i-zemske-zrizeni/2072871|website=České noviny|date=9 August 2021|access-date=10 August 2021|language=cs}}</ref>

==== Czech Pirate Party and Mayors and Independents ====
[[File:Volby 10 - 2021 (3).jpg|thumb|Pirates and Mayors campaign]]
The [[Czech Pirate Party]] and [[Mayors and Independents]] (STAN) formed the [[Liberalism|liberal]] electoral alliance [[Pirates and Mayors]] led by [[Ivan Bartoš]], presenting their cooperation agreement in December 2020. Priorities in the agreement included lower taxes, better availability of health care in the regions, protection of the climate, and transparent governance. The parties also agreed to support adoption of the [[euro]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Ladislav|last=Šustr|title=Piráti a STAN mají smlouvu: EET se celé nezruší, ochrana klimatu, přijetí eura|url=https://echo24.cz/a/S5xnJ/pirati-a-stan-maji-smlouvu-eet-se-cele-nezrusi-ochrana-klimatu-prijeti-eura|website=echo24.cz|date=27 December 2020|language=cs}}</ref> Bartoš said on 11 January that the alliance's priorities during the campaign would include reform of the debt collection system, digitalisation, environmental issues, and education.<ref>{{cite web|title=Pirát Bartoš slíbil zotavení Česka po krizi kvůli covidu a Babišově vládě|url=https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/pirati-celostatni-forum-koalice-stan.A210109_052642_domaci_kop|website=Mladá fronta Dnes|date=9 January 2021|access-date=14 January 2021|language=cs}}</ref>

Pirates and STAN launched their campaign on 18 May 2021, with the slogan "Let's give the country back its future" ({{langx|cs|Vraťme zemi budoucnost}}). Bartoš and Rakušan promised to regulate debt collection, raise taxes on commercial buildings, and begin preparations to adopt the euro.<ref>{{cite web|title=Vraťme zemi budoucnost, zahájili Piráti a STAN kampaň s Úřadem vlády za zády|url=https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/pirati-stan-zahajeni-volebni-kampane-program-koalice-logo.A210518_054741_domaci_kop|website=Mladá fronta Dnes|date=18 May 2021|access-date=20 May 2021|language=cs}}</ref> A major focus of the alliance's platform is digitalisation of the country.<ref>{{cite web|first=Michaela|last=Ryšavá|title=Piráti se starosty zahájili kampaň: slibují obří digitalizaci, plánují zrušení státní maturity|url=https://domaci.ihned.cz/c1-66926570-pirati-se-starosty-zahajili-kampan-slibuji-obri-digitalizaci-planuji-zruseni-statni-maturity|website=Hospodářské noviny|date=18 May 2021|access-date=20 May 2021|language=cs}}</ref> In response to the [[2021 South Moravia tornado]], Pirates and STAN interrupted their campaign.<ref>{{cite web|title=Tornádo a silné bouřky smetly i kampaň. Koalice Pirátů se STAN i Spolu boj voliče pozdrží|url=https://www.blesk.cz/clanek/volby-volby-do-snemovny/683272/tornado-a-silne-bourky-smetly-i-kampan-koalice-piratu-se-stan-i-spolu-boj-volice-pozdrzi.html|website=Blesk|access-date=11 October 2021|language=cs}}</ref>

[[File:Muzeum korupce 2021.jpg|thumb|left|Pirates and Mayors electoral bus.]]
At a press conference on 24 June 2021, Pirates and STAN launched an [[anti-corruption]] campaign, publishing a list of the 10 biggest corruption cases since 1989, primarily involving ODS. The campaign also listed the 10 biggest corruption cases involving the ruling ANO.<ref>{{cite web|title=Piráti a STAN představili 10 největších korupčních kauz. Šijí hlavně do ODS|url=https://www.novinky.cz/domaci/clanek/pirati-a-stan-predstavili-10-nejvetsich-korupcnich-kauz-siji-hlavne-do-ods-40364310|website=Novinky.cz|access-date=2 August 2021|language=cs}}</ref> In July 2021, the alliance released a poster featuring Jakub Michálek, its candidate for Minister of Justice, trying to catch a man in a suit with a lasso, accompanied with anti-corruption slogans. The campaign attracted significant media attention but was also criticised as amateurish and populist.<ref>{{cite web|title=Pirát Michálek s lasem jako lovec lidí. Strana po kritice plakát stáhla|url=https://echo24.cz/a/SAkZv/pirat-michalek-s-lasem-jako-lovec-lidi-strana-po-kritice-plakat-stahla|website=echo24.cz|access-date=2 August 2021|language=cs|date=6 July 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Michálek chytal s lasem korupčníka. Zavádějící, kají se Piráti a reklamu stáhli|url=https://www.novinky.cz/domaci/clanek/michalek-chytal-s-lasem-korupcnika-zavadejici-kaji-se-pirati-a-reklamu-stahli-40365436|website=Novinky.cz|access-date=2 August 2021|language=cs}}</ref>

The alliance relaunched its campaign in August 2021 as a reaction to declining opinion polls. The campaign began to focus more on STAN and its leader Vít Rakušan, though Bartoš remained the alliance's electoral leader and candidate for prime minister.<ref>{{cite web|title=Piráti po utahaném startu otáčejí kormidlo. Místo límečku přijde harmonika|url=https://www.seznamzpravy.cz/clanek/pirati-po-utahanem-startu-otaceji-kormidlo-misto-limecku-prijde-harmonika-170706|website=Seznam Zprávy|access-date=29 September 2021|language=cs}}</ref> The campaign also focused more on budgetary spending and education.<ref>{{cite web|title=Piráti a STAN zjednoduší kampaň. Klíčová témata budou zadlužování či vzdělání|url=https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/pirati-a-stan-zjednoduseni-kampane-zadluzovani-vzdelavani-ochrana-krajiny.A210805_133346_domaci_kop|website=Mladá fronta DNES|date=5 August 2021|access-date=29 September 2021|language=cs}}</ref>

The final phase of the campaign was launched on 9 September 2021. The alliance introduced an electoral bus in an attempt to replicate the success of the [[2017 Czech parliamentary election|2017 elections]]. Pirates and Mayors focused on criticism of the government for its handling of the COVID-19 pandemic and budget spending. Messages written on the bus also recalled various controversies of the government.<ref>{{cite web|title=Piráti recyklují kampaňovou atrakci. Za voliči vyrazil Švindlbus|url=https://www.seznamzpravy.cz/clanek/pirati-recykluji-kampanovou-atrakci-za-volici-vyrazi-svindlbus-174225|website=Seznam Zprávy|access-date=29 September 2021|language=cs}}</ref>
[[File:Kampaň ČSSD 2021.jpg|thumb|160px|ČSSD campaign]]

==== Czech Social Democratic Party ====
The [[Czech Social Democratic Party]] (ČSSD) launched its campaign on 29 March 2021 with the slogan "We know what to do after Covid." The campaign focused on the solution of the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the Czech Republic|COVID-19 crisis]], opposition to privatization of hospitals, support for ''[[Kurzarbeit]]'', and shorter working hours. The party also promised to increase taxes for banks and large companies.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jsme tradiční strana, která umí řešit krize, rozjela ČSSD kampaň|url=https://www.novinky.cz/domaci/clanek/cssd-predstavi-plan-po-koronaviru-cekame-na-tiskovou-konferenci-40355419|website=Novinky.cz|access-date=29 September 2021|language=cs}}</ref>

The final phase of campaign was launched on 22 August 2021. Party leader [[Jan Hamáček]] said that ČSSD was not dead, despite low opinion polling. Major topics of the party's campaign were higher salaries, pension reform, and just redistribution of COVID-19 expenditures. Slogans included "For a just Czech Republic" and "So that no one endangers your life security." ČSSD also expressed their intention to implement progressive taxation and a lower tax on groceries, rejected privatisation of health care, and promised more achievable housing.<ref>{{cite web|title=Nejsme mrtvá strana, bojujeme, burcoval Hamáček. Pokud neuspěje, odejde z vedení ČSSD|url=https://zpravy.aktualne.cz/domaci/nase-volebni-heslo-jsou-jistoty-oznamila-cssd-pokud-neuspeje/r~13f4276c034b11ec878fac1f6b220ee8/|website=Aktualne.cz|date=22 August 2021|access-date=29 September 2021|language=cs}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=ČSSD zahájila ostrou fázi kampaně, strana chce "spravedlivé Česko"|url=https://tn.nova.cz/zpravodajstvi/clanek/442539-cssd-zahajila-ostrou-fazi-kampane-strana-chce-spravedlive-cesko|website=TV Nova|access-date=29 September 2021|language=cs}}</ref>

ČSSD used Minister of Labour and Social Affairs [[Jana Maláčová]] prominently in its campaign. In September, Maláčová and [[Matěj Stropnický]], a candidate for the party in Prague, made a video called "Cool pair", in which they attacked opposition parties, accusing them of corruption and intending to privatize public companies.<ref>{{cite web|title=Šlo to za Husáka, půjde to i teď. Hustá dvojka představila recept na bydlení|url=https://www.idnes.cz/volby/husta-dvojka-malacova-stropnicky-cssd-volby.A210924_090402_domaci_kuka|website=Mladá fronta Dnes|date=24 September 2021|access-date=10 November 2021|language=cs}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Zloději přitvrzují, pustila se ČSSD do ODS kvůli plánu prodat poštu i dráhy|url=https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/zlodeji-utoci-predvolebni-video-cssd-husta-dvojka-malacova-stropnicky.A210910_112440_domaci_kop|website=Mladá fronta Dnes|date=10 September 2021|access-date=10 November 2021|language=cs}}</ref> Maláčová also campaigned at Metro stations giving out leaflets for the party.<ref>{{cite web|title=S letáky u metra zastavuje Maláčová propad ČSSD. Voliče loví se Špidlou i Petříčkem|url=https://zpravy.aktualne.cz/domaci/malacova-ceka-na-volice-rano-u-metra-nejvetsim-nebezpecim-je/r~48147024173211eca7d80cc47ab5f122/|website=Aktuálně.cz|date=20 September 2021|access-date=10 November 2021|language=cs}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Dříve volili ANO, teď ČSSD. Pražané jihnou pod pohledem Jany Maláčové|url=https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/volby-2021-jana-malacova-kampan-praha.A210916_103832_domaci_dape|website=Mladá fronta Dnes|date=16 September 2021|access-date=10 November 2021|language=cs}}</ref>

==== Free Bloc ====
[[File:Poslanec-lubomir-volny-brno (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|Lubomír Volný campaigning in Brno.]]
The [[Czech Sovereignty of Social Democracy|Free Bloc]] launched its campaign on 28 August 2021 with a meeting on [[Letná]]. Led by MP [[Lubomír Volný]], it focused mainly on opposition to COVID-19 restrictions. Other prominent figures in their campaign were [[Jana Bobošíková]] and [[Hana Lipovská]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Volný blok zahájil volební kampaň. Nesouhlasí s vládními omezeními kvůli covidu-19 a s očkováním|url=https://ct24.ceskatelevize.cz/domaci/3361986-volny-blok-zahajil-volebni-kampan-nesouhlasi-s-vladnimi-omezenimi-kvuli-covidu-19-a-s|website=ČT24|publisher=Czech Television|access-date=13 October 2021|language=cs}}</ref> The Free Bloc held electoral meetings at markets, with Volný travelling around the Czech Republic in a bus called "Volňásek".<ref>{{cite web|title=Volný nás zneužívá v předvolební kampani, stěžují si obchody|url=https://www.seznamzpravy.cz/clanek/volny-nas-zneuziva-v-predvolebni-kampani-stezuji-si-obchody-172507|website=Seznam Zprávy|access-date=23 October 2021|language=cs}}</ref> The campaign concluded with a meeting in Krupka on 6 October 2021.<ref name="Kampaň Volného bloku">{{cite web|first=Milan|last=Jaroš|title=Kampaň Volného bloku|url=https://www.respekt.cz/galerie/kampan-volneho-bloku|website=Týdeník Respekt|access-date=23 October 2021|language=cs}}</ref>
[[File:Volby 10 - 2021 (4).jpg|thumb|left|SPD billboard]]

==== Freedom and Direct Democracy ====
[[Freedom and Direct Democracy]] (SPD) launched its campaign on 15 July 2021 with a meeting on Letná.<ref>{{cite web|title=SPD zahájila kampaň. Chystá volební kamion "espéďák" i petici za zachování koruny|url=https://zpravy.aktualne.cz/domaci/politika/spd-zahajilo-kampan/r~77096cf6e56c11eba7d80cc47ab5f122/|website=Aktuálně.cz|date=15 July 2021|access-date=2 August 2021|language=cs}}</ref> SPD stated that the price for their participation in post-election coalition discussions would be a referendum law, and to hold a referendum on membership of the [[EU]] and [[NATO]].<ref>{{Cite news|title=Czech far right sets 'Czexit' referendum law as price for post-vote talks|url=https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/czech-far-right-sets-czexit-referendum-law-price-post-vote-talks-2021-09-22/|agency=Reuters|date=22 September 2021|access-date=10 October 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Czech far right sets 'Czexit' referendum law as price for post-vote talks|url=https://www.euractiv.com/section/elections/news/czech-far-right-sets-czexit-referendum-law-as-price-for-post-vote-talks/|website=[[Euractiv]]|date=23 September 2021|access-date=10 October 2021}}</ref> Other issues in the party's campaign included opposition to COVID-19 restrictions and mandatory vaccination. SPD used an election truck called "espéďák" to travel around the country, and attempted to attract potential voters to meetings by holding [[fair]]s with cheap food.<ref>{{cite web|title=SPD zahájila kampaň. Chystá volební kamion "espéďák" i petici za zachování koruny|url=https://zpravy.aktualne.cz/domaci/politika/spd-zahajilo-kampan/r~77096cf6e56c11eba7d80cc47ab5f122/|website=Aktuálně.cz|date=15 July 2021|access-date=23 October 2021|language=cs}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=SPD se v závěru kampaně zaměří na hesla proti migrantům, EU či Pirátům|url=https://www.ceskenoviny.cz/zpravy/spd-se-v-zaveru-kampane-zameri-na-hesla-proti-migrantum-eu-ci-piratum/2087068|website=České noviny|access-date=23 October 2021|language=cs}}</ref>

==== Green Party ====
The [[Green Party (Czech Republic)|Green Party]] launched its campaign on 29 June 2021, with the slogan "Lets Give Green to Women", focused on feminist issues and environmentalism. Besides green, the party used pink in its campaign.<ref>{{cite web|title=Zelení sázejí na růžovou. Politika podle nich nesmí připomínat pánský klub|url=https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/zeleni-start-volebni-kampane-sazka-na-ruzovou-vice-zen-v-politice.A210629_112650_domaci_kop|website=Mladá fronta Dnes|date=29 June 2021|access-date=3 July 2021|language=cs}}</ref> [[Magdalena Davis]] was announced as the party's electoral leader,<ref>{{cite web|title=Zelení zahájili předvolební kampaň|url=https://denikn.cz/minuta/656029/|website=Deník N|date=29 June 2021|access-date=2 November 2021|language=cs}}</ref> and a large number of their candidates were women. Davis described the predominance of men in politics as a medieval custom.<ref>{{cite web|title=Zelení jdou do voleb s programem reagujícím na změny klimatu a ženská témata|url=https://www.ceskenoviny.cz/zpravy/zeleni-jdou-do-voleb-s-programem-reagujicim-na-zmeny-klimatu-a-zenska-temata/2058253|website=České noviny|access-date=2 November 2021|language=cs}}</ref>

The final phase of the party's campaign was launched on 31 August 2021 in Brno, at the [[Brno astronomical clock]]. The Greens described it as a phallic, masculine symbol, and covered it with various images of female potential. Participants in the meeting held signs with slogans such as "We love modern schools" and "We love fathers on parental leave". Another key issue was the climate crisis, with the party proposing higher penalties for environmental crimes.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dejme ženám šanci. Zelení zahalili "penis" a začali kampaň|url=https://www.seznamzpravy.cz/clanek/dejme-zenam-sanci-zeleni-zahalili-penis-a-zacali-kampan-173569|website=Seznam Zprávy|access-date=2 November 2021|language=cs}}</ref>

==== People FOR ====
The [[People FOR]] political movement, led by political activist [[Mikuláš Minář]], was launched on 3 December 2020, and started gathering the 500,000 signatures required for participation in the elections. Minář said that the movement does not want to be another 5% party.<ref>{{cite web|title=Minář chce půl milionu podpisů, aby jeho nové hnutí šlo do voleb|url=https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/mikulas-minar-lide-pro-restart-politiky-pro-cr-milion-chvllek-pro-demokracii.A201203_102413_domaci_kop|website=Mladá fronta Dnes|date=3 December 2020|access-date=9 December 2020|language=cs}}</ref> On 24 March 2021, Minář announced the end of the movement due to low interest from voters, having collected only 39,251 signatures.<ref>{{cite web|title=Minářovo hnutí končí. Nemá podporu|url=https://www.novinky.cz/domaci/clanek/minarovo-hnuti-lide-pro-do-voleb-nepujde-nesehnalo-podpisy-40354921|website=Novinky.cz|date=24 March 2021|language=cs}}</ref>

==== Přísaha ====
[[File:U Dlabače Zahrádky (3).jpg|thumb|Přísaha poster saying: "People who want a just Czechia live here."]]
Robert Šlachta, the former Director of the police unit against organized crime, formed the anti-corruption party [[Přísaha]] before the election. He launched the campaign at a meeting on 28 January 2021. Šlachta stated that he did not believe it was the right time to adopt the euro and was opposed to migrant quotas.<ref>{{cite web|title=Šlachta zahájil kampaň hnutí Přísaha, je proti přijetí eura i kvótám u migrantů|url=https://zpravy.aktualne.cz/domaci/slachta-zahajil-kampan-sveho-hnuti-prisaha-je-proti-prijeti/r~48be8990619a11ebb115ac1f6b220ee8/|website=Aktuálně.cz|date=28 January 2021|access-date=20 May 2021|language=cs}}</ref>

The final phase of the campaign was launched on 25 August 2021. Přísaha introduced its regional leaders and program, under the slogan "Let's go to them!" The main campaign topic was fighting [[corruption]] and [[clientelism]]. Šlachta also stated that he wanted to make courts faster and fight for Czech identity, rejecting the euro and migration quotas. He also pledged to investigate all state contracts concluded under the state of emergency.<ref>{{cite web|title=Hnutí Přísaha zahájilo finální část kampaně, celostátním lídrem je Šlachta|url=https://ct24.ceskatelevize.cz/domaci/3360538-hnuti-prisaha-zahajilo-finalni-cast-kampane-celostatnim-lidrem-je-slachta|website=ČT24|publisher=Czech Television|access-date=11 October 2021|language=cs}}</ref> Šlachta stated that Přísaha had crowdfunded 13.8 million [[Czech koruna|CZK]] for the campaign, and calculated that the campaign would cost around 15 million CZK.<ref>{{cite web|title=Hnutí Přísaha dá do kampaně do 15 mil. Kč, zahájilo její finální část|url=https://www.ceskenoviny.cz/zpravy/hnuti-prisaha-da-do-kampane-do-15-mil-kc-zahajilo-jeji-finalni-cast/2078724|website=České noviny|access-date=11 October 2021|language=cs}}</ref>

The party hovered around the 5% electoral threshold in polling between May and the election.<ref>{{cite web|title=Sněmovní volby by v květnu vyhrálo koaliční uskupení Piráti/STAN, rostoucí trend zaznamenává Přísaha – Hnutí Roberta Šlachty – Volební preference – 5/2021|url=https://www.kurzy.cz/zpravy/593885-snemovni-volby-by-v-kvetnu-vyhralo-koalicni-uskupeni-pirati-stan-rostouci-trend-zaznamenava/|website=Kurzy.cz|access-date=12 October 2021|language=cs}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Nemáme na rozdávání koblih, i tak za námi lidé chodí, říká Šlachta|url=https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/hnuti-prisaha-kampan-penize-pruzkum.A210914_154137_domaci_lisv|website=Mladá fronta Dnes|date=14 September 2021|access-date=11 October 2021|language=cs}}</ref> In September 2021, Přísaha's support in opinion polls gradually declined, which was blamed on the launch of the ANO campaign.<ref>{{cite web|title=Proč se propadá Přísaha? Schází jí peníze a obírá ji Babiš, míní experti|url=https://www.seznamzpravy.cz/clanek/proc-se-propada-prisaha-schazi-ji-penize-a-obira-ji-babis-mini-experti-174535|website=Seznam Zprávy|access-date=12 October 2021|language=cs}}</ref> Šlachta stated before voting that he believed the party would reach his goal of surpassing the 5% threshold.<ref>{{cite web|title=Šlachta věří, že se Přísaha dostane do Sněmovny|url=https://www.msn.com/cs-cz/zpravy/dom%C3%A1c%C3%AD/%C5%A1lachta-v%C4%9B%C5%99%C3%AD-%C5%BEe-se-p%C5%99%C3%ADsaha-dostane-do-sn%C4%9Bmovny/ar-AAPiYf5|publisher=MSN|access-date=12 October 2021|language=cs}}</ref>

==== SPOLU ====
[[File:Kampaň SPOLU Praha 2021.jpg|thumb|SPOLU poster with leader Petr Fiala]]
Three [[centre-right]] parties, the [[Civic Democratic Party (Czech Republic)|Civic Democratic Party]], [[KDU-ČSL]], and [[TOP 09]], formed an electoral alliance called [[Spolu (Czech Republic)|SPOLU]]. Led by [[Petr Fiala]], the alliance launched its campaign on 9 December 2020, promising to reform tax, the social and pension system, and healthcare. Its proposals included a minimum pension, a simplification of social benefits, support for education, and better use of EU funds as well as a focus on climate change. It opposes leaving the EU and supports membership of NATO. [[TOP 09]] leader [[Markéta Pekarová Adamová]] described the alliance as a centre-right [[liberal conservative]] political force.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jdeme do toho SPOLU, zní heslo ODS, lidovců a TOP 09 pro příští volby|url=https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/ods-lidovci-top-09-kampan.A201209_120118_domaci_mkop|website=Mladá fronta Dnes|date=9 December 2020|access-date=9 December 2020|language=cs}}</ref>

[[File:Volby 10 - 2021 (10).jpg|thumb|left|Billboards of running parties]]
SPOLU launched its campaign on 19 May 2021 in Brno.<ref name="lidovky190521">{{cite web|title=Koalice Spolu zahájila v Brně předvolební kampaň, Feri představil program pro mladé. Zaskočilo je krupobití|url=https://www.lidovky.cz/domov/koalice-spolu-zahaji-v-brne-predvolebni-kampan-feri-predstavi-program-pro-mlade.A210519_071823_ln_domov_lijk|website=Lidové noviny|access-date=20 May 2021|language=cs}}</ref> The campaign's slogan was "We will bring the Czech Republic together." Fiala said that SPOLU wants an "economically capable and educated Czechia".<ref>{{cite web|title=Koalice Spolu zahájila v Brně kampaň pod heslem Dáme Česko dohromady|url=https://www.ceskenoviny.cz/zpravy/koalice-spolu-zahajila-v-brne-kampan-pod-heslem-dame-cesko-dohromady/2038820|website=České noviny|access-date=20 May 2021|language=cs}}</ref><ref name="lidovky190521"/> Spolu planned to use [[Dominik Feri]] as the face of an [[Instagram]] campaign targeting young voters entitled "I have a voice". In May 2021, Feri resigned from his political posts after being accused of sexual assault and rape by eight women, and the campaign was withdrawn.<ref>{{cite web|title='Feri nemá žádné politické dvojče.' Koalice Spolu řeší, jak nepřijít o mladé voliče|url=https://www.lidovky.cz/domov/jak-nahradit-tahouna-feriho-v-praze-mozna-nastoupi-cizinsky-o-mlade-bude-boj-s-piraty.A210530_120729_ln_domov_hetom|website=Lidové noviny|date=30 May 2021|access-date=7 June 2021|language=cs}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Koalice Spolu zahlazuje stopy po Ferim|url=https://www.novinky.cz/domaci/clanek/koalice-spolu-zahlazuje-stopy-po-ferim-40361700|website=Novinky.cz|access-date=7 June 2021|language=cs}}</ref> In response to the [[2021 South Moravia tornado]], Spolu interrupted its campaign in South Moravia and donated 1.5 million CZK to help people in the affected areas.<ref>{{cite web|title=Opozice ruší víkendové sněmy, poslanci i strany posílají na Moravu finanční pomoc|url=https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/spolu-pomoc-stan-snem-ruseni.A210625_100045_domaci_bur|website=Mladá fronta Dnes|date=25 June 2021|access-date=26 June 2021|language=cs}}</ref>

[[File:České Budějovice 09 - 2021 (8).jpg|thumb|left|Billboards used by SPOLU]]
From August, Spolu's campaign featured a bus, known as the "positive bus", to be used for its candidates' personal campaigns. Spolu also screened the film ''[[Women on the Run (film)|Women on the Run]]'' at its campaign meetings, and featured stand-up comedians including Petr Čtvrtníček in electoral adverts.<ref>{{cite web|title=Spolu vjelo do kampaně "pozitivním" autobusem|url=https://www.novinky.cz/domaci/clanek/spolu-vjelo-do-kampane-pozitivnim-autobusem-40366070|website=Novinky.cz|access-date=2 August 2021|language=cs}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Spolu do kampaně nasadí autobus, komedii Ženy v běhu a stand-up komiky|url=https://www.ceskenoviny.cz/zpravy/spolu-do-kampane-nasadi-autobus-komedii-zeny-v-behu-a-stand-up-komiky/2063305|website=České noviny|access-date=2 August 2021|language=cs}}</ref> Fiala became more active on social media and travelled around the Czech Republic as part of a personal campaign.<ref>{{cite web|title=Fiala premiér, Babiš prezident? Fantastický scénář, ale expert by ho nevylučoval|url=https://www.parlamentnilisty.cz/arena/politologove/Fiala-premier-Babis-prezident-Fantasticky-scenar-ale-expert-by-ho-nevylucoval-672369|website=Parlamentni listy|access-date=2 August 2021|language=cs}}</ref> In late August 2021, Spolu used billboards featuring the leaders of ANO, KSČM, and SPD with the word "Threat", which was often juxtaposed with a billboard featuring the leaders of Spolu with the words "Change you can trust."<ref>{{cite web|title=Zastavme Babiše s komunisty a Okamurou. Spolu jde do finále kampaně|url=https://www.seznamzpravy.cz/clanek/zastavme-babise-s-komunisty-a-okamurou-spolu-jde-do-finale-kampane-173134|website=Seznam Zprávy|access-date=11 October 2021|language=cs}}</ref> On 4 September 2021, SPOLU reacted to the launch of ANO's campaign by launching a parody meme generator inspired by the ANO campaign and its slogan "Until my body falls apart!".<ref>{{cite web|title="Budu zdražovat chleba. Až do roztrhání těla." Vyzkoušejte generátor Babišových slibů|url=https://echo24.cz/a/SjjFv/budu-zdrazovat-chleba-az-do-roztrhani-tela-vyzkousejte-generator-babisovych-slibu|website=echo24.cz|date=4 September 2021|access-date=12 October 2021|language=cs}}</ref> On 3 September 2021, SPOLU were endorsed by Austrian Chancellor [[Sebastian Kurz]], who sent a letter to Fiala wishing the alliance electoral success.<ref>{{cite web|title=Babišův kamarád Kurz fandí koalici Spolu. Přeji vám úspěch ve volbách, vzkázal Fialovi kancléř|url=https://cnn.iprima.cz/babisuv-kamarad-kurz-fandi-koalici-spolu-preji-vam-uspech-ve-volbach-vzkazal-fialovi-32822|website=[[CNN Prima News]]|access-date=4 November 2021|language=cs}}</ref>

SPOLU launched the final phase of their campaign on 20 September 2021 with a meeting inspired by the United States presidential campaigns.<ref>{{cite web|title=Teď jde o všechno, rozjelo Spolu horkou fázi kampaně|url=https://www.novinky.cz/domaci/clanek/spolu-zahajuje-horkou-fazi-kampane-40372603|website=Novinky.cz|access-date=25 September 2021|language=cs}}</ref> In a speech, Fiala criticised [[Andrej Babiš' Second Cabinet|Andrej Babiš' Cabinet]] for populism and warned against extremists. Fiala pledged that SPOLU would reduce the public debt without increasing taxes, guarantee the pro-Western orientation of the country, and digitalise public administration. He also said he wanted to solve the housing crisis. The meeting was held under the slogans "It is about everything now" and "Let's start change."<ref>{{cite web|title=Koalice Spolu zahájila horkou část kampaně. Garantuje západní orientaci Česka i konec zadlužování|url=https://ct24.ceskatelevize.cz/domaci/3373248-koalice-spolu-zahajila-horkou-cast-kampane-garantuje-zapadni-orientaci-ceska-i-konec|website=ČT24|publisher=Czech Television|access-date=25 September 2021|language=cs}}</ref> Around this time, prominent representatives of Spolu visited the regions to meet with citizens.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lídři Spolu vyrazili přesvědčovat své vlastní voliče|url=https://www.novinky.cz/volby/do-poslanecke-snemovny/clanek/lidri-spolu-vyrazili-presvedcovat-sve-vlastni-volice-40373296|website=Novinky.cz|access-date=29 September 2021|language=cs}}</ref>

Following the television debates, SPOLU used the line "The cost of Babiš" to attack the government over [[inflation]] and the rising prices of energy and groceries. The term was first used by Fiala during a debate on Prima CNN News, before becoming a part of the alliance's billboard campaign and spreading among ODS supporters.<ref>{{cite web|title=Babišova drahota. Fiala se konečně trefil do černého|url=https://www.info.cz/nazory/babisova-drahota-fiala-se-konecne-trefil-do-cerneho|website=info.cz|access-date=11 October 2021|language=cs}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title="Babišova drahota," pustil se Fiala do Schillerové. "Fialova sprostota," kontrovala|url=https://echo24.cz/a/iGRy5/babisova-drahota-pustil-se-fiala-do-schillerove-fialova-sprostota-kontrovala|website=echo24.cz|date=28 September 2021|access-date=11 October 2021|language=cs}}</ref> Fiala himself used the term repeatedly during debates.<ref>{{cite web|first=Luděk|last=Vainert|title="Babišova drahota" a další kolo zápasu v ekonomickém bahně|url=https://archiv.hn.cz/c1-66979710-bdquo-babisova-drahota-ldquo-a-dalsi-kolo-zapasu-v-ekonomickem-bahne|website=Hospodářské noviny|date=28 September 2021|access-date=23 October 2021|language=cs}}</ref>

In the last polls before the election, Spolu were polling second behind ANO. Commentators noted that the gap between ANO and Spolu was narrowing, but none predicted that Spolu would pull ahead.<ref>{{cite news|first1=Michal|last1=Janko|first2=Kateřina|last2=Perknerová|title=Volební model Deníku: ANO už neroste, koalice Spolu dotahuje Piráty|url=https://www.denik.cz/volby-ps-2021-preference/volebni-model-deniku-29092021.html|website=Deník|date=29 September 2021|access-date=11 October 2021|language=cs}}</ref><ref name="aktualne041021" />

====Tricolour–Svobodní–Soukromníci ====
[[File:Volby 10 - 2021 (8).jpg|thumb|Svobodní campaign]]
The [[Tricolour Citizens' Movement]], [[Svobodní]], and [[Freeholder Party of the Czech Republic]] formed an electoral alliance called Tricolour–Svobodní–Soukromníci (TSS), led by Tricolour leader [[Zuzana Majerová Zahradníková]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Trikolóra, Svobodní a Soukromníci půjdou do voleb společně. Chtějí hájit svobodu i českou korunu|url=https://www.irozhlas.cz/volby/trikolora-svobodni-soukromnici-koalice-volby_2103041610_pj|website=Czech Radio|access-date=13 October 2021|language=cs}}</ref> [[Václav Klaus Jr.]] was originally meant to be the electoral leader, but he quit politics soon after formation of the alliance.<ref>{{cite web|title=Klaus mladší končí v politice. Důvody jsou osobní|url=https://www.seznamzpravy.cz/clanek/klaus-mladsi-konci-v-politice-trikoloru-do-voleb-nepovede-148120|website=Seznam Zprávy|access-date=9 November 2021|language=cs}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Klaus mladší končí v politice. Může to souviset s plány jeho otce, říká politolog|url=https://zpravy.aktualne.cz/domaci/politika/koncim-v-politice-oznamil-vaclav-klaus-mladsi-predseda-triko/r~2c7602ba8bc811eba4560cc47ab5f122/|website=Aktuálně.cz|date=23 March 2021|access-date=9 November 2021|language=cs}}</ref>

TSS launched its campaign on 17 June 2021 with the slogan "We have a right to live". Their campaign focused on traditional values and opposition to COVID-19 restrictions. Majerová Zahradníková targeted right-wing Eurosceptic voters,<ref>{{cite web|title=Chtějí "vrátit normální svět". Trikolórová trojstrana zahájila kampaň|url=https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/trikolora-svobodni-soukromnici-volby-2021-volebni-program.A210617_123131_domaci_mkop|website=Mladá fronta Dnes|date=17 June 2021|access-date=13 October 2021|language=cs}}</ref> and also wanted to use former Czech President Václav Klaus during the campaign.<ref>{{cite web|title=Trikolora, Svobodní a Soukromníci chtějí překvapit Klausem|url=https://www.e15.cz/domaci/trikolora-svobodni-a-soukromnici-chystaji-prekvapeni-s-exprezidentem-klausem-1381441|website=E15.cz|access-date=23 October 2021|language=cs}}</ref> Majerová Zahradníková stated during the campaign that TSS rejected the lockdown, [[Green New Deal]], and grocery quotas. During September 2021 she also campaigned on the issue of rising prices.<ref>{{cite web|first=Ladislav|last=Šustr|title=I bez Klause jsme silní. Potravinové kvóty i Green deal naprosto odmítáme, říká šéfka Trikolóry|url=https://echo24.cz/a/S9CA4/i-bez-klause-jsme-silni-potravinove-kvoty-i-green-deal-naprosto-odmitame-rika-sefka-trikolory|website=echo24.cz|date=26 September 2021|access-date=9 November 2021|language=cs}}</ref> TSS aimed to win 7% of votes.<ref>{{cite web|first=Ondřej|last=Leinert|title=Byli na kraji rozchodu, teď si věří na sedm procent hlasů. Čím víc Fiala mluví, tím lépe pro nás, zní z Trikolóry|url=https://archiv.hn.cz/c1-66942110-byli-na-kraji-rozchodu-ted-si-veri-na-sedm-procent-hlasu-cim-vic-fiala-mluvi-tim-lepe-pro-nas-zni-z-trikolory|website=Hospodářské noviny|date=17 June 2021|access-date=9 November 2021|language=cs}}</ref>

During final phase of the campaign, TSS focused on [[Spolu (Czech Republic)|Spolu]] voters, distributing leaflets warning of a new [[Opposition agreement]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Kdo stojí v pozadí Trikolóry? Právník, co se radí s Hrdličkou|url=https://www.seznamzpravy.cz/clanek/kdo-stoji-v-pozadi-trikolory-pravnik-co-se-radi-s-hrdlickou-175067|website=Seznam Zprávy|access-date=9 November 2021|language=cs}}</ref> TSS also attacked Spolu for being too [[Green politics|Green]] and too [[Pro-Europeanism|pro-Europe]]. The party warned of "Covid totalitarianism" while attacking COVID-19 restrictions, rejecting a new lockdown, school closures, or "segregation of the non-vaccinated".<ref>{{cite web|title=Česko objevilo svou Margaret. Opuštěný prapor konzervativní pravice zvedla Majerová|url=https://www.parlamentnilisty.cz/arena/monitor/Cesko-objevilo-svou-Margaret-Opusteny-prapor-konzervativni-pravice-zvedla-Majerova-679454|website=Parlamentní listy|access-date=9 November 2021|language=cs}}</ref> TSS argued that it was the only "true authentic [[Right-wing politics|right]]" on the Czech political scene. A few hours prior to the election it was endorsed by former Czech president [[Václav Klaus]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Pravice jede. Formaci Trikolora Svobodní Soukromníci podpořil i prezident Klaus|url=https://www.parlamentnilisty.cz/arena/monitor/Pravice-jede-Formaci-Trikolora-Svobodni-Soukromnici-podporil-i-prezident-Klaus-679575|website=Parlamentní listy|access-date=9 November 2021|language=cs}}</ref>

[[File:Nevolte Urza.cz. – voting ballot, 2021 Czech legislative election, Liberec Region, Czechia.png|thumb|Urza.cz voting ballot for Liberec region.]]

====Urza.cz====
[[Urza.cz]] is an [[Anarchocapitalism|anarcho-capitalist]] party led by Martin Urza. Its campaign began gathering signatures in April 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|first=Jan|last=Kubita|title=Váš hlas chce i "Nevolte Urza.cz" s číslem patnáct. Tak je opravdu nevolte|url=https://archiv.hn.cz/c1-66972400-vas-hlas-chce-i-bdquo-nevolte-urza-cz-ldquo-s-cislem-patnact-tak-je-opravdu-nevolte|website=Hospodářské noviny|date=9 September 2021|access-date=8 November 2021|language=cs}}</ref> The party was registered in July 2021.<ref>{{cite web|title=Díky za Vaše podpisy!|url=https://dfens-cz.com/diky-za-vase-podpisy/|website=D-FENS|access-date=8 November 2021|language=cs}}</ref> Urza was campaigning to promote his beliefs, rather than attract votes.<ref>{{cite web|title=#35 Strana, kterou nemáte volit – Urza a Tereza Urzová|url=https://talk.youradio.cz/porady/co-je-slyset-a-co-neni-slyset/35-strana-kterou-nemate-volit-urza-a-tereza-urzova?seek=910|website=Youradio Talk|access-date=8 November 2021|language=cs}}</ref> The party promised that its MPs would resign if elected, as it did not believe that anyone should govern by force.<ref>{{cite web|title=Nehoda na paraglidingu! Českého politika sundal ze skály vrtulník|url=https://tn.nova.cz/zpravodajstvi/clanek/443090-nehoda-na-paraglidingu-ceskeho-politika-sundal-ze-skaly-vrtulnik|website=TV Nova|access-date=9 November 2021|language=cs}}</ref>

====We Will Open Czechia====
The Chcípl pes ({{langx|en|The Dog Croaked}}) initiative was created in opposition to COVID-19 restrictions. Its members decided to form a political party called "We Will Open Czechia". Its campaign was focused against COVID-19 restrictions and included various protests. The party also called on pub owners to open their businesses despite government orders.<ref>{{cite web|title=Nová hnutí na obzoru. Příznivci rychlého rozvolňování mají šanci, míní experti|url=https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/volby-poslanecka-snemovna-nove-strany-a-hnuti-boj-s-korupci-odpor-k-opatrenim.A210202_130229_domaci_chtl|website=Mladá fronta Dnes|date=7 February 2021|access-date=7 December 2021|language=cs}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Chcípl PES půjde do voleb a chystá protestní valentýnské pochody|url=https://www.idnes.cz/brno/zpravy/chcipl-pes-inciativa-politicke-hnuti-volby-protestni-pochody-valentyn.A210201_125423_brno-zpravy_klu|website=Mladá fronta Dnes|date=1 February 2021|access-date=7 December 2021|language=cs}}</ref> In April 2021 the party sent a mobile barber shop to Prague, where the public could get haircuts or buy beer. It was also used as a petition stand. The barber shop later moved from Prague to other locations around the country, finishing its journey in Ostrava.<ref>{{cite web|title=Hnutí Chcípl PES vyslalo z Prahy pojízdné kadeřnictví, lidem prodá i pivo|url=https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/hnuti-chcipl-pes-praha-pojizdne-kadernictvi-peticni-misto-praha-ostrava.A210421_140425_domaci_misl|website=Mladá fronta Dnes|date=21 April 2021|access-date=7 December 2021|language=cs}}</ref> In August 2021, the leaders of the party called for a new [[Defenestrations of Prague|Prague defenestration]], saying that "people should do anything required to overthrow criminal deputies."<ref>{{cite web|title=Hnutí Chcípl PES svolává defenestraci. Volání po násilí maskuje "humorem"|url=https://www.seznamzpravy.cz/clanek/hnuti-chcipl-pes-svolava-defenestraci-volani-po-nasili-maskuje-humorem-173231|website=Seznam Zprávy|access-date=7 December 2021}}</ref>

===Independent initiatives===
[[File:Kampan Milionu chvilek 2021.jpg|thumb|120px|[[Milion chvilek pro demokracii|Million Moments for Democracy]] campaign.]]

====Million Moments for Democracy====
[[Milion chvilek pro demokracii|Million Moments for Democracy]] led a campaign against Andrej Babiš and ANO, attempting to persuade voters to support the opposition alliances Spolu or Pirates and Mayors. Members of the movement talked to people in the streets and gave them leaflets in order to change their minds vote for one of major opposition alliances. The campaign also included a messenger app called "I vote change", which aimed to persuade people through gifs and various questions that they should vote for Spolu or Pirates and Mayors.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ideje počkají, až porazíme Babiše! Na kampani s Milionem chvilek|url=https://a2larm.cz/2021/09/ideje-pockaji-az-porazime-babise-na-kampani-s-milionem-chvilek/|website=A2larm|access-date=12 November 2021|language=cs}}</ref> Leader Benjamin Roll denied that the organisation's activities were a real election campaign, insisting that it was aiming to inform people.<ref>{{cite web|title=Děláme kampaň, ale není to kampaň.
