|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200626232312/https://polandin.com/45413891/new-government-receives-vote-of-confidence |url-status=live}} ===2020 presidential election=== {{further|2020 Polish presidential election}} The 2020 presidential election saw the reelection of incumbent [[President of Poland|president]] [[Andrzej Duda]], a former member of [[Law and Justice (Poland)|Law and Justice]].{{Cite web |last=jk/pap |date=2015-05-26 |title=Andrzej Duda zrzekł się członkostwa w PiS |url=https://www.newsweek.pl/polska/andrzej-duda-zrzekl-sie-czlonkostwa-w-pis/3cnddk4 |access-date=2024-10-12 |website=Newsweek |language=pl}} Originally planned in May, the elections were very affected by the then ongoing [[COVID-19 pandemic in Poland|COVID-19 pandemic]]. The government's proposal to maintain the election in May but only through postal votes launched a strong polemic, with the opposition denouncing the unequal campaigning capacities of the incumbent president compared to other candidates within the context of the lockdown and quarantine measures. The election was then postponed to late June following a compromise within the ruling coalition and the opposition's approval, partly thanks to the latter's control of the Senate.{{cite news |first=Jean-Baptiste |last=François |language=fr |title=En Pologne, la controverse du maintien de l'élection présidentielle |url=https://www.la-croix.com/Monde/Europe/En-Pologne-controverse-maintien-lelection-presidentielle-2020-03-27-1201086406 |work=la-croix.com |date=27 March 2020 |access-date=15 October 2023 |archive-date=11 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230411134646/https://www.la-croix.com/Monde/Europe/En-Pologne-controverse-maintien-lelection-presidentielle-2020-03-27-1201086406 |url-status=live}} Despite the pandemic, both rounds of voting saw higher turnouts, with Duda facing the [[Mayor of Warsaw|Mayor]] of [[Warsaw]], [[Rafał Trzaskowski]], a member of [[Civic Platform]]. Duda beat Trzaskowski, gathering 51% of the votes against the latter's 49%. These results were the most closely fought presidential elections since the return of democracy.{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/jul/13/incumbent-andrzej-duda-wins-polish-presidential-election-commission|title=Duda narrowly re-elected in Poland in boost for ruling nationalists|first=Shaun|last=Walker|work=The Guardian|date=13 July 2020|access-date=15 October 2023|archive-date=15 May 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230515112714/https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/jul/13/incumbent-andrzej-duda-wins-polish-presidential-election-commission|url-status=live}} Duda's victory allows PiS take advantage from his presidential veto in case of an opposition victory in the legislative elections, with the opposition needing a three-fifths majority, which currently amounts to 276 seats, to override one.{{cite web |language=pl |title=Konwencja PO. Budka proponuje Koalicję 276. "Tyle głosów potrzebnych do przejęcia władzy" |trans-title=PO Convention, Budka proposes a coalition for 276: "so many votes will be needed to get in power" |url=https://wiadomosci.gazeta.pl/wiadomosci/7,114884,26762104,konwencja-po-276-glosow-potrzebnych-do-przejecia-wladzy.html |website=gazetapl |date=6 February 2021 |access-date=15 October 2023 |archive-date=19 July 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230719173530/https://wiadomosci.gazeta.pl/wiadomosci/7,114884,26762104,konwencja-po-276-glosow-potrzebnych-do-przejecia-wladzy.html |url-status=live}} ===2023 Polish protests=== {{main|2023 Polish protests}} In May 2023, a law previously passed by the Sejm with the votes of the governing parties came into force, which provides for the establishment of a commission that can, without a court order, exclude politicians from public office for a period of ten years if, in their opinion, the politician was influenced by Russian interests. According to the law, the commission must examine whether this applies to Polish government politicians from 2007 (after PiS' defeat in the [[2007 Polish parliamentary election|2007 election]]). According to critics, the law could have been used as an instrument to prohibit selected opposition politicians from taking part in the parliamentary elections.{{cite web |url=https://www.tagesschau.de/ausland/europa/polen-gesetz-duda-100.html |title=Polen: Duda unterschreibt umstrittenes Gesetz zu Einflussnahme |work=tagesschau.de |date=29 May 2023 |language=de |access-date=30 May 2023 |archive-date=25 September 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230925150417/https://www.tagesschau.de/ausland/europa/polen-gesetz-duda-100.html |url-status=live}} Polish media therefore spoke of a "Lex Tusk" – a law aimed at the opposition leader and former prime minister [[Donald Tusk]] (2007–2014), who could have been excluded from the parliamentary elections in October 2023 as the potentially most promising opposition candidate.{{cite web |url=https://www.tagesschau.de/ausland/europa/polen-protest-pis-100.html |title=Massenprotest gegen polnische Regierung |language=de |access-date=4 June 2023 |archive-date=25 September 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230925200421/https://www.tagesschau.de/ausland/europa/polen-protest-pis-100.html |url-status=live}} PiS party circles repeatedly accused Tusk of making Poland dependent on energy imports from Russia during his term as head of government. The law drew strong criticism from the United States and the European Union, which expressed concern that the law jeopardized freedom and fairness in elections in Poland. President Duda then softened the law by introducing an amendment to the Sejm on 2 June 2023, which deprived the proposed commission of the previously planned right to impose a ban on political activity.{{cite web|url=https://p.dw.com/p/4S7X2|title=Polens Präsident Andrzej Duda gibt klein bei|work=Deutsche Welle|date=2 June 2023|access-date=5 June 2023|language=de|archive-date=18 October 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231018131550/https://www.dw.com/de/polens-pr%C3%A4sident-andrzej-duda-gibt-klein-bei/a-65807484|url-status=live}} On 4 June 2023 (the anniversary of the [[1989 Polish parliamentary election|first partially free elections in Poland in 1989]]) according to organizers, citing the city administration, half a million people took part in a "Great March for Democracy" organized by Tusk's Civic Platform in Warsaw to protest against the law.{{cite web |author=Viktoria Großmann |url=https://www.sueddeutsche.de/politik/polen-donald-tusk-pis-1.5900446 |title=500000 Menschen protestieren gegen Polens Regierung |date=4 June 2023 |language=de |access-date=4 June 2023 |archive-date=5 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230605081645/https://www.sueddeutsche.de/politik/polen-donald-tusk-pis-1.5900446 |url-status=live}} There were also protests with tens of thousands of participants in other cities, including Krakow, Szczecin and Częstochowa. The demonstration in Warsaw was joined by numerous civil rights movements, the Civic Platform spoke of the largest demonstration in Poland's history since the fall of communism in 1989. The protest march through the center of Warsaw was also led by the former Polish President [[Lech Wałęsa]].{{cite news |title="Europa, wir entschuldigen uns für die PiS": Zehntausende demonstrieren in system== {{Further|Elections in Poland}} The [[President of Poland]] set the election day to be Sunday, 15 October 2023.{{cite web |title=Prezydent: podjąłem decyzję o zarządzeniu wyborów do Sejmu i Senatu na dzień 15 października 2023 roku |url=https://www.pap.pl/aktualnosci/news%2C1606184%2Cprezydent-podjalem-decyzje-o-zarzadzeniu-wyborow-do-sejmu-i-senatu-na |access-date=10 August 2023 |website=Polska Agencja Prasowa SA |language=pl |archive-date=9 August 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230809071130/https://www.pap.pl/aktualnosci/news,1606184,prezydent-podjalem-decyzje-o-zarzadzeniu-wyborow-do-sejmu-i-senatu-na |url-status=live}} This date was consistent with requirements posed in Article 98 Section 2 of the [[Constitution of Poland|Polish Constitution]], whereby the election is to take place within the final 30 days of the [[9th term Sejm and 10th term Senate of Poland|current term of Parliament]] (ending 11 November 2023). The vote ought to be held on a non-working day – a Sunday or a [[Public holidays in Poland|public holiday]]. Other possible dates included 22 October, 29 October, [[All Saints' Day#Poland|1 November]], 5 November and [[National Independence Day (Poland)|11 November]].{{cite web |url=https://polityka.se.pl/wiadomosci/wybory-2023-cztery-mozliwe-terminy-wyjasniamy-kiedy-wybory-parlamentarne-2023-moga-sie-odbyc-02-02-aa-FJMa-bZd5-BzER.html |title=Znamy cztery daty, kiedy wybory 2023 mogą się odbyć. "Decyzję podejmie prezydent" |access-date=2 February 2023 |archive-date=4 February 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230204025140/https://polityka.se.pl/wiadomosci/wybory-2023-cztery-mozliwe-terminy-wyjasniamy-kiedy-wybory-parlamentarne-2023-moga-sie-odbyc-02-02-aa-FJMa-bZd5-BzER.html |url-status=live}} The process of election for the Sejm is through [[party-list proportional representation]] via the [[D'Hondt method]] in multi-seat [[constituency|constituencies]],{{cite web |url=http://electionresources.org/pl/ |title=Election Resources on the Internet: Elections to the Polish Sejm, Part I |publisher=electionresources.org |access-date=3 August 2014 |archive-date=24 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210224021334/http://electionresources.org/pl/ |url-status=live}} with a 5% threshold for single party (KW) and citizen committees (KWW) and an 8% threshold for coalitions (KKW). National minority committees, such as the [[German minority in Poland|German minority]], can apply to be exempt from the nationwide threshold, and in such case participate in the d'Hondt seat distribution within their constituency, in this specific case [[21st electoral district for the Sejm of the Republic of Poland|Opole]], regardless of the national share of votes.{{cite web |url=https://demagog.org.pl/wypowiedzi/jaki-jest-prog-wyborczy-dla-mniejszosci-narodowych/ |title=Jaki jest próg wyborczy dla mniejszości narodowych? |date=1 February 2023 |language=pl |website=demagog.org.pl |access-date=31 October 2023 |archive-date=31 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231031170035/https://demagog.org.pl/wypowiedzi/jaki-jest-prog-wyborczy-dla-mniejszosci-narodowych/ |url-status=live }} Contrary to popular belief, minority committees are not guaranteed seats in the parliament.{{cite web |last1=Ogiolda |first1=Krzysztof |title=Mniejszość niemiecka bez reprezentacji w Sejmie. Tego jeszcze nie było |url=https://opolska360.pl/mniejszosc-niemiecka-bez-reprezentacji-w-sejmie-tego-jeszcze-nie-bylo/ |website=Opolska360 |access-date=28 October 2023 |language=pl-PL |date=16 October 2023 |archive-date=28 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231028141523/https://opolska360.pl/mniejszosc-niemiecka-bez-reprezentacji-w-sejmie-tego-jeszcze-nie-bylo/ |url-status=live }} [[File:Senat RP okręgi blank map.svg|thumb|The 100 Senate constituencies]] [[Senate of Poland|Senators]] are elected by [[First-past-the-post voting|first-past-the-post method]] in [[List of constituencies for the Senate of the Republic of Poland|100 constituencies]]. Most of the opposition (Civic Coalition, New Left and Third Way) signed a so-called ''[[Senate Pact 2023|senate pact]]'', under which the parties agreed to enter one commonly accepted candidate in each district.{{cite web |date=28 February 2023 |title=Opozycja zawarła pakt senacki. Co to konkretnie oznacza? |url=https://www.polityka.pl/tygodnikpolityka/kraj/2203490,1,opozycja-zawarla-pakt-senacki-co-to-konkretnie-oznacza.read |access-date=10 August 2023 |website=www.polityka.pl |language=pl |archive-date=10 August 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230810230359/https://www.polityka.pl/tygodnikpolityka/kraj/2203490,1,opozycja-zawarla-pakt-senacki-co-to-konkretnie-oznacza.read |url-status=live}} This strategy has previously granted them 51 seats despite losing the Sejm.{{cite web |date=25 July 2023 |title=Pakt senacki. notcollapsed }} ==Opinion polls== {{main|Opinion polling for the 2023 Polish parliamentary election}} [[File:Polish Opinion Polling for the 2023 Election.png|900px|center]] == Results == === Sejm === {{See also|List of Sejm members (2023–2027)}} PiS remained the largest party in the Sejm, but with about 35% of the vote, lost its majority and was unable to form a government. The three main opposition groups, Civic Coalition, Third Way and New Left, took 54% of the votes, winning enough seats to allow them to take power.{{cite news |last1=Gera |first1=Vanessa |last2=Scislowska |first2=Monika |title=Polish election marks huge win for Donald Tusk as ruling conservatives lose to centrist coalition |url=https://apnews.com/article/poland-election-tusk-results-f687cf22fee9d395e92a08d2b6ab0f03 |work=AP News |date=17 October 2023 |access-date=17 October 2023 |archive-date=17 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231017140837/https://apnews.com/article/poland-election-tusk-results-f687cf22fee9d395e92a08d2b6ab0f03 |url-status=live}} According to the final vote count by the [[National Electoral Commission (Poland)|National Electoral Commission]], Law and Justice won 194 seats, the Civic Coalition 157, the Third Way 65, The Left 26, and the Confederation Liberty and Independence 18.{{cite news |last=Cienski |first=Jan |date=17 October 2023 |title=Poland election results: Opposition secures win, final count shows |url=https://www.politico.eu/article/poland-election-results-opposition-donald-tusk-wins-final-count-civic-platform-pis/ |work=Politico |location=Warsaw |access-date=17 October 2023 |archive-date=17 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231017075052/https://www.politico.eu/article/poland-election-results-opposition-donald-tusk-wins-final-count-civic-platform-pis/ |url-status=live}} Although the [[German Minority Electoral Committee]] did win 5.37% of the vote in the Opole region in this election, they came 6th instead of the expected 5th place, falling 5,372 votes short. The Opole Voivodeship represents a total of 12 Sejm seats, and as the 5th place was taken by the far-right [[Confederation Liberty and Independence]], the last 12th seat, which had previously been won by German Minority, went to them instead.{{cite web |author=Krzysztof Ogiolda |date=21 October 2023 |title=Mniejszość Niemiecka bez posła w Sejmie. Co poszło nie tak? |url=https://opolska360.pl/mniejszosc-niemiecka-bez-posla-w-sejmie-co-poszlo-nie-tak/ |website=opolska360.pl |language=pl |access-date=23 October 2023 |archive-date=24 October 2023 Committee failed to win any parliamentary seat for the first time in 32 years.{{cite web |date=17 October 2023 |title=German minority out of Polish parliament for the first time in 32 years Duda had a maximum of 30 days to call parliament into session, especially if he wanted the ruling Law and Justice party to try to build a government. Opposition parties had called on Duda to allow them to form a government as soon as possible and respect the will of the voters. Representatives of Duda stated that he would do so within the timeframe that the Constitution demands and allows.{{cite web | url=https://www.nwaonline.com/news/2023/oct/25/premier-hopeful-emerges-in-poland | title=Premier hopeful emerges in Poland | Northwest Arkansas Democrat-Gazette | date=25 October 2023 | access-date=26 October 2023 | archive-date=26 October 2023 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231026040039/https://www.nwaonline.com/news/2023/oct/25/premier-hopeful-emerges-in-poland/ | url-status=live }} On 6 November, Duda named Law and Justice's incumbent prime minister [[Mateusz Morawiecki]] as his prime ministerial nominee.{{Cite web |title=Prezydent Andrzej Duda wskazał, komu powierzy misję tworzenia rządu |url=https://wiadomosci.onet.pl/kraj/prezydent-andrzej-duda-wskazal-komu-powierzy-misje-tworzenia-rzadu/7rsnxbv |access-date=6 November 2023 |website=wiadomosci.onet.pl |date=6 November 2023 |language=pl |archive-date=6 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231106191818/https://wiadomosci.onet.pl/kraj/prezydent-andrzej-duda-wskazal-komu-powierzy-misje-tworzenia-rzadu/7rsnxbv |url-status=live }} This move was criticized by the opposition, as the United Right was 40 seats short of a majority and no other bloc had agreed to join them for coalition talks.{{Cite web |title=Prezydent wszystkich Polaków (którzy głosowali na PiS) |url=https://wiadomosci.onet.pl/opinie/prezydent-wszystkich-polakow-ktorzy-glosowali-na-pis/3web5ys |access-date=6 November 2023 |website=wiadomosci.onet.pl |date=6 November 2023 |language=pl |archive-date=6 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231106192156/https://wiadomosci.onet.pl/opinie/prezydent-wszystkich-polakow-ktorzy-glosowali-na-pis/3web5ys |url-status=live }} On 10 November, Civic Coalition, Poland 2050, Polish People's Party and New Left signed a coalition agreement with Tusk as their candidate for prime minister. The opposition parties wanted to sign the agreement before the Sejm's first sitting in order to show that they stood ready to govern. Morawiecki was required to secure the Sejm's [[Motion of no confidence|confidence]] within two weeks of being sworn in. Under the Constitution, if Morawiecki failed to do so, the Sejm would then designate its own candidate for prime minister, and Duda would be required to appoint that candidate before 11 December. Most commentators expected Morawiecki to come up short of the support needed to govern, as no other party willing to go into coalition with PiS would give it enough support to command the confidence of the Sejm.{{cite web | url = https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-67381267.amp | title = Poland's Tusk-led pro-EU opposition signs deal and waits to govern | work = [[BBC]] | author = Easton, Adam | date = 10 November 2023 | access-date = 10 November 2023 | archive-date = 10 November 2023 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20231110171740/https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-67381267.amp | url-status = live }} On 13 November, the newly elected Sejm held its first session. [[Szymon Hołownia]], leader of Poland 2050, was elected [[Marshal of the Sejm]], winning over the incumbent [[Elżbieta Witek]] of PiS.{{cite web | url = January 2022 in [[Portugal]] to elect members of the [[Assembly of the Republic (Portugal)|Assembly of the Republic]] to the [[15th Legislature of the Third Portuguese Republic]].{{cite web|date=2022-01-30|title=Live: Polls close in Portugal as Socialist Costa tries to keep power|url=https://www.euronews.com/2022/01/30/live-portugal-heads-to-the-polls-to-pick-new-government|access-date=2022-01-30|website=Euronews}} All 230 seats to the Assembly of the Republic were up for election.{{cite web|url=https://www.electionguide.org/elections/id/3823/|title=IFES Election Guide – Portuguese Republic|website=Election Guide|date=30 January 2022|access-date=2 February 2022}} The election was called after the government's state budget was rejected by Parliament in late October 2021. This election was also the third national election held in Portugal during the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] - as the country held a [[2021 Portuguese presidential election|presidential election]] (January) and [[2021 Portuguese local elections|local elections]] (September) in 2021{{cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-portugal-election-idUSKBN29S0BU|title=Portugal holds presidential election as COVID-19 cases spiral|publisher=Reuters|date=23 January 2021|access-date=2 February 2022}}{{cite news|url=https://www.publico.pt/2021/02/12/politica/noticia/rui-rio-quer-autarquicas-22-novembro-14-dezembro-1950431|title=Rui Rio quer autárquicas entre 22 de Novembro e 14 de Dezembro|work=Público|language=pt|date=12 February 2021|access-date=2 February 2022}} - and the fourth overall, with the [[2020 Azorean regional election|Azorean regional election]] in October 2020. The [[Socialist Party (Portugal)|Socialist Party]] (PS) of incumbent Prime Minister [[António Costa]] won an unexpected [[majority government]] in the Assembly of the Republic, the second in the party's history.{{Cite news|date=2022-01-31|title=Portugal election: Socialists win unexpected majority|work=BBC News|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/entertainment-arts-60194375|access-date=2022-01-31}} The PS received 41.4 percent of the vote and 120 seats, four seats above the minimum required for a majority.{{Cite news|date=2022-01-31 |title=Os eleitores deram ao PS a maioria absoluta que Costa pediu|language=pt|work=Público|url=https://www.publico.pt/2022/01/31/politica/noticia/eleitores-deram-ps-maioria-absoluta-costa-pediu-1993678|access-date=2022-01-31}} The PS won the most votes in all districts in mainland Portugal, only failing to win the [[Autonomous Region of Madeira]].{{Cite news|date=2022-01-31|title=Distrito a distrito, quem ganhou e quem perdeu|language=pt|work=Público|url=https://www.publico.pt/2022/01/31/politica/noticia/distrito-distrito-ganhou-perdeu-1993679|access-date=2022-01-31}} Political analysts considered the PS to have benefited from voters of the BE and the [[Unitary Democratic Coalition]] (CDU) casting their votes for the PS instead.{{Cite news|date=2022-01-31|title=Maioria absoluta de Costa foi à custa de 344.861 votos da esquerda. Veja como quebrou quatro dogmas eleitorais|language=pt|work=Expresso|url=https://expresso.pt/eleicoes-legislativas-2022/maioria-absoluta-de-costa-foi-a-custa-de-344-861-votos-da-esquerda-veja-como-quebrou-quatro-dogmas-eleitorais/|access-date=2022-01-31}} The [[Social Democratic Party (Portugal)|Social Democratic Party]] (PSD) remained stable but underperformed opinion polls that had predicted a close race with the PS. The PSD won 29.1 percent of the vote, a slightly higher share than in 2019, and received 77 seats, two seats less than the previous election. The PSD was surpassed by the PS in districts like [[Leiria District|Leiria]] and [[Viseu District|Viseu]], and lost [[Bragança District|Bragança]] by only 15 votes to the PS. In the aftermath of the election, party leader [[Rui Rio]] announced he would resign from the leadership.{{Cite news|last=Dinis|first=Rito|date=31 January 2022|title="Auf Wiedersehen": como o voto útil em Costa acabou com a "utilidade" de Rio|language=pt|work=[[Expresso (newspaper)|Expresso]]|url=https://expresso.pt/eleicoes-legislativas-2022/xeque-mate-como-o-voto-util-em-costa-acabou-com-a-utilidade-de-rio/|access-date=31 January 2022}} [[Chega]] finished in third place, winning 12 seats and 7.2 percent of the vote.{{Cite news|date=2022-01-31|title=André Ventura: "A partir de agora, vai haver a oposição que faltou ao PS"|language=pt|work=Jornal de Notícias|url=https://www.jn.pt/nacional/andre-ventura-a-partir-de-agora-vai-haver-a-oposicao-que-faltou-ao-ps-14543629.html|access-date=2022-01-31}} The [[Liberal Initiative (Portugal)|Liberal Initiative]] (IL) finished in fourth place, winning 8 seats and 4.9 percent of the vote.{{Cite news|date=2022-01-31|title=País acorda "hoje mais liberal" com oito deputados|language=pt|work=Jornal de Notícias|url=https://www.jn.pt/nacional/pais-acorda-hoje-mais-liberal-com-il-como-quarta-forca-politica-e-seis-deputados-14543666.html|access-date=2022-01-31}} Both parties experienced a surge of voters and made gains this election, though Chega received 100,000 fewer votes than its leader had received in the previous year's presidential election, an election in which turnout was lower.{{Cite web|date=2022-01-30|title=Portugal's ruling Socialists win re-election with outright majority|url=https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20220130-portugal-s-ruling-socialists-and-far-right-party-chega-eye-gains-in-snap-legislative-elections|access-date=2022-01-31|website=France 24}} The BE and CDU both suffered significant losses, being surpassed by the IL and Chega. Their rejection of the 2022 budget was considered to be a factor in losing votes and seats, along with [[tactical voting]]. The BE won 5 seats and 4.4 percent of the vote.{{Cite news|date=2022-01-31|title=De 19 para cinco. Foi assim que o BE saiu das legislativas|language=pt|work=Diário de Notícias|url=https://www.dn.pt/politica/de-19-para-cinco-foi-assim-que-o-be-saiu-das-legislativas-14543577.html|access-date=2022-01-31}} CDU won 6 seats and 4.3 percent of the vote, while losing seats in Évora and Santarém districts.{{Cite news|date=2022-01-31|title=CDU perde metade dos mandatos mas "aluta continua"|language=pt|work=Observador|url=https://observador.pt/programas/reportagem-observador/cdu-perde-metade-dos-mandatos-mas-a-luta-continua/|access-date=2022-01-31}} The [[Ecologist Party "The Greens"]] (PEV) lost all their seats for the first time.{{Cite journal |last=Lopes |first=Hugo Ferrinho |date=2022 |title=An unexpected Socialist majority: the 2022 Portuguese general elections |url=https://doi.org/10.1080/01402382.2022.2070983 |journal=West European Politics |volume=46 |issue=2 |pages=437–450 |doi=10.1080/01402382.2022.2070983 |s2cid=249301731 |issn=0140-2382|hdl=10451/55021 |hdl-access=free |url-access=subscription }}{{Cite news|date=2022-01-31|title="Verdes" perdem representação parlamentar|language=pt|work=Jornal de Negócios|url=https://www.jornaldenegocios.pt/economia/politica/eleicoes/eleicoes-legislativas-2022/detalhe/verdes-perdem-representacao-parlamentar|access-date=2022-01-31}} The [[CDS – People's Party]] (CDS–PP) lost all their seats for the first time, receiving 1.6 percent of the vote. Party leader [[Francisco Rodrigues dos Santos]] announced his resignation.{{Cite news|date=2022-01-31|title=Diogo Feio apela a reflexão sobre "tudo" no CDS. Incluindo a extinção|language=pt|work=Expresso|url=https://expresso.pt/eleicoes-legislativas-2022/diogo-feio-apela-a-reflexao-sobre-tudo-no-cds-incluindo-a-extincao/|access-date=2022-01-31}} [[People Animals Nature]] (PAN) suffered losses as well, winning 1 seat and 1.6 percent of the vote, 3 fewer seats than in the previous election.{{Cite news|date=2022-01-31|title=PAN elege no último minuto, mas sai destas eleições como um dos grandes derrotados|language=pt|work=Público|url=https://www.publico.pt/2022/01/31/politica/noticia/pan-elege-ultimo-minuto-sai-eleicoes-derrotados-1993663|access-date=2022-01-31}} [[LIVRE]] won 1 seat and received 1.3 percent of the vote, holding on to the single seat they won in the previous election, with party leader [[Rui Tavares]] being elected in Lisbon.{{Cite news|date=2022-01-31|title=O Livre faz oito anos, Rui Tavares vai ser deputado e Ana vai pintar o cabelo de verde. Cantam todos juntos por "uma terra sem amos"|language=pt|work=CNN Portugal|url=https://cnnportugal.iol.pt/eleicoes-legislativas/o-livre-faz-oito-anos-rui-tavares-vai-ser-deputado-e-ana-vai-pintar-o-cabelo-de-verde-cantam-todos-juntos-por-uma-terra-sem-amos/20300125/61f742b50cf2c7ea0f164c2f|access-date=2022-01-31}} The voter turnout grew, compared with the previous election, with 51.5 percent of registered voters casting a ballot, despite the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]].{{Cite web|date=2022-01-31|title=Portugal election: Key takeaways as Socialists cement power|url=https://www.euronews.com/2022/01/31/portugal-election-three-takeaways-as-socialists-cement-power|access-date=2022-01-31|website=Euronews}} After controversies and accusations because of the counting of overseas ballots, the [[Constitutional Court (Portugal)|Constitutional Court]] forced the repetition of the election in the Europe constituency, which elects two MPs.{{Cite news|date=2022-02-15|title=TC declara nula eleição no círculo da Europa que terá de ser repetida|language=pt|work=Sapo|url=https://www.sapo.pt/noticias/atualidade/tc-declara-nula-eleicao-no-circulo-da-europa-_620bf95fdaf0035eff8b0d9c|access-date=2022-02-15}} Therefore, the swearing in of the new Parliament and Government was delayed by a month and a half.{{Cite news|date=2022-02-15|title=Decisão do TC adia tomada de posse do novo Governo|language=pt|work=SIC Notícias|url=https://sicnoticias.pt/pais/decisao-do-tc-adia-tomada-de-posse-do-novo-governo/|access-date=2022-02-15}} The rerun of the election in the overseas constituency of Europe occurred, for in person voting, on 12 and 13 March 2022, and postal ballots were received until 23 March 2022.{{Cite news|date=2022-02-16|title=Votação dos emigrantes vai repetir-se a 12 e 13 março|language=pt|work=Expresso|url=https://expresso.pt/politica/votacao-dos-emigrantes-vai-repetir-se-a-12-e-13-marco/|access-date=2022-02-16}} The final, certified results of the election were published in the official journal, ''[[Diário da República]]'', on 26 March 2022.{{Cite web |title=Diário da República n.º 60-A/2022, Série I de 2022-03-26 |url=https://dre.pt/dre/detalhe/diario-republica/60-a-2022-181161523 |access-date=2022-03-26 |website=dre.pt}} ==Background== After winning the [[2019 Portuguese legislative election|October 2019 legislative election]] with 36% of the votes, more than 8 percentage points ahead of the PSD, the Socialists decided to not renew the 2015 "Geringonça" (''Contraption'') deal with the [[Left Bloc (Portugal)|Left Bloc]] and the [[Portuguese Communist Party|Communist Party]], opting to govern through a case-by-case approach between the left-wing and right-wing opposition parties.{{cite web|url=https://www.publico.pt/2019/10/11/politica/noticia/bloco-esquerda-lamenta-fim-geringonca-1889720|title=Catarina Martins lamenta fim da "geringonça"|publisher=Público|date=11 October 2019|access-date=31 January 2026|language=pt}} This option, aggravated by the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal|COVID-19 pandemic outbreak]], increased political instability.{{cite web|url=https://jornaleconomico.pt/noticias/fim-de-linha-de-compromisso-historico-geringonca-em-portugal-esta-desgastada-avisa-financial-times-679486|title="Fim de linha" de "compromisso histórico". Geringonça em Portugal está desgastada, avisa Financial Times|publisher=Jornal Económico|date=21 December 2020|access-date=31 January 2026|language=pt}} During Costa's second minority government term, the [[2020 Azorean regional election|PS lost the regional government of the Azores]],{{cite news|url=https://www.politico.eu/article/portugals-socialists-lose-absolute-majority-in-azores-regional-election/ |title=Portugal’s Socialists lose absolute majority in Azores regional election|publisher=[[Politico Europe]]|date=26 October 2020|access-date=4 July 2026}} and also suffered losses in the [[2021 Portuguese local elections|2021 local elections]], especially in [[2021 Lisbon local election|Lisbon]].{{cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/portugals-ruling-socialists-lead-local-elections-lose-lisbon-2021-09-27/|title=Portugal's ruling Socialists lead in local elections but lose Lisbon|publisher=Reuters|date=27 September 2021|access-date=2 February 2022}} ===Fall of the government=== {{See also|2019 Portuguese legislative election#Budget rejection and fall of the government}} On 27 October 2021, the budget proposed by the [[XXII Constitutional Government of Portugal|Socialist minority government]] was rejected by the Assembly of the Republic. The [[Left Bloc (Portugal)|Left Bloc]] (BE) and the [[Portuguese Communist Party]] (PCP), both of whom had previously supported the government, joined the centre-right to right-wing opposition parties and rejected the budget.[https://sicnoticias.pt/especiais/orcamento-de-estado/2021-10-27-Parlamento-chumba-Orcamento-do-Estado-7b00c570 "Parlamento chumba Orçamento do Estado "] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211027195701/https://sicnoticias.pt/especiais/orcamento-de-estado/2021-10-27-Parlamento-chumba-Orcamento-do-Estado-7b00c570 |date=27 October 2021 }}, ''[[SIC Notícias]]'', 27 October 2021. Retrieved 27 October 2021.{{cite news |last1= |first1= |last2= |first2= |date=28 October 2021 |url=https://www.rtp.pt/noticias/politica/orcamento-do-estado-para-2022-chumbado-pelo-parlamento-na-generalidade_e1358855|title=Orçamento do Estado para 2022 chumbado pelo Parlamento na generalidade |language=pt |newspaper=RTP|location=Lisbon |access-date=8 October 2022}} [[Prime Minister of Portugal|Prime Minister]] [[António Costa]] said to members of parliament, in his speech before the final vote, that he would not resign and would ask for a "stable, reinforced and lasting new majority" if an early election was called.{{cite news |last1= |first1= |last2= |first2= |date=27 October 2021 |url=https://www.rtp.pt/noticias/politica/oe2022-antonio-costa-pede-nova-maioria-estavel-reforcada-e-duradoura_v1359065|title=OE2022. António Costa pede nova maioria estável, reforçada e duradoura|language=pt |newspaper=RTP|location=Lisbon |access-date=28 December 2022}} File:Votação do Orçamento do Estado (Lusa - Aconteceu em 2021).png|2022 State Budget debate: [[Socialist Party (Portugal)|Socialist]] MPs voting in favour. File:Rejeição do Orçamento do Estado (Lusa - Aconteceu em 2021).png|2022 State Budget debate: Opposition MPs voting against. After the Parliamentary vote, [[President of Portugal|President]] [[Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa]] started hearing parties and convened the [[Council of State (Portugal)|Council of State]], announcing on 4 November 2021 the dissolution of Parliament and a snap election for 30 January 2022.{{Cite news|last1=Ferreira|first1=Ricardo Simões|last2=Henriques|first2=Susete|date=4 November 2021|title=Marcelo marca eleições para 30 de janeiro|language=pt|work=[[Diário de Notícias]]|url=https://www.dn.pt/politica/marcelo-fala-ao-pais-sobre-a-dissolucao-do-parlamento-14288921.html|access-date=31 January 2022}} ===Leadership changes and challenges=== ====Liberal Initiative==== Early in December 2019, the [[Liberal Initiative (Portugal)|Liberal Initiative]] (IL) elected a new leader after their previous leader, [[Carlos Guimarães Pinto]], stepped down. Their sole MP, [[João Cotrim de Figueiredo]], was elected as leader with 96 percent of the votes in the party's convention.[https://observador.pt/2019/12/08/joao-cotrim-figueiredo-eleito-presidente-da-iniciativa-liberal-com-96-dos-votos/ "João Cotrim Figueiredo eleito presidente da Iniciativa Liberal com 96% dos votos "], ''[[Observador]]'', 8 December 2019. Retrieved 5 January 2020. Three candidates were in the race: incumbent PSD leader [[Rui Rio]], former PSD parliamentary caucus leader [[Luís Montenegro]] and current Deputy Mayor of [[Cascais]] [[Miguel Pinto Luz]].[https://observador.pt/2020/01/02/tres-candidaturas-a-presidencia-do-psd-formalmente-aceites/ "Três candidaturas à presidência do PSD formalmente aceites "], ''[[Observador]]'', 2 January 2020. Retrieved 5 January 2020. Around 40,000 party members, out of almost 110,000, were registered to vote.[https://www.cmjornal.pt/politica/detalhe/pelo-menos-40-mil-militantes-podem-votar-nas-proximas-diretas-do-psd "Pelo menos 40 mil militantes podem votar nas próximas diretas do PSD"], ''[[Correio da Manhã (Portugal)|Correio da Manhã]]'', 23 December 2019. Retrieved 5 January 2020. In the first round, on 11 January, Rui Rio polled ahead with 49 percent of the votes against the 41.4 percent of Luís Montenegro and 9.6 percent of Miguel Pinto Luz, with both Rio and Montenegro qualifying for a second round.[https://tvi24.iol.pt/politica/rui-rui/eleicoes-psd-rio-obteve-49-02-dos-votos-na-1-volta-e-montenegro-41-42 "Eleições PSD: Rio obteve 49,02% dos votos na 1.ª volta e Montenegro 41,42%"], ''[[TVI24]]'', 15 January 2020. Retrieved 19 January 2020. A week later, on 18 January, Rui Rio was re-elected as PSD leader with 53.2 percent of the votes, against the 46.8 percent of Luís Montenegro.[https://www.publico.pt/2020/01/19/politica/noticia/rio-reeleito-mostrase-disposto-gerar-unidade-psd-1900888 "Rio é reeleito e mostra-se disposto a gerar unidade no PSD "], ''[[Público (Portugal)|Público]]'', 19 January 2020. Retrieved 19 January 2020. In both rounds, turnout of registered members achieved almost 80%. The election is then called by the [[president of Portugal]], not at the sole request of the [[prime minister of Portugal]], after listening to all of the parties represented in Parliament. The election date must be announced at least 60 days in advance if it is held as the legislature ends,{{cite web |url=http://app.parlamento.pt/site_antigo/ingles/cons_leg/Constitution_VII_revisao_definitive.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=7 October 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141022091934/http://app.parlamento.pt/site_antigo/ingles/cons_leg/Constitution_VII_revisao_definitive.pdf |archive-date=22 October 2014 }} but the election must be held within 55 days if it is called during an ongoing legislature (dissolution of parliament). The election day is the same in all multi-seat constituencies, and should fall on a Sunday or a national holiday. The next legislative election should have taken place no later than 8 October 2023;{{Cite web|url=http://www.cne.pt/sites/default/files/dl/legis_lear_2015_0.pdf|title=Electoral law to the Assembly of the Republic}} however, due to the rejection of the 2022 State Budget, during which the left-wing parties joined the right-wing parties and voted against the proposal, a snap election was called for 30 January 2022. === Electoral system === The [[Assembly of the Republic (Portugal)|Assembly of the Republic]] has 230 members elected to four-year terms. Governments do not require absolute majority support of the Assembly to hold office, as even if the number of opposers of government is larger than that of the supporters, the number of opposers still needs to be equal or greater than 116 (absolute majority) for both the Government's Programme to be rejected or for a [[motion of no confidence]] to be approved.{{cite web|url = http://www.en.parlamento.pt/Legislation/CRP/Constitution7th.pdf|title = Constitution of the Portuguese Republic|access-date = 29 October 2019|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160303222446/http://www.en.parlamento.pt/Legislation/CRP/Constitution7th.pdf|archive-date = 3 March 2016|url-status = dead}} The number of seats assigned to each constituency depends on the [[district magnitude]].{{cite web|url=http://www.tcd.ie/Political_Science/staff/michael_gallagher/ElSystems/Docts/effthresh.php |title=Effective threshold in electoral systems |publisher=Trinity College, Dublin |access-date=2015-10-21}} The use of the [[d'Hondt method]] makes for a higher effective threshold than certain other allocation methods such as the [[Largest remainder method|Hare quota]] or [[Sainte-Laguë method]], which are more generous to small parties.Gallaher, Michael (1992). Europe]] ||style="text-align:center;"| 2 |} ===Voting during COVID-19=== In January 2022, Portugal was experiencing rising infection rates as the [[SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant]] had a prevalence of 93% among variants in the country.[https://www.publico.pt/2022/01/18/ciencia/noticia/covid19-variante-omicron-prevalencia-93-detetada-linhagem-portugal-1992336 "COVID-19: variante Ómicron com prevalência de 93%. Foi detectada outra linhagem em Portugal "], ''Público'', 18 January 2022. Retrieved 19 January 2022. Because of this situation, thousands of voters were likely to be in isolation on 30 January, election day. To address this situation, the government asked for legal advice regarding the issue from the Portuguese Attorney-General's Office.[https://jornaleconomico.pt/noticias/legislativas-governo-pediu-parecer-a-pgr-para-saber-se-isolamento-impede-direito-de-voto-827318 "Legislativas: Governo pediu parecer à PGR para saber se isolamento impede direito de voto (com áudio)"], ''Jornal Económico'', 5 January 2022. Retrieved 19 January 2022. On 19 January, the government announced that isolated voters would be able to vote on election day and recommended that these voters cast a ballot during the last hour the polls were open, between 6pm and 7pm 30 January.[https://www.tsf.pt/portugal/sociedade/eleitores-vao-poder-sair-de-confinamento-para-votar-14506014.html "Eleitores em isolamento vão poder sair de casa para votar"], ''[[TSF (radio station)|TSF radio]]'', 19 January 2022. Retrieved 19 January 2022. ===Early voting=== Voters were also able to [[vote early]], which happened on 23 January, one week before election day. Voters had to register between 16 and 20 January 2022 in order to be eligible to cast an early ballot. By the 20 January deadline, 315,785 voters had requested to vote early, a number well below expectations.[https://www.rtp.pt/noticias/politica/voto-antecipado-inscricoes-muito-aquem-do-esperado-lamenta-governo_v1378683 "Voto antecipado. Inscrições "muito aquém do esperado", lamenta Governo"], ''RTP'', 21 January 2022. On 23 January, 285,848 voters (90.5 percent of voters that requested) cast an early ballot.[https://www.jornaldenegocios.pt/economia/politica/eleicoes/eleicoes-legislativas-2022/detalhe/mais-de-285-mil-votaram-antecipadamente-para-as-legislativas-90-dos-inscritos "Mais de 285 mil votaram antecipadamente para as legislativas. 90% dos inscritos"], ''Jornal de Negócios'', 26 January 2022. ==Parties== {{main list|Party lists for the 2022 Portuguese legislative election }} === Parliamentary factions === Before the election, the [[CDS – People's Party]] (CDS–PP) was open to the idea of a joint coalition with the Social Democrats (PSD),{{Cite web |title=Rodrigues dos Santos diz que coligação PSD/CDS é possibilidade “em cima da mesa” |url=https://www.publico.pt/2021/11/26/politica/noticia/rodrigues-santos-coligacao-psdcds-possibilidade-cima-mesa-1986604 |date=26 November 2021|access-date=26 July 2026 |website=www.publico.pt |language=pt-PT}} however, this proposal was rejected by the PSD,{{Cite web |title=Legislativas. Shortly after, the debates between Jerónimo de Sousa and other party leaders on those cable channels, were cancelled, thus reducing the number of debates to 32.{{Cite web|url=https://zap.aeiou.pt/jeronimo-sousa-catarina-martins-debates-453585|title = Jerónimo de Sousa e Catarina Martins não se vão enfrentar nos debates televisivos|author=ZAP Notícias|date=29 December 2021|access-date=29 December 2021}} On 11 January 2022, the PCP announced that Jerónimo de Sousa would undergo urgent vascular surgery on 12 January and would be out of the campaign trail for 10 days, thus being absent in the debates.{{Cite web|url=https://visao.sapo.pt/atualidade/politica/legislativas2022/2022-01-11-jeronimo-de-fora-da-campanha-por-dez-dias-devido-a-cirurgia/|title = Jerónimo de Sousa operado de urgência à carótida fica fora da campanha durante dez dias|author=Visão Notícias|date=11 January 2022|access-date=11 January 2022}} João Oliveira substituted him in the debate with [[Social Democratic Party (Portugal)|PSD]] leader [[Rui Rio]].{{Cite web|title=João Oliveira toma lugar de Jerónimo pela CDU nos restantes debates|url=https://www.dn.pt/politica/joao-oliveira-toma-lugar-de-jeronimo-pela-cdu-nos-restantes-debates-14484816.html|access-date=2022-01-12|website=www.dn.pt|language=pt-PT}} [[Observador|Rádio Observador]] organised two hour and a half debates with the head candidates for the Porto and Lisbon districts. leader, [[Francisco Rodrigues dos Santos]], reacting after his party was wiped out from Parliament for the first time in democracy. }} The [[Socialist Party (Portugal)|Socialist Party]] (PS) of incumbent prime minister [[António Costa]] won an unexpected [[absolute majority]] in the Assembly of the Republic, the second in the party's history. The PS received 41.5% of the vote and 118 seats, two above the minimum required for a majority. The PS won the most votes in all districts in mainland Portugal, only failing to win [[Madeira]]. Commentators considered the PS to have benefited from a transfer of the BE and the [[Unitary Democratic Coalition]] (CDU) voters to them. Costa said that his "absolute majority doesn't mean absolute power" and that he would still be open to forming a coalition, despite it no longer being a requirement to govern.{{cite news |last1=Jones |first1=Sam |title=Portugal general election: Socialists win surprise outright majority |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2022/jan/31/portugal-general-election-pm-antonio-costa-wins-surprise-outright-majority |access-date=31 January 2022 |work=The Guardian |date=31 January 2022}} He also promised reforms, saying: "The conditions have been created to carry out investments and reforms for Portugal to be more prosperous, fairer, more innovative."{{Cite web|date=2022-01-30|title=Portugal's ruling Socialists win re-election with outright majority|url=https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20220130-portugal-s-ruling-socialists-and-far-right-party-chega-eye-gains-in-snap-legislative-elections|access-date=2022-02-01|website=France 24}} The [[Social Democratic Party (Portugal)|Social Democratic Party]] (PSD) remained stable, underperforming opinion polls that had predicted a close race with the PS. The PSD won 29 percent of the vote, a slightly higher share than in 2019, and received 77 seats, two less than the previous election. The PSD was surpassed by the PS in their strongholds, such as [[Leiria District|Leiria]] and [[Viseu District|Viseu]], and lost [[Bragança District|Bragança]] by only 15 votes to the PS. In the aftermath of the election, party leader [[Rui Rio]] announced he would resign from the leadership.{{cite news |last1=Soares Botelho |first1=Pedro |title=Auf Wiedersehen? Perante a derrota, Rui Rio pergunta como pode ser ser útil ao partido |url=https://24.sapo.pt/atualidade/artigos/auf-wiedersehen-perante-a-derrota-rui-rio-pergunta-como-pode-ser-ser-util-ao-partido |access-date=31 January 2022 |work=SAPO |date=31 January 2022 |language=pt}} [[Chega]] finished in third place, winning 12 seats and 7.2 percent of the vote. The [[Liberal Initiative (Portugal)|Liberal Initiative]] (IL) finished in fourth place, winning 8 seats and 4.9 percent of the vote. Both parties experienced a surge of voters and made gains in this election. Chega leader [[André Ventura]] celebrated a "great night", though the party received more than 100,000 fewer votes than Ventura had received in the previous year's presidential election, an election in which turnout was lower. He blamed the PS majority on PSD leader Rio for not forming an alliance between the two right-wing parties and stated "From now on there won't be a soft opposition. We will assume the role of being the real opposition to the Socialists and restore dignity to this country." IL leader [[João Cotrim de Figueiredo]] also celebrated sufficient gains to form a parliamentary group, and said that his party would be a "firm opposition to socialism".{{cite news |title=João Cotrim de Figueiredo: "Grupo parlamentar da Iniciativa Liberal será oposição firme ao socialismo" |url=https://sicnoticias.pt/eleicoes-legislativas/joao-cotrim-de-figueiredo-grupo-parlamentar-da-iniciativa-liberal-sera-oposicao-firme-ao-socialismo/ |access-date=31 January 2022 |work=SIC Notícias |date=31 January 2022 |language=pt}} Both the BE and CDU suffered losses, being surpassed by the Chega and IL, with 5 seats and 4.4 percent of the vote; their rejection of the 2022 budget was considered to be a factor in losing votes and seats, as well as [[tactical voting]] to avoid a PSD plurality.{{cite web |last1=Gomes |first1=Celso |last2=Resende |first2=Guilherme |date=1 February 2022 |title=Portugal: How the Left Won and Lost a Parliamentary Election |url=https://europeelects.eu/2022/02/01/portugal-how-the-left-won-and-lost-a-parliamentary-election/ |access-date=6 February 2022 |website=Europe Elects |quote=The poor result of all these parties is not due to a rise of the right; its vote was hollowed out from the left, by PS. Given the snap election was called because the 2022 budget put forth by PS failed at the first hurdle, at first glance it appears electors penalised the parties who voted it down. However, it is likely that a subset of these vote transfers does not reflect a change of political orientation. Instead, they would be attributed to tactical voting for PS by electors startled by the possibility of a PSD plurality. Amongst the damage, this should be a silver lining for left-wing parties—it is the electorate they may easily claw back.}} The CDU won 6 seats and 4.3 percent of the vote, while losing seats in [[Évora District|Évora]] and [[Santarém District|Santarém]] districts. The [[Ecologist Party "The Greens"]] (PEV) lost all their seats for the first time. [[Catarina Martins]] of the BE blamed the PS for having created a "false crisis" that she believed had resulted in a polarised election that penalised parties to the left of the PS. She also spoke out against the gains for Chega.{{cite news |title=Catarina Martins fala em "crise artificial" criada pelo PS e promete combater "deputados racistas" |url=https://www.rtp.pt/noticias/politica/catarina-martins-fala-em-crise-artificial-criada-pelo-ps-e-promete-combater-deputados-racistas_v1380853 |access-date=31 January 2022 |work=Rádio e Televisão de Portugal |date=30 January 2022 |language=pt}} [[Portuguese Communist Party]] leader [[Jerónimo de Sousa]] made a similar statement about the PS.{{cite news |title=Jerónimo culpa "extrema" bipolarização mas diz que quem "perde a coragem, perde tudo" |url=https://www.sapo.pt/noticias/atualidade/jeronimo-culpa-extrema-bipolarizacao-mas-diz-_61f726decbff2f5f4cc70e9f |access-date=31 January 2022 |work=SAPO |date=30 January 2022 |language=pt}} The [[CDS – People's Party]] (CDS–PP) lost all their seats for the first time, receiving 1.6 percent of the vote. Party leader [[Francisco Rodrigues dos Santos]] announced his resignation.{{Cite news|title=CDS fica fora do Parlamento e líder demite-se|language=pt|work=Público|url=https://www.publico.pt/2022/01/31/politica/noticia/cds-fica-parlamento-lider-demitese-1993672|date=31 January 2022|first=Sofia|last=Rodrigues}} Also due to tactical voting, [[People Animals Nature]] (PAN) suffered losses, winning 1 seat and 1.6 percent of the vote, 3 fewer seats than in the previous election. PAN leader [[Inês Sousa Real]] spoke of sadness after this result, and said that an absolute majority would be bad for democracy.{{cite news |last1=Peres Pinto |first1=Sónia |title=Inês Sousa Real passa a única deputada do PAN |url=https://sol.sapo.pt/artigo/760853/in-s-sousa-real-passa-a-nica-deputada-do-pan- |access-date=31 January 2022 |work=Jornal SOL |date=31 January 2022 |language=pt}} [[LIVRE]] won 1 seat and received 1.3 percent of the vote, holding on to the single seat they won in the previous election, with party leader [[Rui Tavares]] being elected in Lisbon. Tavares pledged to get Costa to work with other left-wing parties.{{cite news |last1=Pincho |first1=João Pedro |title=A festa de anos do Livre teve a eleição de Rui Tavares como brinde |url=https://www.publico.pt/2022/01/31/politica/noticia/festa-anos-livre-eleicao-rui-tavares-brinde-1993662 |access-date=31 January 2022 |work=Público |date=31 January 2022 |language=pt}} The voter turnout was the highest since the [[2015 Portuguese legislative election]], with 51.5 percent of registered voters casting a ballot. ===Overseas ballots controversy=== In this election, 257,791 ballots from overseas were received, but, during the process of counting the ballots, a controversy started.{{cite news |last1=Dinis |first1=David |title=Foram invalidados 157 mil votos na emigração. PS não vai para o TC, mas quer mudar a lei eleitoral|url=https://expresso.pt/eleicoes-legislativas-2022/foram-invalidados-157-mil-votos-na-emigracao-ps-nao-vai-para-o-tc-mas-quer-mudar-a-lei-eleitoral/ |access-date=15 February 2022 |work=Expresso |date=10 February 2022 |language=pt}} The Social Democratic Party (PSD) filed a complaint in order for the ballots with no [[Identity document|ID card]] copy to be put aside.{{Cite news |date=8 February 2022 |title=PSD contesta contagem de votos dos emigrantes, PS diz que decisão foi de todos |language=pt |work=Público |url=https://www.publico.pt/2022/02/08/politica/noticia/psd-contesta-contagem-votos-emigrantes-ps-decisao-1994749 |access-date=15 February 2022}} The Portuguese electoral law requires that for a ballot received by mail to be valid, it needs to be accompanied with an ID card copy of the voter (in order to confirm the identity of the voter, as the equivalent of presenting the ID to the poll workers when voting in person).{{cite news |last1=Carvalho |first1=Joana Mourão |title=Votos emigrantes. Constitucionalistas falam em "ato negligente" e de "fuga a responsabilidades"|url=https://ionline.sapo.pt/artigo/762386/votos-emigrantes-constitucionalistas-falam-em-ato-negligente-e-de-fuga-a-responsabilidades?seccao=Portugal_i|access-date=15 February 2022 |work=Jornal i |date=15 February 2022 |language=pt}} The Socialist Party (PS) protested against the PSD complaint, reminding the PSD that all parties had had an informal meeting in which it had been decided that all ballots, with or without an ID card copy, would be counted and declared valid. The PSD had confirmed their position in that meeting, but announced that they had changed their mind after they were given a document stating that any such actions would be illegal.{{cite news |last1=Céu |first1=Beatriz |title=Acusações de fraude, "reuniões de amigos" em vez de leis: 5 esclarecimentos sobre a anulação dos votos dos emigrantes|url=https://cnnportugal.iol.pt/politica/novogoverno/confuso-com-a-polemica-dos-votos-dos-emigrantes-um-guia-sobre-o-que-esta-em-causa/20711231/620420790cf21a10a41e62c1|access-date=15 February 2022|work=CNN Portugal |date=9 February 2022 |language=pt}} Nonetheless, the PSD and the Electoral Commission (CNE) warned and advised counting staffs to separate the ballots. Constitucional manda repetir votação onde se verificaram irregularidades|url=https://www.tsf.pt/portugal/politica/circulo-da-europa-constitucional-manda-repetir-votacao-onde-se-verificaram-irregularidades-14592104.html|access-date=2022-02-17|website=TSF Rádio Notícias|language=pt-PT}} Of the 5 complaints filed, however, the court accepted only [[Volt Portugal]]'s complaint.{{Cite web|date=2022-02-16|title=Visão {{!}} Quem é Mateus Carvalho, o jovem que "convenceu" o Tribunal Constitucional a repetir as eleições no círculo da Europa|url=https://visao.sapo.pt/atualidade/2022-02-16-quem-e-mateus-carvalho-o-jovem-que-evitou-a-anulacao-dos-votos-da-europa-e-convenceu-o-tribunal-constitucional-a-repetir-as-eleicoes/|access-date=2022-02-17|website=Visão|language=pt-PT}} On 15 February, the Court annulled the election in the Europe constituency and demanded a repetition of the vote.{{cite news |last1=Dinis |first1=Rita |title=Tribunal Constitucional manda repetir voto dos emigrantes na Europa|url=https://expresso.pt/politica/tc-manda-repetir-voto-dos-emigrantes-na-europa/ |access-date=15 February 2022 |work=Expresso |date=15 February 2022 |language=pt}} The National Election Committee determined that for the rerun of the parliamentary elections in the constituency of Europe on March 12 and 13 can be voted in person, just as until March 23 by absentee ballot.{{Cite web|title=CNE marca repetição das legislativas no círculo da Europa para 12 e 13 de março|url=https://cnnportugal.iol.pt/eleicoes-legislativas/emigrantes/cne-marca-repeticao-das-legislativas-no-circulo-da-europa-para-12-e-13-de-marco/20301124/620d56f10cf2cc58e7e35f87|access-date=2022-02-17|website=CNN Portugal|language=pt}} 109,350 ballots were received until 23 March, and of those, 30% (32,777) were declared null as they were not accompanied with an ID card copy. General elections were held in [[Sweden]] on 11 September 2022 to elect the 349 members of the [[Riksdag]] who in turn elected the [[Prime Minister of Sweden]]. Under the constitution, regional and municipal elections were also held on the same day. The preliminary results presented on 15 September showed the government parties lost their majority, which were confirmed by the final results published on 17 September. After a month of negotiations following the elections that led to the [[Tidö Agreement]] among the right-wing bloc, [[Moderate Party]] (M) leader [[Ulf Kristersson]] was elected prime minister on 17 October. The [[Kristersson cabinet]] is a [[minority government]] of the Moderates, [[Christian Democrats (Sweden)|Christian Democrats]] (KD) and [[Liberals (Sweden)|Liberals]] (L) that relies on [[confidence and supply]] from the [[Sweden Democrats]] (SD).

The campaign period was met with issues regarding [[Sweden–NATO relations|Sweden's accession to NATO]] due to the [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]], as well as [[Crime in Sweden|crime]], [[Energy in Sweden|energy]], the [[Economy of Sweden|economy]], and [[Immigration to Sweden|immigration]]. Parliamentary parties campaigned through July and August, while in late August SD surpassed M in opinion polls. [[Exit poll]]s showed that S and its confidence-and-supply parties [[Left Party (Sweden)|Left Party]], [[Centre Party (Sweden)|Centre Party]] and [[Green Party (Sweden)|Green Party]] had a narrow lead against the right-leaning bloc (SD, M, KD, L). During the counting of the preliminary results and later on, Sweden's [[Election Authority (Sweden)|Election Authority]] said that the right overtook the left (S, V, C, MP) by three seats. Andersson conceded the election three days later, and resigned the day after that.

The election saw massive swings between the two blocs in different regions.<!-- See<ref>{{cite web|url=https://valresultat.svt.se/2022/index.html|title=Valresultat 2022 – för riksdagsvalet, region- och kommunalval|trans-title=Election Results 2022 – for Riksdag, Regional and Municipal elections|publisher=[[SVT Nyheter]]|language=sv|date=15 September 2022|access-date=17 September 2022}}</ref> quoted in the 'Results' section for source to all statements. --> The left-leaning bloc won the most votes in large cities and several university towns with unprecedented massive margins. [[Stockholm Municipality|Stockholm]] city went red by 18 points, [[Gothenburg Municipality|Gothenburg]] by 11 points and the left also flipped two suburban municipalities in [[Stockholm County]]. Meanwhile, the right managed to overturn dozens of municipalities that had historically been dominated by S, especially in the central interior [[Bergslagen]] region. In this historically industrial area, the county of [[Dalarna County|Dalarna]] was won by the right-leaning coalition for the first time in history, while the left held on by just 373 votes in [[Värmland County|Värmland]]. Likewise, some municipalities that the outright leftist parties (S, V, MP) had won with an overall majority of 50 points in the [[1994 Swedish general election]], flipped to the right.<!-- See [[Results of the 1994 Swedish general election]] and<ref>{{cite web|url=https://share.scb.se/ov9993/data/historisk%20statistik/SOS%201911-%2FValstatistiken%2FAllm%C3%A4nna%20valen%20(SOS)%201970-1998%2FValstatistik-Allmanna-valen-1994-Del-1-Riksdagsvalet.pdf|title=Allmänna valen 1994. Del 1, Riksdagsvalet den 18 september 1994|trans-title=General election on the 18 September 1994|publisher=[[Statistiska Centralbyrån|SCB]]|language=sv|date=18 September 1994|access-date=17 September 2022}}</ref>--> In middle Sweden, the right won [[Eskilstuna Municipality|Eskilstuna]], [[Gävle Municipality|Gävle]], [[Norrköping Municipality|Norrköping]], [[Södertälje Municipality|Södertälje]] and [[Västerås Municipality|Västerås]]. All five had been historical leftist strongholds.

Major gains in minority were also made by the right-leaning bloc in [[Northern Sweden]], leading the vote in eight municipalities compared to none four years prior. In the lower east, the historically leftist swing counties [[Kalmar County|Kalmar]], [[Södermanland County|Södermanland]], [[Västmanland County|Västmanland]] and [[Östergötland County|Östergötland]] all went to the right to seal the parliamentary majority. S won 30% of the popular vote, with a net increase in spite of the election loss. SD became the second-largest party with above 20% of the popular vote, surpassing M at 19%. The blocs were separated by a thin margin of about half a percentage point. The parties aligned with the outgoing government did somewhat better in the regional and municipal elections.<!-- Government parties got 50.1% to 45.9% and 49.1% to 45.9% compared to the opposition, respectively. See https://www.aftonbladet.se/valresultat2022/ -->

=== Löfven's government ===
{{see also|Löfven I Cabinet|Löfven II Cabinet|Löfven III Cabinet}}
{{further|2021 Swedish government crisis|COVID-19 pandemic in Sweden}}
The first confirmed case of [[COVID-19]] in Sweden became known on 31 January 2020. The government later ordered 100,000 people a week to be tested to curb the spread of the disease; with insufficient healthcare resources and unclear responsibilities, the goal was not met. In contrast to the [[World Health Organization]], the government did not recommend the use of [[face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Ludvigsson |first=Jonas F. |date=23 November 2020 |title=Så har Sveriges coronastrategi framstått under åtta månader |url=https://lakartidningen.se/klinik-och-vetenskap-1/kommentar/2020/11/sa-har-sveriges-coronastrategi-framstatt-under-atta-manader/ |access-date=31 August 2022 |website=Läkartidningen |language=sv-SE |archive-date=9 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220909230651/https://lakartidningen.se/klinik-och-vetenskap-1/kommentar/2020/11/sa-har-sveriges-coronastrategi-framstatt-under-atta-manader/ |url-status=live}}</ref> During the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], the government did not impose [[national lockdowns]] but rather limits on the number of people that were allowed to meet at public places.<ref>{{cite web |date=7 September 2021 |title=Fler restriktioner tas bort från och med den 29 september |url=https://www.regeringen.se/artiklar/2021/09/fler-restriktioner-tas-bort-fran-och-med-den-29-september/ |access-date=31 August 2022 |website=Regeringskansliet |language=sv |archive-date=9 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220909230657/https://www.regeringen.se/artiklar/2021/09/fler-restriktioner-tas-bort-fran-och-med-den-29-september/ |url-status=live}}</ref> In December 2019, Kristersson held a meeting with SD leader [[Jimmie Åkesson]], and said that he would cooperate with SD in the [[Riksdag]]. According to Ann-Cathrine Jungar of [[Södertörn University]], this put Sweden in line with several other European countries in which [[centre-right]] and [[Radical right (Europe)|radical-right]] parties cooperate.<ref>{{cite news |last=Milne |first=Richard |title=Mainstream Swedish party open to working with once-spurned nationalists |url=https://www.ft.com/content/1e692a28-1764-11ea-9ee4-11f260415385 |access-date=30 June 2021 |work=Financial Times |date=5 December 2019}}</ref> In August 2020, the right-wing opposition criticised the Löfven government for a perceived failure to deal with rising [[Crime in Sweden|crime]] including [[Gun violence in Sweden|gun violence]], which Kristersson called a "second pandemic".<ref>{{cite news |last=Milne |first=Richard |title=Sweden's right seizes on crime to warn of 'second pandemic' |url=https://www.ft.com/content/67b04d32-da13-440e-ad68-099b533470e1 |access-date=30 June 2021 |work=Financial Times |date=30 August 2020}}</ref>

== Electoral system ==
{{see also|Elections in Sweden}}
The [[Riksdag]] is made up of 349 seats, and all are elected through [[open list]], [[proportional representation]] on multi-member party lists.<ref>{{cite web |title=Sweden Riksdagen (Parliament) |url=http://archive.ipu.org/parline-e/reports/2303.htm |access-date=31 August 2022 |website=Parline |date=1 November 2017|archive-date=28 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211228013500/http://archive.ipu.org/parline-e/reports/2303.htm |url-status=live}}</ref>

Of the 349 seats, 310 are elected within the 29 constituencies. The number of members per district ranges from 2 to 40. The remainder{{snd}}the 39 other members{{snd}}are apportioned nationally as [[levelling seat]]s to ensure a proportional result. They are allocated to particular districts.

Were a party to win more constituencies than it is entitled to overall, a redistribution of constituency seats may occur to reduce the number of constituency seats won by that party.<ref>{{cite web |title=Vallag (2005:837) Svensk författningssamling 2005:2005:837 t.o.m. SFS 2021:1328 |url=https://www.riksdagen.se/sv/dokument-lagar/dokument/svensk-forfattningssamling/vallag-2005837_sfs-2005-837 |url-status=live |website=Riksdagen |date=15 May 2016 |access-date=27 August 2022 |at=Avdelning IV. Fördelning av mandat, 14 kap. Fördelning av mandat, 4 a § |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220830104719/https://www.riksdagen.se/sv/dokument-lagar/dokument/svensk-forfattningssamling/vallag-2005837_sfs-2005-837 |archive-date=30 August 2022 |language=sv}}</ref>

Sweden has the distinction of having elections on a fixed date with a parliamentary system in which early elections can be called. In the latter case, the newly elected legislature would serve the remainder of the four-year term begun by the previous legislature. Elections are organised on the second Sunday of September every four years, at the same time as the municipal and regional elections.<ref>{{cite web |title=Elections in Sweden: The way it's done |url=http://krasinskiy.ru/electionsswed.pdf |date=7 October 2013|access-date=31 August 2022 |website=Election Authority |location=Solna |archive-date=30 July 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200730230151/http://krasinskiy.ru/electionsswed.pdf |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=The Swedish electoral system |url=https://www.val.se/servicelankar/other-languages/english-engelska/the-swedish-electoral-system.html |url-status=dead |website=Valmyndigheten |date=16 September 2018 |access-date=13 September 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180916130429/https://www.val.se/servicelankar/other-languages/english-engelska/the-swedish-electoral-system.html |archive-date=16 September 2018 |language=sv}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=The 2022 election |url=https://www.riksdagen.se/en/the-2022-election/ |url-status=live |quote=Parliamentary elections will take place on 11 September. On this day voters will have the opportunity to decide which candidates will represent them in the Riksdag over the next four years. On the same day, there are elections to municipalities and regional councils. |website=Riksdag |date=31 August 2022 |access-date=31 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220831215425/https://www.riksdagen.se/en/the-2022-election/ |archive-date=31 August 2022}}</ref>

Each of the 29 constituencies has a set number of parliamentarians that is divided through constituency results to ensure regional representation. The other [[members of parliament]] (MPs) are then elected through a proportional balancing, to ensure that the numbers of elected MPs for the various parties accurately represent the votes of the electorate. The Swedish constitution ({{lang|sv|Regeringsformen}}) 1 Ch. 4 § says that the Riksdag is responsible for taxation and making laws, and 1 Ch. 6 § says that the government is held responsible to the Riksdag. This means that Sweden has [[parliamentarism]] in a [[constitutional monarchy]]{{snd}}ensuring that the government is responsible to the people's representatives. A minimum of 4% of the national vote, or alternatively 12% or more within a constituency, is required for a party to enter the Riksdag. Were the latter to occur, the party only gains representation within that constituency's seat share.

In previous Swedish elections, voters could openly pick up several party-specific ballots and then, in the [[voting booth]], use the ballot they chose. Two election observers of the [[OSCE]] who were present at the 2018 general election criticised this system, saying that the open selection of party-specific ballots could endanger [[ballot secrecy]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Bolling |first=Anders |date=9 September 2018 |title=Utländska observatörer granskar valsedlar som ligger öppet |language=sv |work=Dagens Nyheter |url-status=live}}</ref>

In August Lööf stated that she would want the [[Centre Party (Sweden)|Centre Party]] (C) to be part of a Social Democrat-led government (S, C, V, MP).<ref>{{cite news |date=16 August 2022 |title=Centre Party 'ready to join Social Democrat-led government' |url=https://www.thelocal.se/20220816/centre-party-ready-to-join-social-democrat-led-government/ |access-date=31 August 2022 |website=The Local Sweden |archive-date=31 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220831200841/https://www.thelocal.se/20220816/centre-party-ready-to-join-social-democrat-led-government/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Lööf was later a target of attack by a former member of the [[Nordic Resistance Movement]], a [[neo-Nazi]] political party.<ref name="Löfgren-2022" /> During the election campaign, the Left Party campaigned on "taking back control over welfare" and climate issues. Dadgostar stated her support for investing in [[green technology]] and infrastructure, and also criticised the parties on the right.<ref name="Waterton-2022">{{cite news |last=Waterton |first=Becky |date=24 August 2022 |title=What election pledges have Sweden's smaller political parties made this year? |url=https://www.thelocal.se/20220808/what-are-swedens-political-parties-election-pledges-for-2022/ |access-date=31 August 2022 |website=The Local Sweden |archive-date=31 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220831200841/https://www.thelocal.se/20220808/what-are-swedens-political-parties-election-pledges-for-2022/ |url-status=live}}</ref> She also stated that the Left Party would work with parties on the left to form a government.<ref>{{cite news |last=Orange |first=Richard |date=4 July 2022 |title=Left Party leader demands place in Swedish government after election |url=https://www.thelocal.se/20220704/left-party-leader-wants-place-in-swedish-government-after-election/ |access-date=31 August 2022 |website=The Local Sweden |archive-date=31 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220831200845/https://www.thelocal.se/20220704/left-party-leader-wants-place-in-swedish-government-after-election/ |url-status=live}}</ref> The [[Christian Democrats (Sweden)|Christian Democrats]] (KD) campaigned on installing more security cameras and increasing funding in resources for the police to fight gang crime. Busch called for the re-opening of [[Ringhals Nuclear Power Plant]], as well as expanding water and wind production.<ref name="Waterton-2022" /> The [[Liberals (Sweden)|Liberals]] (L) stated their support for more investments into solar, wind, and nuclear power. Additionally, the Liberals stated that they would want to lower taxes on electricity, especially VAT and excise taxes.<ref name="Waterton-2022" /> In August 2022 there was an internal conflict among the Liberals regarding campaigning on a bus tour that would have included SD.<ref>{{cite web |title=Strid i Liberalerna om bussturné med SD |url=https://www.dagenssamhalle.se/styrning-och-beslut/demokrati/liberal-om-bussturnen-ett-stycke-tidningsanka-ingen-storre-grej |access-date=16 September 2022 |website=Dagens Samhälle |language=sv |url-status=live |date=22 August 2022 |archive-date=12 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220912215248/https://www.dagenssamhalle.se/styrning-och-beslut/demokrati/liberal-om-bussturnen-ett-stycke-tidningsanka-ingen-storre-grej/}}</ref> Pehrson responded by stating that the four parties (M, SD, KD, L) would visit a nuclear power plant together, and described it as "hardly a big ideological question". There was also internal criticism regarding cooperating with SD on the budget.<ref>{{cite web |title=VAL 2022: Internt uppror i Liberalerna |url=https://marcusoscarsson.se/just-nu-internt-uppror-i-liberalerna/ |access-date=31 August 2022 |website=Marcus Oscarsson |language=sv |date=23 August 2022|archive-date=22 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220822151849/https://marcusoscarsson.se/just-nu-internt-uppror-i-liberalerna/ |url-status=live}}</ref> The Green Party campaigned on climate and social issues, including investment and expansion of rail/train transport in Sweden, and replacing fossil fuels and diesel with renewable fuels, as well as protecting free media and initiating a citizenship initiative system to allow in part for legislation proposed by citizens.<ref name="Waterton-2022"/>
