|url=https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2022-09-29-controversial-expropriation-bill-is-finally-approved-after-navigating-a-14-year-rocky-road/ |access-date=5 March 2024 |website=[[Daily Maverick]]|archive-date=29 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240529191037/https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2022-09-29-controversial-expropriation-bill-is-finally-approved-after-navigating-a-14-year-rocky-road/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Moves towards expropriation without compensation are largely framed as solutions to racial injustice.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Cocks |first=Tim |date=7 December 2021 |title=S. African law change plan to allow land expropriation fails to pass |url=https://www.reuters.com/markets/commodities/safrican-law-change-plan-allow-land-expropriation-fails-pass-2021-12-07/ |access-date=29 April 2024 |work=[[Reuters]] |archive-date=30 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230530220435/http://www.reuters.com/markets/commodities/safrican-law-change-plan-allow-land-expropriation-fails-pass-2021-12-07/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Reports from the South African government indicate that whites own 72% of total farms of agricultural holdings,<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 2017 |title=Land Audit Report |url=https://www.gov.za/sites/default/files/gcis_document/201802/landauditreport13feb2018.pdf |access-date=29 April 2024 |website=Department of Rural Development and Land Reform |archive-date=15 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240515223614/https://www.gov.za/sites/default/files/gcis_document/201802/landauditreport13feb2018.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref> while black South Africans are generally only responsible for between 5 and 10% of the country's agricultural output.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Constrained rural entrepreneurship in South Africa: A tale of two agricultures |url=https://business.leeds.ac.uk/cees/dir-record/research-blog/2161/constrained-rural-entrepreneurship-in-south-africa-a-tale-of-two-agricultures |access-date=30 April 2024 |website=business.leeds.ac.uk|archive-date=30 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240430231738/https://business.leeds.ac.uk/cees/dir-record/research-blog/2161/constrained-rural-entrepreneurship-in-south-africa-a-tale-of-two-agricultures |url-status=live }}</ref>

The ANC sees the current policy as a continuation of Nelson Mandela's promise to return 30% of the land to black South Africans. Currently, the ANC hopes to accomplish the goal by 2030.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hull |first=Elizabeth |date=17 October 2022 |title=Land reform in South Africa is failing. Ignoring the realities of rural life plays a part |url=http://theconversation.com/land-reform-in-south-africa-is-failing-ignoring-the-realities-of-rural-life-plays-a-part-190452 |access-date=30 April 2024 |website=The Conversation|archive-date=30 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240430231737/http://theconversation.com/land-reform-in-south-africa-is-failing-ignoring-the-realities-of-rural-life-plays-a-part-190452 |url-status=live }}</ref> In their election manifesto, the ANC claims that they will "accelerate land reform and redistribution to reduce asset inequality and protect security of tenure, improve food security and agricultural production, promote rural and urban development and enable greater access to housing."<ref name=":02">{{Cite web |date=24 February 2024 |title=ANC Election Manifesto |url=https://www.anc1912.org.za/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/ANC-2024-Elections-Manifesto.pdf |access-date=18 April 2024 |website=ANC Manifesto |archive-date=19 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240419030549/http://www.anc1912.org.za/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/ANC-2024-Elections-Manifesto.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref>

The EFF shares a similar stance to that of the ANC. In their manifesto, the EFF outlines seven pillars on which they are basing their policies. The first is explicitly in favor of expropriation, reading "expropriation of South Africa's land without compensation for equal redistribution in use."<ref name=":13">{{Cite web |date=10 February 2024 |title=2024 Election Manifesto |url=https://effonline.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/A5-EFF-2024-Manifesto-full-version.pdf |access-date=29 April 2024 |website=Economic Freedom Fighters |archive-date=9 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240309185642/https://effonline.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/A5-EFF-2024-Manifesto-full-version.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref> On the issue of expropriation, the EFF and ANC are mostly unified. Julius Malema, leader of the EFF, asserted that "when we say economic freedom, we mean Black people own productive farms."<ref>{{Cite web |date=18 November 2019 |title=Julius Malema: Land Expropriation Without Compensation |work=Berkeley Political Review |url=https://bpr.studentorg.berkeley.edu/2019/11/18/julius-malema-land-expropriation-without-compensation/ |access-date=30 April 2024|archive-date=30 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240430231739/https://bpr.studentorg.berkeley.edu/2019/11/18/julius-malema-land-expropriation-without-compensation/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

The DA opposes the policy of expropriation without compensation and sees attempts at expropriation as violating section 25 of the Constitution. Section 25 states that land may only be expropriated with compensation if the expropriation is in the public interest.<ref>Republic of South Africa. "THE CONSTITUTION of the REPUBLIC of SOUTH AFRICA, 1996." ''Justice.gov.za'', 1996, http://www.justice.gov.za/legislation/constitution/SAConstitution-web-eng.pdf {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140425031318/http://www.justice.gov.za/legislation/constitution/SAConstitution-web-eng.pdf |date=25 April 2014 }}.</ref> The party has called attempts to pass expropriation legislation "ruinous," an "assault on our constitutional values," and "archaic."<ref>{{Cite web |title=DA to challenge any attempt to bulldoze Expropriation Bill through parliament |url=https://www.da.org.za/2024/03/da-to-challenge-any-attempt-to-bulldoze-expropriation-bill-through-parliament |access-date=30 April 2024 |website=Democratic Alliance|archive-date=30 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240430231739/https://www.da.org.za/2024/03/da-to-challenge-any-attempt-to-bulldoze-expropriation-bill-through-parliament |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Energy crisis===
{{main|South African energy crisis}}

Rolling blackouts, or "loadshedding", caused by problems with the state utility [[Eskom]] have been occurring since 2007, however the prevalence of blackouts has increased substantially since 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |author=Hohm Energy |date=12 May 2023 |title=Sponsored Content: Its now official: South Africa has now had more load shedding in 2023 to date than in 2022 combined |url=https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2023-05-12-its-now-official-south-africa-has-now-had-more-load-shedding-in-2023-to-date-than-in-2022-combined/ |access-date=7 August 2023 |website=Daily Maverick|archive-date=7 August 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230807125836/https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2023-05-12-its-now-official-south-africa-has-now-had-more-load-shedding-in-2023-to-date-than-in-2022-combined/ |url-status=live }}</ref> There is general dissatisfaction with the ANC's handling of the blackouts, with a 2023 survey finding that 24% of voters who had previously supported the ANC were planning to switch to other parties if the issue was not resolved.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Payton |first=Ben |date=14 March 2024 |title=Power struggle: Energy in focus in South Africa's pivotal election |url=https://african.business/2024/03/energy-resources/power-struggle-energy-in-focus-in-south-africas-pivotal-election |access-date=27 March 2024 |website=African Business|archive-date=27 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240327212957/https://african.business/2024/03/energy-resources/power-struggle-energy-in-focus-in-south-africas-pivotal-election |url-status=live }}</ref>

The parties have taken varying stances on the issue. The ANC has pledged to create 12.5 million new jobs, a large portion of which will be devoted to a clean energy transition and modernisation of the nation's electrical system. The ANC has also linked the blackouts and energy crisis to environmental justice and climate change, claiming that its energy transition platform is also part of a larger transition to a cleaner economy.<ref>{{Cite web |date=24 February 2024 |title=South Africa's ANC launches election manifesto as president highlights party's achievements |url=https://apnews.com/article/south-africa-elections-anc-manifesto-jobs-646a45300a06f720fae842f5c1cad56b |access-date=18 April 2024 |website=AP News|archive-date=13 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240513151041/https://apnews.com/article/south-africa-elections-anc-manifesto-jobs-646a45300a06f720fae842f5c1cad56b |url-status=live }}</ref> According to the ANC's election manifesto, the party pledges to "cultivate partnerships to expand domestic industries with significant potential to create sustainable jobs... such as energy."<ref name=":02" /> Additionally, the party views a clean energy transition as essential in solving the energy crisis. Part of this transition is moving away from the coal-based electrical grid that is currently facing loadshedding.<ref>{{Cite web |date=24 February 2024 |title=South Africa's ANC launches election manifesto as president highlights party's achievements |url=https://apnews.com/article/south-africa-elections-anc-manifesto-jobs-646a45300a06f720fae842f5c1cad56b |access-date=30 April 2024 |website=AP News|archive-date=13 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240513151041/https://apnews.com/article/south-africa-elections-anc-manifesto-jobs-646a45300a06f720fae842f5c1cad56b |url-status=live }}</ref> That being said, the ANC has shown historical resistance to transitioning to new energy sources (i.e. renewables).<ref>{{Cite web |date=24 January 2024 |title=Rolling Blackouts in South Africa |url=https://blog.ecoflow.com/za/rolling-blackouts-in-south-africa/ |access-date=1 May 2024 |website=EcoFlow|archive-date=1 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240501000622/https://blog.ecoflow.com/za/rolling-blackouts-in-south-africa/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

The DA largely blames the ANC for the energy crisis, saying that the state uses an "outdated" model of control and regulation. The DA intends to reduce government control over the energy sector if it is able to form a government. Using the [[Western Cape]] as a case study, the DA says it has a successful platform for energy solutions. They argue that recent contracts to build new solar plants in the area are indicative of this.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024 |title=The DA's Rescue Plan For South Africa |url=https://cdn.da.org.za/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/16143750/DA-Election-Manifesto-2024.pdf |access-date=18 April 2024 |website=DA Election Manifesto |archive-date=19 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240419012148/http://cdn.da.org.za/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/16143750/DA-Election-Manifesto-2024.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref> Much of their energy platform has to do with deregulation and reducing taxes on private entities.<ref>{{Cite web |title=What has the DA been doing to fix the electricity crisis? |url=https://www.da.org.za/fixing-the-electricity-crisis |access-date=30 April 2024 |website=Democratic Alliance|archive-date=1 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240501000615/https://www.da.org.za/fixing-the-electricity-crisis |url-status=live }}</ref>

The EFF takes a [[Marxism|Marxist]] and [[Black nationalism|black nationalist]] approach to the issue. The party calls for the end of the privatization of Eskom, while calling for the involvement of the private sector in new electricity generation as part of efforts to shift control to the "majority of black people."<ref name=":13" />

=== Crime ===
{{Main|Crime in South Africa}}

According to the [[South African Police Service]] Crime Statistics for Quarter 2 of the 2023–24 financial year, reported contact crimes (defined by SAPS as "crimes against the person") has increased by 3 391 (2.1%) compared to the previous year.<ref name=":0">South African Police Service, 2023. Police Recorded Crime Statistics, Republic of South Africa: Second Quarter of 2023–2024 Financial Year (July 2023 to September 2023). Available at https://www.gov.za/sites/default/files/gcis_documents/saps_stats.pdf {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231209070050/https://www.gov.za/sites/default/files/gcis_documents/saps_stats.pdf |date=9 December 2023 }} Accessed on 3 January 2024</ref> Recorded attempted murder illustrated the highest increase year-on-year, with 12.3%.<ref name=":0" /> Total contact crimes reported for the quarter are 165,909. The murder rate correlates to 77 people murdered per day, while 160 cases of assault with intent to do grievous bodily harm are reported over the same period.<ref>{{Cite web |date=17 November 2023 |title=Cele and his management content with South Africans living in a slaughter house as bloodbath continues |url=https://actionsociety.co.za/cele-and-his-management-content-with-south-africans-living-in-a-slaughter-house-as-bloodbath-continues/ |access-date=3 January 2024 |website=Action Society|archive-date=3 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240103195512/https://actionsociety.co.za/cele-and-his-management-content-with-south-africans-living-in-a-slaughter-house-as-bloodbath-continues/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Prior to the election, political violence was reportedly on the rise, especially in [[KwaZulu-Natal]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=3 December 2023 |title=South Africa: The region where political violence is on the rise ahead of elections |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-67576270 |access-date=31 January 2024 |publisher=BBC News|archive-date=31 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240131225830/https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-67576270 |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[Action Society]] notes that "if the current murder trend continues, at least 31,000 people will be killed in the next 12 months...the [South African Government] has lost control..."<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |last=du Preez |first=Juanita |date=16 February 2024 |title=One raped every 12 minutes; South Africans abandoned in war against crime – Action Society |url=https://actionsociety.co.za/one-raped-every-12-minutes-south-africans-abandoned-in-war-against-crime-action-society/ |access-date=21 February 2024 |website=Action Society|archive-date=21 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240221195906/https://actionsociety.co.za/one-raped-every-12-minutes-south-africans-abandoned-in-war-against-crime-action-society/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Housing ===
{{Main|Land reform in South Africa}}

The lack of adequate housing has been a major issue.<ref>{{Cite web |date=19 December 2023 |title=Key statistics ahead of South Africa's 2024 elections |url=https://www.citizen.co.za/news/key-statistics-ahead-of-south-africas-2024-elections/ |access-date=31 January 2024 |website=The Citizen|archive-date=31 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240131225830/https://www.citizen.co.za/news/key-statistics-ahead-of-south-africas-2024-elections/ |url-status=live }}</ref> According to a report from [[Parliament of South Africa|Parliament]], dated May 2022, the human settlements sector had a total of 3.4 million housing units built since 1994. The respective provinces and municipalities delivered a separate 1.3 million "serviced sites".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Parliament of the Republic of South Africa |title=Report of the Portfolio Committee on Human Settlements on Budget Vote 33: Human Settlements and on the revised Strategic Plan for the coming Medium Term Expenditure Framework (MTEF) period and Annual Performance Plan 2022–23, 4 May 2022. |url=https://www.groundup.org.za/media/uploads/documents/dhs-2022.pdf |website=GroundUp |access-date=6 February 2024 |archive-date=28 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240128045857/https://www.groundup.org.za/media/uploads/documents/dhs-2022.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref> A parliamentary question to the Minister of Human Settlements revealed there were 2,456,773 households registered on the National Housing Needs Register as of February 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Question to the Minister of Human Settlements – NW535 |url=https://pmg.org.za/committee-question/21399/ |access-date=6 February 2024 |website=pmg.org.za|archive-date=6 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240206165510/https://pmg.org.za/committee-question/21399/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In the [[City of Cape Town]], there were 375,150 on the municipalities' Housing Needs Register.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bezuidenhout |first=Natasha |title='It is finally happening': Construction of Village Heights development commence |url=https://www.news24.com/news24/community-newspaper/peoples-post/it-is-finally-happening-construction-of-village-heights-development-commence-20230530 |access-date=6 February 2024 |website=News24|date=30 May 2023 |archive-date=1 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240601124851/https://www.news24.com/news24/community-newspaper/peoples-post/it-is-finally-happening-construction-of-village-heights-development-commence-20230530 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In answer to a [[Parliamentary question]] to the Minister of Human Settlements on 24 March 2024, she stated that her department had built 245,587 houses in the five years between January 2019 and January 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Question to the Minister of Human Settlements – NW398 |url=https://pmg.org.za/committee-question/25189/ |access-date=2 April 2024 |website=pmg.org.za|archive-date=2 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240402180717/https://pmg.org.za/committee-question/25189/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Cadre deployment ===
The ANC has practised a policy of employing people who are loyal to the ANC to positions within institutions of government. The [[Zondo Commission]] has found that cadre deployment played a significant part in corruption and went as far as to say that it is "illegal and unconstitutional".<ref>{{Cite web |title='Cadre deployment is illegal' – Zondo |url=https://www.news24.com/citypress/politics/cadre-deployment-is-illegal-zondo-20220625 |access-date=23 February 2024 |website=City Press|archive-date=23 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240223173949/https://www.news24.com/citypress/politics/cadre-deployment-is-illegal-zondo-20220625 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 12 February 2024, the [[Constitutional Court of South Africa|Constitutional Court]] ruled that the ANC had five days to hand over their cadre deployment records to the [[Democratic Alliance (South Africa)|Democratic Alliance]] dating back to 1 January 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Davis |first=Rebecca |date=12 February 2024 |title=ANC has five days to hand over cadre deployment records to DA |url=https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2024-02-12-anc-given-five-days-to-release-contentious-cadre-deployment-records-to-da/ |access-date=14 February 2024 |website=Daily Maverick|archive-date=14 |website=Democratic Alliance |archive-date=23 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240223173950/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1bOVxoA2IR4 |url-status=live }}</ref> showing that |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Cape independence===
{{main|Cape independence}}

The [[Freedom Front Plus]] and the [[Referendum Party (South Africa)|Referendum Party]] contested the election with [[Cape independence]] as part of their platform. The Referendum Party was formed in November 2023 as a single-issue political party aiming to pressure the Western Cape [[Democratic Alliance (South Africa)|Democratic Alliance]] government into holding a referendum on Western Cape independence as part of any potential coalition agreement.<ref>{{Cite web |date=26 November 2023 |title=Challenging political norms: Referendum Party versus DA in the Western Cape |url=https://www.biznews.com/rational-perspective/2023/11/26/referendum-party-vs-da-western-cape |access-date=31 December 2023 |website=BizNews|archive-date=31 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231231210609/https://www.biznews.com/rational-perspective/2023/11/26/referendum-party-vs-da-western-cape |url-status=live }}</ref> The [[Cape Independence Party]], which had contested in [[2009 South African general election|2009]] and [[2019 South African general election|2019]], did not make it on to the national ballot or the Western Cape provincial ballot, while the Referendum Party made it on to all three.<ref>{{Cite web |date=4 February 2022 |title=Self-determination is the issue of the year in the Western Cape |url=https://mg.co.za/thought-leader/opinion/2022-02-04-self-determination-is-the-issue-of-the-year-in-the-western-cape/ |access-date=4 January 2024 |archive-date=4 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240104080235/https://mg.co.za/thought-leader/opinion/2022-02-04-self-determination-is-the-issue-of-the-year-in-the-western-cape/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Bourdin |first=Julie |title=CapeXit? ==Highly contested provinces==
=== Gauteng ===
[[Gauteng]] is the most populated province and is the ''de facto'' economic hub of South Africa. In 2019 the ANC had barely retained the province, getting 50.19% of the vote. The DA hoped to win Gauteng with [[Solly Msimanga]] as their premier candidate.<ref>{{Cite web |date=13 September 2023 |title=Solly Msimanga is DA candidate for Gauteng premier |url=https://mg.co.za/politics/2023-09-13-solly-msimanga-is-da-candidate-for-gauteng-premier/ |access-date=11 April 2024 |website=The Mail & Guardian|archive-date=16 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016133200/https://mg.co.za/politics/2023-09-13-solly-msimanga-is-da-candidate-for-gauteng-premier/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Funzi Ngobeni was [[ActionSA]]'s premier candidate,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Njilo |first=Nonkululeko |date=29 February 2024 |title=ActionSA's Funzi Ngobeni joins competitive race for Gauteng premier |url=https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2024-02-29-actionsas-funzi-ngobeni-joins-competitive-race-for-gauteng-premier/ |access-date=11 April 2024 |website=Daily Maverick|archive-date=1 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240301023504/https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2024-02-29-actionsas-funzi-ngobeni-joins-competitive-race-for-gauteng-premier/ |url-status=live }}</ref> while the ANC's candidate was current premier, [[Panyaza Lesufi]].

The ANC lost its majority in Gauteng, claiming under 35% of the vote, followed by the DA with just over 28%.

=== KwaZulu-Natal ===
[[KwaZulu-Natal]] is the second most populated province and is home to the [[Durban|busiest port]] in southern Africa. Recent polling had the new [[MK Party]] leading in the province, having grown substantially at the expense of ANC support. [[Chris Pappas (South African politician)|Christopher Pappas]] was the premier candidate for the DA, while Thami Ntuli was the [[Inkatha Freedom Party|IFP]]'s candidate.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Maliti |first=Soyiso |title=DA pins its KZN hopes on 'principled' Pappas for premier |url=https://www.news24.com/news24/politics/da-pins-its-kzn-hopes-on-principled-pappas-for-premier-20230925 |access-date=11 April 2024 |website=News24|archive-date=1 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240601125823/https://www.news24.com/news24/politics/da-pins-its-kzn-hopes-on-principled-pappas-for-premier-20230925 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Mbolekwa |first=Sisanda |title=Thami Ntuli was KZN IFP premier candidate |url=https://www.timeslive.co.za/politics/2024-01-29-thami-ntuli-is-kzn-ifp-premier-candidate/ |access-date=11 April 2024 |website=TimesLIVE|date=29 January 2024 |archive-date=4 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240404082704/https://www.timeslive.co.za/politics/2024-01-29-thami-ntuli-is-kzn-ifp-premier-candidate/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The ANC's premier candidate was Sbongiseni Duma. MK took 45.9% of the vote, leaving the ANC with only 17.6%, the DA not far behind.

=== Western Cape ===
As of April 2024, the [[Western Cape]] was the only province not to be controlled by the ANC. The DA, which has controlled the province since 2009, looked to retain the province with Premier [[Alan Winde]] as their premier candidate.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cotterell |first=Gareth |date=26 August 2023 |title=Alan Winde announced as DA's Western Cape premier candidate for 2024 election |url=https://www.citizen.co.za/news/south-africa/politics/alan-winde-da-western-cape-premier-candidate-2024-election/ |access-date=11 April 2024 |website=The Citizen|archive-date=30 September 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230930071326/https://www.citizen.co.za/news/south-africa/politics/alan-winde-da-western-cape-premier-candidate-2024-election/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

The DA retained control of the Western Cape with a 53% majority.

== Incidents ==
=== DA campaign video ===
In May 2024, the [[Democratic Alliance (South Africa)|DA]] released a campaign video attacking the ANC and showing a [[South African flag]] on fire, saying that the same fate would befall the country should the ANC remain in power. The flag appears restored in the final seven seconds of the advert. DA leader [[John Steenhuisen]] described the video as "the most successful political advertisement in our democratic history," saying that it was seen by at least four million people online and heard by "millions more" in other media. President and [[African National Congress|ANC]] leader Cyril Ramaphosa called the ad "despicable" and "treasonous", while the public broadcaster [[SABC]] announced that it would not air the video, saying that it would only fuel "outrage", and called on the DA to amend the advert.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Imray |first=Gerald |date=10 May 2024 |title=A campaign ad by a South African party showing a burning flag is called treason by the president |url=https://apnews.com/article/south-africa-election-ad-flag-burning-150e662e71aabbc447f9bbe52abeb75b |access-date=10 May 2024 |website=[[Associated Press]]|archive-date=10 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240510145219/https://apnews.com/article/south-africa-election-ad-flag-burning-150e662e71aabbc447f9bbe52abeb75b |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=9 May 2024 |title=Rejection of Democratic Alliance's TV Advertisement |url=https://pbs.twimg.com/media/GNJT78WWUAIffKz?format=jpg&name=large |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240509151707/https://pbs.twimg.com/media/GNJT78WWUAIffKz?format=jpg&name=large |archive-date=9 May 2024 |access-date=10 May 2024 |website=Internet Archive}}</ref> Several analysts and organisations have noted that, although in "poor taste", the burning of the flag is protected under Section 16 of the [[Constitution of South Africa|Constitution]] as a freedom of expression.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Manjeya |first=Yamkeleka |title=SABC's ban on DA advert raises free speech concerns |url=https://www.news24.com/citypress/politics/sabcs-ban-on-da-advert-raises-free-speech-concerns-20240510 |access-date=10 May 2024 |website=City Press|archive-date=2 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240602154535/https://www.news24.com/citypress/politics/sabcs-ban-on-da-advert-raises-free-speech-concerns-20240510 |url-status=live }}</ref>

The Complaints and Compliance Committee of the [[Independent Communications Authority of South Africa]] ruled on 24 May that the SABC be directed to desist from not airing the advert and pay a R500,000 fine within seven days.<ref>{{Cite web |date=24 May 2024 |title=SABC fined R500 000 for refusing to air DA election ad – TechCentral |url=https://techcentral.co.za/sabc-fined-refusing-to-air-da-election-ad/245330/ |access-date=24 May 2024|archive-date=24 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240524192344/https://techcentral.co.za/sabc-fined-refusing-to-air-da-election-ad/245330/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Jacob Zuma ===
Former [[President of South Africa|President]] [[Jacob Zuma]] founded the [[UMkhonto we Sizwe (political party)|uMkhonto we Sizwe]] (MK Party) in December 2023, intending to contest the election.<ref>{{Cite web |date=19 May 2024 |title=Jacob Zuma's MK takes fight to ANC stronghold of Soweto in South Africa election |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c51134895v8o |access-date=21 May 2024 |publisher=BBC News|archive-date=21 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240521172917/https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c51134895v8o |url-status=live }}</ref> On 20 May 2024, the [[Constitutional Court of South Africa]] ruled that Zuma is ineligible to run in the parliamentary election due to his 2021 jail sentence.<ref>{{Cite web |date=20 May 2024 |title=Jacob Zuma barred from standing in South Africa's election by Constitutional Court |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cv22l7mlxdzo |access-date=21 May 2024 |publisher=BBC News|archive-date=21 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240521134435/https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cv22l7mlxdzo |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Presidential Address to the Nation ===
On 26 May, the [[President of South Africa|Presidency]] announced that [[Cyril Ramaphosa]] would address the nation at 6pm.<ref>{{Cite web |title=President Ramaphosa to address the nation |url=https://www.thepresidency.gov.za/president-ramaphosa-address-nation-15 |access-date=26 May 2024 |website=thepresidency.gov.za |archive-date=26 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240526182431/https://www.thepresidency.gov.za/president-ramaphosa-address-nation-15 |url-status=live }}</ref> In his address, broadcast by the [[SABC]], he listed the achievements of his government. The address was criticised by opposition parties as an abuse of government resources for electioneering in favour of the ruling party.<ref>{{Cite web |title=WRAP {{!}} COMMENT: Ramaphosa 'abuses' national address to cynically campaign for the ANC |url=https://www.news24.com/news24/southafrica/news/live-president-cyril-ramaphosa-to-address-the-nation-20240526 |access-date=26 May 2024 |website=News24|archive-date=26 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240526182456/https://www.news24.com/news24/southafrica/news/live-president-cyril-ramaphosa-to-address-the-nation-20240526 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Voting==
[[Early voting]] for overseas citizens was held in [[List of diplomatic missions of South Africa|South African diplomatic missions]] on 17 and 18 May.<ref name="logistics" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=About voting abroad – Electoral Commission of South Africa |url=https://www.elections.org.za/pw/VotingAbroad/About-Voting-Abroad |website=Elections.org.za |access-date=29 May 2024 |archive-date=21 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240521225524/https://www.elections.org.za/pw/VotingAbroad/About-Voting-Abroad |url-status=live }}</ref> Early voting for domestic voters was held on 27 May, covering 1.6 million people including essential workers and about 624,000 people unable to leave their homes.<ref>{{Cite news |date=27 May 2024 |title=Early voting begins in South African elections that could spell end of ANC dominance |url=https://www.france24.com/en/africa/20240527-early-voting-begins-in-south-african-elections-that-could-spell-end-of-anc-dominance |access-date=27 May 2024 |work=France 24|archive-date=27 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240527141754/https://www.france24.com/en/africa/20240527-early-voting-begins-in-south-african-elections-that-could-spell-end-of-anc-dominance |url-status=live }}</ref> On election day, polling in more than 23,000 precincts<ref>{{Cite news |date=29 May 2024 |title=South Africans begins voting in an election seen as their country's most important in 30 years |url=https://apnews.com/article/south-africa-election-anc-vote-db201bc1aa21a1d986d50af1674a8e78 |access-date=29 May 2024 |work=[[Associated Press]]|archive-date=2 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240602154457/https://apnews.com/article/south-africa-election-anc-vote-db201bc1aa21a1d986d50af1674a8e78 |url-status=live }}</ref> opened at 07:00 and closed at 21:00.<ref>{{Cite news |date=29 May 2024 |title=South Africans vote in election that could end the ANC's parliamentary majority |url=https://www.france24.com/en/africa/20240529-south-africans-vote-in-election-that-could-end-the-anc-s-parliamentary-majority |access-date=29 May 2024 |work=France 24|archive-date=29 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240529061323/https://www.france24.com/en/africa/20240529-south-africans-vote-in-election-that-could-end-the-anc-s-parliamentary-majority |url-status=live }}</ref> Three thousand [[SANDF]] soldiers were deployed to ensure security during the election, while the Independent Electoral Commission said two people were arrested for interfering with voting operations.<ref>{{Cite news |date=29 May 2024 |title=South Africans vote in a pivotal election as president says he has no doubt his ANC party will win |url=https://apnews.com/article/south-africa-election-anc-vote-db201bc1aa21a1d986d50af1674a8e78 |access-date=29 May 2024 |work=[[Associated Press]]|archive-date=2 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240602154457/https://apnews.com/article/south-africa-election-anc-vote-db201bc1aa21a1d986d50af1674a8e78 |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Julius Malema]] voted in [[Limpopo]] after queuing for three hours.<ref>{{Cite web |title=EFF's Malema votes after queuing for three hours |url=https://www.the-star.co.ke/news/africa/2024-05-29-effs-malema-votes-after-queuing-for-three-hours/ |access-date=29 May 2024 |website=[[The Star (Kenya)|The Star]]|archive-date=29 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240529150331/https://www.the-star.co.ke/news/africa/2024-05-29-effs-malema-votes-after-queuing-for-three-hours/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Counting was delayed in several precincts due to last-minute queues of voters,<ref>{{Cite web |title=South Africa counts ballots in most competitive election since apartheid |url=https://www.france24.com/en/africa/20240530-south-africa-counts-ballots-after-most-competitive-election-since-apartheid |access-date=30 May 2024 |website=[[France 24]] |date=30 May 2024}}</ref> with the last ballots being cast at around 03:00 on 30 May as electoral law allows those still lining up to vote at regular closing time to participate.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Partial count in South Africa election puts ruling ANC below 50% as country senses monumental change |url=https://apnews.com/article/south-africa-election-change-vote-anc-25a03780bec29503ab3d9f6e9f96dc4c |access-date=30 May 2024 |website=[[Associated Press]] |date=30 May 2024|archive-date=1 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240601131904/https://apnews.com/article/south-africa-election-change-vote-anc-25a03780bec29503ab3d9f6e9f96dc4c |url-status=live }}</ref> 

The [[African Union]] sent a mission led by former Kenyan president [[Uhuru Kenyatta]] to monitor the election.<ref>{{Cite web |title=South Africa leader under pressure after election blow |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cyeek2xlgzzo |access-date=1 June 2024 |publisher=[[BBC]]|archive-date=31 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240531225129/https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cyeek2xlgzzo |url-status=live }}</ref> The voting was described as free and fair by the IEC and independent observers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=South Africa political parties cobble together unity government as deadline to elect president looms |url=https://apnews.com/article/south-africa-elections-lawmakers-parliament-negotiations-3fc23d8f18cbd62be982d1076c7e2e46 |access-date=13 June 2024 |website=[[Associated Press]]|date=13 June 2024 |archive-date=13 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240613084029/https://apnews.com/article/south-africa-elections-lawmakers-parliament-negotiations-3fc23d8f18cbd62be982d1076c7e2e46 |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Results ==
{{Main article|Results of the 2024 South African general election}}

The election resulted in a historic defeat for the ANC, which having received only 40% of the vote, lost the parliamentary majority that it held since 1994.<ref>{{Cite web |title=South Africa election result: Will ANC share power with MK party or DA? |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cyeek2xlgzzo |access-date=2 June 2024 |publisher=BBC|archive-date=1 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240601124426/https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cyeek2xlgzzo |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=1 June 2024 |title=South Africa's ANC loses its 30-year majority in landmark election |url=https://www.voanews.com/a/7638745.html |access-date=2 June 2024 |website=Voice of America|archive-date=2 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240602160329/https://www.voanews.com/a/7638745.html |url-status=live }}</ref> It also failed to secure a majority in [[Northern Cape]] and [[Gauteng]], and was outpolled in [[KwaZulu-Natal]] by the MK. In overseas voting, the DA won 75.23% of the 39,084 votes cast and retained its majority in the [[Western Cape]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2 June 2024 |title=South Africa elections results: What happens next? |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/6/2/south-africa-elections-results-what-happens-next |access-date=2 June 2024 |website=Al Jazeera|archive-date=2 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240602155002/https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/6/2/south-africa-elections-results-what-happens-next |url-status=live }}</ref> The ANC retained reduced majorities in [[Eastern Cape]], [[Free State (province)|Free State]], [[Limpopo]], [[Mpumalanga]] and [[North West (South African province)|North West]] and retained largest opposition status in Western Cape, while the DA retained its largest opposition status in the National Assembly. No overall majority was achieved in the National Assembly, nor in the provinces of KwaZulu-Natal, Gauteng or Northern Cape, with the MK achieving a plurality in KwaZulu-Natal and the ANC being forced into second-largest party status in KwaZulu-Natal for the first time since it first won the province in 2004.<ref>IEC South Africa, National and Provincial election results https://results.elections.org.za/home/Downloads/NPE-Results {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240603111020/https://results.elections.org.za/home/Downloads/NPE-Results |date=3 June 2024 }}</ref> Most of the ANC's loss of support flowed into the MK, while the DA saw some gains, and the EFF lost some support.<ref>{{Cite web |date=4 June 2024 |title=Race to form South Africa's next government: Who will the ANC ally with? |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/6/3/race-to-form-south-africas-next-government-who-will-the-anc-ally-with |access-date=4 June 2024 |website=Al Jazeera|archive-date=3 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240603235209/https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/6/3/race-to-form-south-africas-next-government-who-will-the-anc-ally-with |url-status=live }}</ref> The proportion of women members of the National Assembly remained at 45%, the same level as after the [[2019 South African general election|2019 election]].<ref name="nai.uu.se">{{Cite web |title=Big man politics and multi-party rule call for new gender plans - The Nordic Africa Institute |url=https://nai.uu.se/stories-and-events/news/2024-11-13-big-man-politics-and-multi-party-rule-call-for-new-gender-plans.html |access-date=2024-11-15 |website=nai.uu.se |language=en}}</ref>

===Provincial legislatures===
{{Main article|2024 South African provincial elections}}
[[File:South-africa-provincial-elections.svg|thumb|250px|Provincial election results]]
The ANC won seven provinces out of nine, securing majorities in five of them except for the [[Northern Cape]]<ref>{{cite news |last1=Monteiro |first1=Ana |title=ANC Loses Its Outright Majority in South Africa's Northern Cape |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2024-05-31/anc-loses-its-outright-majority-in-south-africa-s-northern-cape |access-date=4 June 2024 |agency=Bloomberg |date=31 May 2024 |archive-date=5 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240605080415/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2024-05-31/anc-loses-its-outright-majority-in-south-africa-s-northern-cape |url-status=live }}</ref> and [[Gauteng]],<ref>{{cite news |last1=SCHRIEBER |first1=SINESIPHO |title=From 53% to 36%: ANC loses confidence of Gauteng voters |url=https://www.timeslive.co.za/politics/2024-06-01-from-53-to-36-anc-loses-confidence-of-gauteng-voters/ |access-date=4 June 2024 |agency=Times Live |date=1 June 2024 |archive-date=5 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240605235559/https://www.timeslive.co.za/politics/2024-06-01-from-53-to-36-anc-loses-confidence-of-gauteng-voters/ |url-status=live }}</ref> where it earned pluralities. It performed best in [[Limpopo]], the country's northernmost province, winning slightly less than three quarters of the vote.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Matlata |first1=Alex |title=Limpopo delivers big win for ANC, defying expectations |url=https://www.citizen.co.za/news/south-africa/elections/limpopo-delivers-big-win-for-anc-defying-expectations/ |access-date=4 June 2024 |agency=The Citizen |date=4 June 2024 |archive-date=4 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240604050643/https://www.citizen.co.za/news/south-africa/elections/limpopo-delivers-big-win-for-anc-defying-expectations/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The DA held on to the [[Western Cape]], continuing its 15-year-rule over the province.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Monique |first1=Vanek |title=South Africa's DA Holds Onto Power in Western Cape Province |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2024-06-01/south-africa-s-da-holds-onto-power-in-western-cape-province |access-date=4 June 2024 |agency=Bloomberg |date=1 June 2024 |archive-date=5 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240605080415/https://www.bloomberg.com/article/api/blens |url-status=live }}</ref> Finally, the new MK party flipped [[KwaZulu Natal]] from the ANC, earning 37 out of 80 seats to gain a plurality.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hunter |first1=Qaanitah |title=Zuma big election 'winner' as South Africa heads for coalition government |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/5/31/zuma-big-election-winner-as-south-africa-heads-for-coalition-government |access-date=4 June 2024 |agency=AlJazeera |date=31 May 2024 |archive-date=31 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240531143528/https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/5/31/zuma-big-election-winner-as-south-africa-heads-for-coalition-government |url-status=live }}</ref> Women's average representation after the provincial elections was 44% in the provincial legislatures and 47% in the provincial executives. Only two out of the nine premiers were women, and only two out of the nine speakers in the legislatures were men.<ref name="nai.uu.se"/>

==Aftermath==
{{Main|Third Cabinet of Cyril Ramaphosa|28th South African Parliament|2024 South African presidential election}}

While counting was ongoing, the ANC said that its leadership would meet on 31 May to "reflect on what is good for the country." The DA's [[John Steenhuisen]] said that the results showed that South Africa was "heading into coalition country" and expressed a willingness to work alongside the ANC, adding that he would have to first consult with other signatories of the Multi-Party Charter.<ref>{{Cite news |date=31 May 2024 |title=South Africa heads for 'coalition country' as partial election results put ruling ANC well below 50% |url=https://apnews.com/article/south-africa-election-vote-anc-0799ce0d04399fdf594aa8a7ac7914e3 |access-date=31 May 2024 |work=[[Associated Press]]|archive-date=31 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240531084810/https://apnews.com/article/south-africa-election-vote-anc-0799ce0d04399fdf594aa8a7ac7914e3 |url-status=live }}</ref> The DA also said that a government composed of the ANC, the MK, and the EFF would be a "doomsday coalition" pursuing previous policy failures in the country. The EFF's [[Julius Malema]] said that the election results marked the end of the ANC's "entitlement of being the sole dominant party", adding that he was open to talks with the ANC on forming a coalition government. The Patriotic Alliance's [[Gayton McKenzie]] compared prospects of an ANC-DA coalition to "a marriage of two drunk people in Las Vegas" that would prove "unworkable".<ref>{{Cite web |date=2 June 2024 |title=The ANC party that freed South Africa from apartheid loses its 30-year majority in landmark election |url=https://apnews.com/article/south-africa-election-vote-anc-d9da7582ca98a4e00fec2da6a5fe1e91 |access-date=2 June 2024 |website=Associated Press|archive-date=2 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240602034552/https://apnews.com/article/south-africa-election-vote-anc-d9da7582ca98a4e00fec2da6a5fe1e91 |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[Gwede Mantashe]], the ANC's [[National Executive Committee of the African National Congress|national chair]], said that the party had started to conduct informal talks with other parties for a possible coalition.<ref>{{Cite news |date=31 May 2024 |title=Zuma big election 'winner' as South Africa heads for coalition government |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/5/31/zuma-big-election-winner-as-south-africa-heads-for-coalition-government |access-date=31 May 2024 |work=[[Al Jazeera]]|archive-date=31 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240531143528/https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/5/31/zuma-big-election-winner-as-south-africa-heads-for-coalition-government |url-status=live }}</ref> On 2 June, ANC secretary-general [[Fikile Mbalula]] announced the official opening of negotiations,<ref name="f24anc" /> adding that the party had heard the popular will and was "humbled" by the election result. Mbalula also said that the ANC would reject conditions by other parties for [[Cyril Ramaphosa]] to step down as president.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2 June 2024 |title=South Africa's 'humbled' ANC talking On the same day, the ANC, the DA, the [[Inkatha Freedom Party]] (IFP) and the [[Patriotic Alliance]] (PA), agreed to form a national unity government, with [[Cyril Ramaphosa]] being re-elected [[President of South Africa]].<ref name="ancda2">{{cite news |last1=Chothia |first1=Farouk |last2=Kupemba |first2=Danai Kesta |last3=Plett-Usher |first3=Barbra |date=14 June 2024 |title=ANC and DA agree on South Africa unity government |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c8007w4vqveo |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240614112052/https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c8007w4vqveo |archive-date=14 June 2024 |access-date=14 June 2024 |work=BBC News}}</ref><ref name="ramaphosare-elected2">{{cite news |date=14 June 2024 |title=South Africa's National Assembly re-elects Cyril Ramaphosa as president |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/south-africas-national-assembly-re-elects-cyril-ramaphosa-president-2024-06-14/ |access-date=14 June 2024 |work=Reuters}}</ref> He was sworn in as president on 19 June while negotiations on the cabinet were ongoing. 

In an interview on [[SABC News]]' ''Face the Nation'' current affairs programme, DA Federal Council Chairperson [[Helen Zille]] said in reference to the Patriotic Alliance admission: "So you can't just let anybody come in without consulting with us and then he makes the appointments in consultation with the leaders of the parties who have been accepted for admission".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Maromo |first=Jonisayi |date=19 June 2024 |title=Patriotic Alliance: Helen Zille thinks she is in charge of the government of national unity |url=https://www.iol.co.za/news/politics/patriotic-alliance-helen-zille-thinks-she-is-in-charge-of-the-government-of-national-unity-f249576f-b76c-4621-971b-cf711bdeb237 |access-date=19 June 2024 |website=IOL News}}</ref> Zille specifically referred to Clause 17 of the Statement of Intent, which governs the President's powers in appointing an Executive. Clauses 18 and 19 of the statement deal with the concept of "sufficient consensus", which among other points, only exists when "parties to the [[Third Cabinet of Cyril Ramaphosa|GNU]] representing 60% of the seats in the National Assembly agree".<ref name="SignedStatementOfIntent2"/>

Other parties to join the national unity government were GOOD, shortly after the first sitting of parliament, the [[Pan Africanist Congress|PAC]], on the 19th, and the [[FF+]] on the 20th of June. The [[United Democratic Movement|UDM]] decided to join on the 21st, [[Rise Mzansi]] on the 22nd, [[Al Jama-ah]] on the 23rd, and [[United Africans Transformation|UAT]] on the 30th of June 2024.<ref name="President30June2024">{{cite web |date=30 June 2024 |title=Statement by President Cyril Ramaphosa on the appointment of members of the national executive |url=https://www.presidency.gov.za/statement-president-cyril-ramaphosa-appointment-members-national-executive |access-date=7 July 2024}}</ref><ref name="President30June2024YouTube">{{cite web |date=30 June 2024 |title=President Ramaphosa Announces South African New Government: GNU, A Historic Unity of 11 Parties! |website=[[YouTube]] |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YTTYtynxGY8 |access-date=30 June 2024}}</ref> This brought the GNU to [[Cabinet of South Africa#Current cabinet|288 seats]] in the 400 seat parliament (72%). On 12 July 2024 the UAT withdrew from the GNU, because it did not receive any positions in the [[Cabinet of South Africa|Cabinet]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Ludidi |first=Velani |title=United Africans Transformation withdraws from GNU after not getting positions |url=https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2024-07-12-uat-withdraws-from-gnu-after-not-getting-positions/ |access-date=12 July 2024 |website=Daily Maverick|date=12 July 2024 }}</ref> This did not adjust the 72% of GNU seats in parliament.

The DA reportedly requested 10 posts in the cabinet, including the ministries of Communication and digital technology, Trade and industry, Transport, Public service and administration, Water and sanitation, Local government and Health, as well as deputy minister posts of finance and health. In addition, the DA requested that [[John Steenhuisen]] be designated as deputy president over ANC incumbent [[Paul Mashatile]]. The ANC rejected most of the requests on the grounds of multiple other parties joining the coalition negotiations, instead agreeing to up to five cabinet positions for the DA. The DA's negotiators, including Steenhuisen and [[Tony Leon]], considered withdrawing, but instead agreed to keep negotiations open with the ANC.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patel |first=Faizel |date=2024-06-23 |title=DA 'wants Steenhuisen as deputy president' in GNU |url=https://www.citizen.co.za/news/south-africa/politics/da-steenhuisen-deputy-president-gnu-ramaphosa-cabinet-latest/ |access-date=2024-06-23 |website=The Citizen |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Staff Reporter |date=June 23, 2024 |title=Breaking News: ANC issues deadline to DA for new cabinet proposals amid deadlock |url=https://www.iol.co.za/news/politics/breaking-news-anc-issues-deadline-to-da-for-new-cabinet-proposals-amid-deadlock-d64241a9-6998-4643-b1e7-cb1aab56b0de |work=[[Independent Online]]}}</ref>

On 30 June, Ramaphosa unveiled his new 32-member cabinet, with the ANC holding 20 posts, the DA holding six, and the remainder being held by other coalition members. John Steenhuisen was appointed as agriculture minister, while the leaders of four other parties were also named ministers.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://apnews.com/article/south-africa-coalition-cabinet-president-757b0f886812371085699c957ae1607a |title=South African parties agree on Cabinet positions, sealing deal on new coalition government |access-date=1 July 2024 |work=Associated Press}}</ref> In addition, 42 deputy ministers were named from among the coalition parties.

In the 6th Parliament's final session, the National Assembly voted to establish the [[Electoral Reform Consultation Panel]] to independently investigate and recommend potential reforms to South Africa's electoral system.<ref>{{Cite web |date=14 May 2024 |title=ANNOUNCEMENTS, TABLINGS AND COMMITTEE REPORTS |url=https://www.parliament.gov.za/storage/app/media/Docs/atc/51295b9b-a89c-4ff7-bc4f-2d60ad978ee1.pdf |access-date=31 July 2024 |website=Parliament of South Africa}}</ref> The [[Electoral Reform Consultation Panel]] published their final report in August 2025 recommending a change to the electoral system to be used in the 2029 election.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Electoral Reform Consultation Panel |title=Electoral Reform Consultation Panel Final Report |url=https://www.dha.gov.za/images/ecrp/ERCP_Original_Report.pdf}}</ref>

=== Allegations of misconduct ===
On 1 June, [[Jacob Zuma]] said that the MK was seeking to have the announcement of official results legally halted pending investigations over allegations of vote-rigging raised by the party, with MK officials citing possible tampering of the Independent Electoral Commission's computer system following glitches earlier that day. The IEC said it had received 579 objections from both voters and political parties regarding the election results,<ref>{{Cite news |date=2 June 2024 |title=Former South Africa leader Zuma threatens legal action over allegations of election irregularities |url=https://apnews.com/article/south-africa-elections-zuma-objections-ead32e32fb549ef56574b0229ada6a05 |access-date=2 June 2024 |work=[[Associated Press]]|archive-date=1 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240601222033/https://apnews.com/article/south-africa-elections-zuma-objections-ead32e32fb549ef56574b0229ada6a05 |url-status=live }}</ref> and ordered recounts in 24 cases.<ref name="f24anc">{{Cite news |date=2 June 2024 |title=South Africa's ANC to enter coalition talks after landmark election |url=https://www.france24.com/en/africa/20240602-south-africa-s-anc-to-enter-coalition-talks-after-landmark-election |access-date=2 June 2024 |work=[[France 24]]}}</ref> Police Minister [[Bheki Cele]] warned that authorities would not tolerate "threats of instability in order to register objections or concerns about the electoral processes".<ref>{{Cite news |date=3 June 2024 |title=South Africa president faces up to poor poll result |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cx99vww50y5o |access-date=3 June 2024 |publisher=[[BBC]]|archive-date=2 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240602231938/https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cx99vww50y5o |url-status=live }}</ref>

The MK later filed a petition asking the Constitutional Court to halt the opening session of the new National Assembly on 14 June,<ref>{{cite news| title=South African political party led by Zuma seeks to halt parliament election of country's president |date=11 June 2024 |url=https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/south-african-political-party-led-zuma-seeks-halt-111027490 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240611231843/https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/south-african-political-party-led-zuma-seeks-halt-111027490 |archive-date=11 June 2024 |access-date=12 June 2024}}</ref> adding that it would boycott the meeting.<ref>{{cite news |title=Zuma's party seeks to halt parliament election of country's president |date=12 June 2024 |url=https://www.africanews.com/2024/06/12/zumas-party-seeks-to-halt-parliament-election-of-countrys-president/ |work=Africanews |access-date=12 June 2024 |archive-date=12 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240612085150/https://www.africanews.com/2024/06/12/zumas-party-seeks-to-halt-parliament-election-of-countrys-president/ |url-status=live }}</ref> On 13 June, the Constitutional Court dismissed the petition, allowing the session to proceed.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://abcnews.go.com/Business/wireStory/south-africa-political-parties-cobble-unity-government-deadline-111083179 |title=South Africa political parties cobble together unity government as deadline to elect president looms |website=ABC News |access-date=13 June 2024 |archive-date=13 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240613141022/https://abcnews.go.com/Business/wireStory/south-africa-political-parties-cobble-unity-government-deadline-111083179 |url-status=live }}</ref> The MK continued to boycott parliamentary proceedings until 26 June, when its MPs finally took their oath as members of the National Assembly.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.africanews.com/2024/06/26/south-africa-mk-party-mps-end-boycott-and-take-oath/ |title=South Africa: MK Party MPs end boycott and take oath |website=[[Africanews]] |date=26 June 2024 |access-date=26 June 2024 }}</ref>

{{Politics of Albania}}

Parliamentary elections were held in [[Albania]] on 11 May 2025 to elect the 140 members of [[Parliament of Albania|Parliament]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Si |first=Nen |date=2024-12-05 |title=President Begaj decrees the date of 2025 parliamentary elections |url=https://euronews.al/en/president-begaj-decrees-the-date-of-2025-parliamentary-elections/ |access-date=2025-10-26 |website=Euronews Albania |language=en-US}}</ref> They resulted in a fourth consecutive victory for the ruling [[Socialist Party of Albania|Socialist Party]] (PS) led by Prime Minister [[Edi Rama]],<ref>{{cite web | url=https://iemis.kqz.gov.al/results2025/?lang=AL&v1=ALL | title=Rezultatet | website=Komisioni Qendror i Zgjedhjeve }}</ref> which increased its majority in parliament, with a promise of attaining [[Accession of Albania to the European Union|European Union membership for Albania]] by 2030.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-13 |title=Albania: Rama wins parliamentary elections with promise of accession by 2030. |url=https://table.media/en/https/tablemedia/europe/news/albania-rama-wins-parliamentary-elections-with-promise-of-accession-by-2030/ |access-date=2025-05-14 |website=Table.Media |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-13 |title=What Rama's triumph in Albanian elections means for the EU|website=New Union Post |url=https://newunionpost.eu/2025/05/13/edi-rama-triumph-elections-albania-eu/ |access-date=2025-05-14 |language=en-GB}}</ref>

The elections took place against a backdrop of scandals during the party's [[Rama III Government|previous term]], including the arrest of [[Tirana]] mayor [[Erion Veliaj]],<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.panorama.com.al/lajm-i-fundit-arrestohet-erion-veliaj/ | title=Arrestohet kryebashkiaku i Tiranës, Erion Veliaj|website=Panorama }}</ref> [[Kukës]] mayor [[Safet Gjici]],<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.reporter.al/2024/06/24/apeli-ndryshon-vendimin-e-gjicit-denohet-per-korrupsion/ | title=Apeli ndryshon vendimin e Gjicit, dënohet për korrupsion |website=Reporter | date=24 June 2024 }}</ref> the [[Albanian incinerators scandal|incinerator scandal]],<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.cna.al/editorial/afera-e-inceneratoreve-pertej-korrupsionit-i384057 | title=Afera e inceneratorëve përtej korrupsionit | website=CNA | date=14 December 2023 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.reporter.al/2024/07/16/spak-ne-aferen-e-inceneratorit-te-tiranes-u-pastruan-20-milion-euro/ | website=Reporter | title=SPAK: Në aferën e inceneratorit të Tiranës u pastruan 20 milionë euro | date=16 July 2024 }}</ref> and the 5D Affair.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.kapitali.al/investigimi-kompania-5d-construction-aferat-korruptive-ne-bashkine-e-tiranes/ | title=Investigimi/ Kompania '5D Construction', aferat korruptive në bashkinë e Tiranës|website=Kapitali }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.cna.al/aktualitet/afera-5d-drejtoret-hajdute-te-veliajt-moren-qindra-mijera-euro-i405552 | title=Afera "5D"/ Drejtorët hajdutë të Veliajt morën qindra mijëra euro | date=10 August 2024 |website=CNA}}</ref> Opposition leader and leader of the [[Democratic Party of Albania|Democratic Party]] [[Sali Berisha]] accused PS of pressure, fraud and vote-buying following the elections.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-12 |title=Berisha: Kriteret e zgjedhjeve janë shkelur në mënyrën më të pamëshirë! PD do bëjë vlerësimin e saj kur të numërohet edhe vota e fundit. Vetëm ai që është sipër mund të ndalojë PD-në pa bërë gjithçka për mbrojtjen e votës së shqiptarëve - Partia Demokratike e Shqipërisë |url=https://pd.al/berisha-kriteret-e-zgjedhjeve-jane-shkelur-ne-menyren-me-te-pameshire-pd-do-beje-vleresimin-e-saj-kur-te-numerohet-edhe-vota-e-fundit-vetem-ai-qe-eshte-siper-mund-te-ndaloje-pd-ne-pa-bere-gjithcka/ |access-date=2025-05-14 |website=pd.al |language=sq}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-14 |title=Albania PM's Socialist Party scores large victory in parliamentary elections |url=https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20250514-albania-socialist-parliamentary-elections |access-date=2025-05-14 |website=France 24 |language=en}}</ref> Other allegations included [[vote buying]] through financial incentives and public sector jobs,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-13 |title=VIDEO - SYRI TV/ Klientët e Ramës, mbi 10 miliarda euro orët e fundit të fushatës |url=https://www.syri.net/politike/787753/syri-tv-klientet-e-rames-mbi-10-miliarda-euro-oret-e-fundit-te-fushates/ |access-date=2025-05-14 |website=Syri |language=sq-AL}}</ref> misuse of state resources,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-13 |title=Deklarata - BE hedh në erë zgjedhjet në Shqipëri: Garë jo e barabartë! PS përdori shtetin... |url=https://www.syri.net/politike/787792/be-hedh-ne-ere-zgjedhjet-ne-shqiperi-gare-jo-e-barabarte-ps-perdori-shtetin/ |access-date=2025-05-14 |website=Syri |language=sq-AL}}</ref> and a patronage system in which PS activists monitored voters near polling stations.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-11 |title=VIDEO - Skenë krimi në Tiranë, Syri Tv kap mat patronazhistët te 'rruga e Kosovarëve'! Ikin me vrap si 'minj', 'zhdukin' dhe provat |url=https://www.syri.net/politike/787341/skene-krimi-ne-tirane-syri-tv-kap-mat-patronazhistet-te-rruga-e-kosovareve-ikin-me-vrap-si-minj-zhdukin-dhe-provat/ |access-date=2025-05-14 |website=Syri |language=sq-AL}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-12 |title=Pyetjet e gazetarëve - Patronazhistët/ Drejtuesja e misionit të OSBE: Kishte presion ndaj administratës, për policinë nuk di çfarë të them... |url=https://www.syri.net/politike/787549/patronazhistet-drejtuesja-e-misionit-te-osbe-kishte-presion-ndaj-administrates-per-policine-nuk-di-cfare-te-them/ |access-date=2025-05-14 |website=Syri |language=sq-AL}}</ref>

[[OSCE]]'s observation mission had a mixed reaction, saying the elections were competitive and well-run but lacked a level playing field including self-censorship by journalists, and a confrontational and polarizing campaign, with the two main political parties using divisive language and attempting to unduly influence voters. The elections were marked by widespread misuse of public resources and institutional power by the ruling party PS, while numerous reports of pressure on public employees and other voters as well as cases of intimidation were of concern.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Albania's parliamentary elections competitive and well run but lacked level playing field, international observers say |url=https://www.osce.org/odihr/elections/590610 |access-date=2025-05-14 |website=OSCE |language=en}}</ref>

The elections also marked the first time that Albanian citizens living abroad were [[Non-resident citizen voting|allowed to vote]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=nc |first=fra |date=2024-07-24 |title=Votimi në Komisionin e Ligjeve, miratohet vota e diasporës |url=https://euronews.al/votimi-ne-komisionin-e-ligjeve-miratohet-vota-e-diaspores/ |access-date=2025-05-14 |website=Euronews Albania |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Background==
In the [[2021 Albanian parliamentary election|2021 parliamentary elections]], the [[Socialist Party of Albania|Socialist Party]] (PS) won 74 of the 140 seats in the parliament, resulting in [[Edi Rama]] being re-elected as Prime Minister. The PD-AN alliance, which was led by the centre-right [[Democratic Party of Albania|Democrats]] and added several smaller parties to its coalition in the 2021 election, increased their seat-share from 43 to 59 seats.<ref>{{cite web |last=Kalemaj |first=Ilir |publisher=Groupe d'Études Géopolitiques (GEG) |title=Parliamentary Election in Albania, 25 April 2021 |url=https://geopolitique.eu/en/articles/parliamentary-election-in-albania-25-april-2021/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240714170739/https://geopolitique.eu/en/articles/parliamentary-election-in-albania-25-april-2021/ |archive-date=14 July 2024 |date=25 April 2021 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Rüttershoff">{{cite web |last=Rüttershoff |first=Tobias |publisher=[[Konrad Adenauer Foundation]] (KAS) |title=Albania Has Voted |url=https://www.kas.de/en/country-reports/detail/-/content/albania-has-voted |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220625211807/https://www.kas.de/en/country-reports/detail/-/content/albania-has-voted |archive-date=25 June 2022 |date=29 April 2021 |url-status=live}}</ref>

During the same period, President [[Ilir Meta]] faced widespread allegations of violating the constitution, particularly in his intervention in the electoral process and the overt partisan stance against the PS he adopted during the 2021 elections.<ref>{{cite web |publisher=Deutsche Welle (DW) |title=Albania parliament impeaches President Meta |url=https://www.dw.com/en/albania-parliament-impeaches-president-ilir-meta-removes-him-from-office/a-57830015 |access-date=15 November 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210609145317/https://www.dw.com/en/albania-parliament-impeaches-president-ilir-meta-removes-him-from-office/a-57830015 |archive-date=9 June 2021 |date=9 June 2021}}</ref> In June 2021, the parliament initiated impeachment proceedings against Meta, accusing him of undermining the neutrality of the presidency.<ref>{{cite web |publisher=Euronews Albania |title=Parliament votes in favor of impeaching President Ilir Meta |url=https://euronews.al/en/parliament-votes-today-on-president-metas-impeachment-after-allegations-of-16-constitutional-violations/ === Corruption and governance context ===
The election was held after three consecutive Socialist Party mandates under [[Edi Rama]], whose governments had presented [[Accession of Albania to the European Union|EU accession]] as the central strategic objective while also facing persistent domestic and international scrutiny over corruption, public procurement and the relationship between state institutions and party power. In its 2025 enlargement report, the [[European Commission]] assessed that Albania's parliamentary elections were professionally conducted but noted shortcomings including an unequal playing field and abuse of public resources.<ref name="ECAlbaniaReport2025">{{cite web |date=4 November 2025 |title=Albania 2025 Report |url=https://enlargement.ec.europa.eu/document/download/fe9138b7-90fe-4277-a12c-3a03f6d1957f_en?filename=albania-report-2025.pdf |publisher=[[European Commission]] |format=PDF |access-date=8 July 2026}}</ref> The [[OSCE Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights]] (ODIHR) later concluded that the ruling party benefited from administrative resources and institutional leverage, blurring the line between state and party, while also noting allegations of pressure on public employees, intimidation of opposition supporters, patronage networks, vote buying and the influence of criminal elements in some areas.<ref name="ODIHRFinal2025">{{cite web |date=23 October 2025 |title=Albania, Parliamentary Elections, 11 May 2025: Final Report |url=https://odihr.osce.org/sites/default/files/documents/official_documents/2026/05/ALB%20Parliamentary%202025%20Final%20Report_23.10.2025.pdf |publisher=[[OSCE Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights]] |format=PDF |access-date=8 July 2026}}</ref>

Several high-profile corruption cases involving Socialist Party officials or figures associated with the governing majority shaped the pre-election environment. In February 2025, Tirana mayor [[Erion Veliaj]], a senior Socialist Party figure and former minister in Rama's cabinet, was arrested after the Special Prosecution against Corruption and Organized Crime (SPAK) accused him of corruption, money laundering and related offences. Prosecutors alleged that Veliaj and his wife obtained over €1 million in illicit income through a scheme involving public contracts, permits, non-governmental organizations and private companies; Veliaj denied wrongdoing and called the case politically motivated.<ref name="OCCRPVeliaj2025">{{cite web |last=Cela |first=Lindita |date=11 February 2025 |title=Tirana Mayor Arrested in €1M Corruption, Fraud Scandal |url=https://www.occrp.org/en/news/tirana-mayor-arrested-in-eur1m-corruption-fraud-scandal |website=[[Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project]] |access-date=8 July 2026}}</ref><ref name="APVeliaj2025">{{cite news |last=Semini |first=Llazar |date=10 February 2025 |title=An Albanian court orders the capital's mayor into custody and accuses him of corruption |url=https://apnews.com/article/albania-tirana-mayor-corruption-arrest-98d0fa2e987eaf57b9e41123c832e8dc |work=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=8 July 2026}}</ref> The case was politically sensitive because Veliaj governed the capital city, had been considered a possible successor to Rama within the Socialist Party, and was arrested three months before election day.

The opposition used Veliaj's arrest, the earlier [[Albanian incinerators scandal]], the [[Kukës]] case involving former Socialist mayor [[Safet Gjici]], and the so-called 5D affair in Tirana Municipality to portray the Socialist Party as a clientelist network. The governing party rejected opposition claims that the election was illegitimate and argued that the work of SPAK demonstrated the independence of justice reform. International observers did not adopt the opposition's terminology, but the ODIHR final report stated that abuses of office and public resources were often left unsanctioned because the Complaints and Sanctions Commission applied a narrow interpretation of rules on administrative resources.<ref name="ODIHRFinal2025" />

Corruption allegations continued after the election. In December 2025, SPAK indicted Deputy Prime Minister and infrastructure minister [[Belinda Balluku]], a close ally of Rama, on suspicion of interfering in major infrastructure tenders; Balluku denied wrongdoing.<ref name="ReutersBallukuProbe2026">{{cite news |date=19 February 2026 |title=The probe into corruption at the heart of Albania's government |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/probe-into-corruption-heart-albanias-government-2026-02-19/ |work=[[Reuters]] |access-date=8 July 2026}}</ref> Reuters reported that the allegations concerned two construction contracts from 2021 worth more than €200 million and that the scandal, together with a string of corruption cases, fueled protests and posed a challenge to Rama's fourth mandate and Albania's EU ambitions.<ref name="ReutersBallukuProbe2026" /> Rama initially stood by Balluku, but dismissed her in February 2026 after the investigation intensified and opposition protests continued.<ref name="ReutersBallukuFired2026">{{cite news |date=26 February 2026 |title=Albanian PM fires deputy as corruption investigation heats up |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/albanian-pm-fires-deputy-corruption-investigation-heats-up-2026-02-26/ |work=[[Reuters]] |access-date=8 July 2026}}</ref>

==Electoral system==
The electoral system of Albania is constructed upon the principles defined in the [[Constitution of Albania|constitution]] and the electoral code. As a [[parliamentary republic]], Albania implements a regional [[proportional representation]] method that allocates seats in the [[Parliament of Albania|parliament]] according to the proportion of votes garnered by political parties in a [[multi-party system]].{{sfn|OSCE|1998|p=1|loc=Article 1}}{{sfn|OSCE|1998|p=12|loc=Article 64}}{{sfn|OSCE|2021|p=6}} The parliament is composed of 140 representatives with a term of four years.{{sfn|OSCE|1998|p=12|loc=Article 64}} The constitution codifies substantial democratic principles, stipulating that voting rights are equal, free, and conducted through [[secret ballot]].{{sfn|OSCE|1998|p=9|loc=Article 45}}{{sfn|OSCE|1998|p=14|loc=Article 73}} All citizens of Albania, upon reaching the age of 18 and having not been deprived of voting rights, are permitted to participate in elections.{{sfn|OSCE|1998|p=8|loc=Article 45}} The electoral code also establishes comprehensive procedures for voter registration, ensuring that all eligible citizens can participate fully in the process. The allocation of representatives in the parliament is based on population size within 12 electoral districts, which correspond to the [[Counties of Albania|first-level administrative regions (counties)]] of Albania.{{sfn|OSCE|2021|p=6}} The [[D'Hondt method]] is employed for seat distribution to parties, contingent upon an [[electoral threshold]] of 1%.{{sfn|OSCE|2021|p=6}}

In the 2025 election, 46 seats were filled by politicians on [[closed list]]s and one-third of the politicians elected to the parliament [[reserved seats|needed to be women]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://albaniantimes.al/electoral-lists-divide-power-between-party-leaders-and-voters-in-albanias-upcoming-elections/ |title=Electoral lists divide power between party leaders and voters in Albania's upcoming elections |work=Albanian Times|date=22 January 2025 }}</ref>

=== Election date ===
According to the constitution, parliamentary elections in Albania are required to be conducted no later than 60 days after and no earlier than 30 days prior to the expiration of the parliament's mandate.{{sfn|OSCE|1998|p=12|loc=Article 64}} On 11 October 2024, commissioner [[Ilirjan Celibashi]] of the {{lang|sq|[[Central Election Commission (Albania)|Komisioni Qendror i Zgjedhjeve]]|i=no}} (KQZ) recommended the period between 20 April and 11 May 2025, as the most appropriate timeframe for the upcoming parliamentary elections.<ref>{{cite web |work=Zëri |title=Datat për zgjedhjet 2025/ Celibashi, letër partive: S'kemi kohë për votim elektronik, e bëjmë vetëm në Elbasan e Durrës! |url=https://zeri.ai/politike-zbulohen-datat-per-zgjedhjet-2025-celibashi-leter-partive-per-votimin-elektronik-nuk-kemi-kohe-mund-te-realizoh-i213087 |access-date=15 November 2024 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20241115111701/https://zeri.ai/politike-zbulohen-datat-per-zgjedhjet-2025-celibashi-leter-partive-per-votimin-elektronik-nuk-kemi-kohe-mund-te-realizoh-i213087 |archive-date=15 November 2024 |location=Tirana |language=sq |date=11 October 2024 |url-status=live}}</ref> On 11 November 2024, President [[Bajram Begaj]] procedurally initiated consultations to determine the election date for the elections, inviting representatives from the Coalition for Reforms, Integration, and Consolidated Institutions (KRIIK) to the {{lang|sq|[[Presidential Office Building, Tirana|Presidenca]]|i=no}}.<ref>{{cite web |publisher=[[ABC News (Albania)|ABC News]] |title=Presidenti Begaj takim me përfaqësues të Kriik: Shoqëria civile të angazhohet në mbikëqyrjen e zgjedhjeve |url=https://abcnews.al/presidenti-begaj-takim-me-perfaqesues-te-kriik-shoqeria-civile-te-angazhohet-ne-mbikeqyrjen-e-zgjedhjeve/ |access-date=15 November 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241112044419/https://abcnews.al/presidenti-begaj-takim-me-perfaqesues-te-kriik-shoqeria-civile-te-angazhohet-ne-mbikeqyrjen-e-zgjedhjeve/ |archive-date=12 November 2024 |language=sq |date=11 November 2024 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Following on 19 November, Begaj held the first round of consultations with leaders of smaller opposition parties, who proposed 4 May as the most suitable election date.<ref>{{cite web |work=Zëri |title=Data e zgjedhjeve/ Presidenti Begaj nis nesër konsultimet me partitë politike |url=https://zeri.ai/politike-data-e-zgjedhjeve-presidenti-begaj-nis-neser-konsultimet-me-partite-politike-i215467 |access-date=29 November 2024 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20241129113512/https://zeri.ai/politike-data-e-zgjedhjeve-presidenti-begaj-nis-neser-konsultimet-me-partite-politike-i215467 |archive-date=29 November 2024 |location=Tirana |language=sq |date=19 November 2024 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="SHQ20November">{{cite web |work=Shqiptarja |title=Data e zgjedhjeve 2025/ Presidenti nis takimet me partitë! 'Të vegjlit' propozojnë 4 majin! Begaj: Hapi i parë i një procesi që duhet të jetë model |url=https://shqiptarja.com/lajm/begaj-nis-konsultimet-per-daten-e-zgjedhjeve-2025-pres-sot-pr-pbdnj-pdiu-e-lzhk |access-date=29 November 2024 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20241129113543/https://shqiptarja.com/lajm/begaj-nis-konsultimet-per-daten-e-zgjedhjeve-2025-pres-sot-pr-pbdnj-pdiu-e-lzhk |archive-date=29 November 2024 |location=Tirana |language=sq |date=20 November 2024 |url-status=live}}</ref> This suggestion was made in light of the anticipated [[European Political Community]] Summit in Tirana on 9 May, with leaders arguing that holding elections before the summit would prevent potential electoral manipulation.<ref name="SHQ20November"/> Begaj described the consultations as the beginning of a transparent and constructive electoral process.<ref name="SHQ20November"/> He emphasised that the decision regarding the election date should be based on the best interests of voters, following a balanced, open debate with input from a wide range of political and institutional actors.<ref>{{cite web |publisher=Euronews Albania |title=Data e zgjedhjeve, Begaj: Proces konsultash dhe llogaridhënie për aktorët politikë |url=https://euronews.al/data-e-zgjedhjeve-begaj-proces-konsultash-dhe-llogaridhenie-per-aktoret-politike/ |access-date=29 November 2024 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20241129114114/https://euronews.al/data-e-zgjedhjeve-begaj-proces-konsultash-dhe-llogaridhenie-per-aktoret-politike/ |archive-date=29 November 2024 |language=sq |date=20 November 2024 |url-status=live}}</ref> The Democratic Party declined to participate in consultations with Begaj. The Freedom Party accepted the invitation, with Tedi Blushi and Erisa Xhixho requesting that the President decree any election date permitted by the Electoral Code, except the one proposed by [[Taulant Balla]] of the Socialist Party. === Amendments ===
On 26 July 2024, the parliament approved the amendments to the new electoral code, which included provisions for [[Albanian diaspora|diaspora]] [[Non-resident citizen voting|voting]] and the allocation of mandates. A significant focus centered on the formula employed for candidate lists, which was no longer entirely open; instead, one-third was designated as closed and subject to the discretion of the party leader, thereby exempting it from preferential voting. Furthermore, the new regulations stipulated that one out of every three candidates elected from the open list was required to be a woman, thereby reflecting a commitment to enhancing gender representation within the electoral framework.<ref name="Shqiptarja">{{cite web |work=Shqiptarja |title=106 vota pro, PS-PD miratojnë ndryshimet në Kodin Zgjedhor: Lista të hapura në 2/3 dhe votë të diasporës!
