[[Parliamentary elections in Slovenia|Parliamentary elections]] were held in [[Slovenia]] on 24 April 2022 to elect all 90 [[Member of parliament|members]] of the [[National Assembly (Slovenia)|National Assembly]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Slovenia's president to set general election for April 24|url=https://abcnews.go.com/Business/wireStory/slovenias-president-set-general-election-april-24-82371426|access-date=2022-01-22|website=ABC News|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Opposition Slovenian liberal party on course for landslide win, say exit polls|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2022/apr/24/opposition-slovenian-liberal-party-on-course-for-landslide-win-say-exit-polls|access-date=2022-04-24|website=The Guardian|date=24 April 2022|language=en}}</ref>

The ruling [[Slovenian Democratic Party]] (SDS), led by [[Prime Minister of Slovenia|prime minister]] [[Janez Janša]], conceded and was defeated by [[Robert Golob]] and his [[Freedom Movement (Slovenia)|Freedom Movement]] (GS). [[New Slovenia]] (NSi) placed third, and was followed by the [[Social Democrats (Slovenia)|Social Democrats]] (SD) and [[The Left (Slovenia)|The Left]] (Levica), both of which suffered some losses. The [[Democratic Party of Pensioners of Slovenia]], [[Party of Alenka Bratušek]], [[Slovenian National Party]] and the [[List of Marjan Šarec]] fell below the 4% [[electoral threshold]] and won no seats. Turnout stood at 70%, a substantial increase compared to previous two elections (52.63% in 2018 and 51.71% in 2014).<ref>{{Cite news |last=Lihtenvalner |first=Katja |date=2022-04-24 |title=Slovenia's populist PM loses election to environmentalist party-election commission |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/slovenias-populist-pm-faces-close-election-race-against-environmentalist-party-2022-04-23/ |access-date=2022-04-24}}</ref> Internationally, the election has been described  as a defeat for Janša and [[right-wing populism]], Janša being a supporter of former US president [[Donald Trump]] and an ally of Hungary's Prime Minister [[Viktor Orbán]].<ref name="MMCtujina"/><ref name="Guardian"/>

Following the election, the Freedom Movement formed a three-party [[Centre-left politics|centre-left]] [[coalition government]] with the Social Democrats and The Left, with Robert Golob heading the [[15th Government of Slovenia|15th Government]] as the next [[Prime Minister of Slovenia|prime minister]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Krašovec |first=Alenka |date=2023 |title=Slovenia: Political Developments and Data in 2022: A Year of Elections and Political Changes |url=https://ejpr.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/2047-8852.12409 |journal=European Journal of Political Research Political Data Yearbook |language=en |doi=10.1111/2047-8852.12409 |issn=2047-8844|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Electoral system ==
The 90 members of the [[National Assembly (Slovenia)|National Assembly]] are elected through two methods. Eighty-eight seats are elected by [[open list]] [[proportional representation]] in eight 11-seat [[Constituencies in Slovenia|constituencies]] and seats, with seats allocated to parties at the constituency level using the [[Droop quota]].

Elected Deputies are identified by ranking all of a party's candidates in a constituency based on the percentage of votes they received in their respective districts. Seats that remain unallocated are then allocated to the parties at the national level using the [[D'Hondt method]], with an electoral threshold of 4%.<ref name=":2">[http://www.dvk-rs.si/index.php/en/elections/national-assembly-of-the-republic-of-slovenia National Assembly of the Republic of Slovenia] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200913023210/http://www.dvk-rs.si/index.php/en/elections/national-assembly-of-the-republic-of-slovenia |date=2020-09-13 }} State Election Commission</ref> 

Although the country is divided into 88 electoral districts, deputies are not elected from all 88 districts. In practice, more than one deputy is elected in some districts, resulting in other districts having no elected deputy. For instance, 21 of the 88 electoral districts had no elected deputy in the 2014 elections.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.vecer.com/imamo-sploh-legalno-volilno-zakonodajo-za-drzavni-zbor-6343369|title=Imamo sploh legalno volilno zakonodajo za državni zbor?|work=Časnik Večer d.o.o.|access-date=2018-03-18|language=sl-si|archive-date=2018-03-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180319004313/https://www.vecer.com/imamo-sploh-legalno-volilno-zakonodajo-za-drzavni-zbor-6343369|url-status=live}}</ref> 

Parties must ensure that at least 35% of their candidate lists represent each gender, except in cases where a list contains only three candidates, in which case at least one candidate of each gender is required.<ref>[http://www.ipu.org/parline-e/reports/2287_B.htm Electoral system] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161121044338/http://www.ipu.org/parline-e/reports/2287_B.htm |date=2016-11-21 }} IPU</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://pisrs.si/|title=Zakon o volitvah v državni zbor (ZVDZ)|website=pisrs|access-date=2018-03-17|archive-date=2007-02-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070207222422/http://pisrs.si/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Two additional deputies are elected by the [[Istrian Italians|Italian]] and [[Hungarians in Slovenia|Hungarian]] minorities using [[plurality voting]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dvk-rs.si/index.php/si/strani/navodila-in-rokovnik-dz-2018|title=Navodila in rokovnik - DZ 2018 {{!}} Državna volilna komisija|website=Državna volilna komisija|access-date=2018-06-16|archive-date=2018-03-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180317044257/http://www.dvk-rs.si/index.php/si/strani/navodila-in-rokovnik-dz-2018|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=":2" />

== Campaign ==
[[President of Slovenia|President]] [[Borut Pahor]] signed a decree for the election to be held on 24 April 2022. Pahor explained that he will nominate a prime minister based on the composition of the parliament, requesting leaders of parliamentary groups to put forward at least 46 signatures.<ref>{{Cite web |title=President Pahor to Sign Decree for General Election on 24 April |url=https://www.total-slovenia-news.com/politics/9564-president-pahor-to-sign-decree-for-general-election-on-24-april |access-date=2022-02-11 |website=www.total-slovenia-news.com |language=en-gb}}</ref> [[Prime Minister of Slovenia|Prime Minister]] [[Janez Janša]] tested positive for [[COVID-19]] on the same day.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Predsednik vlade Janez Janša okužen s koronavirusom {{!}} GOV.SI |url=https://www.gov.si/novice/2022-02-09-predsednik-vlade-janez-jansa-okuzen-s-koronavirusom/ |access-date=2022-02-11 |website=Portal GOV.SI |language=sl}}</ref>

Following the decision of the [[European Court of Human Rights|ECtHR]] in ''The Committee for the organization and registration of the Romanian Communist Party v. Romania'' case in which the ECtHR confirmed Romania's decision to refuse to register a political party that did not distance itself from the former communist regime, [[Vili Kovačič]] asked the [[Constitutional Court of Slovenia|Constitutional Court]] to decide on the constitutionality of [[The Left (Slovenia)|The Left]]'s program and actions of The Left and [[Social Democrats (Slovenia)|Social Democrats]]. The latter is the legal successor of the [[League of Communists of Slovenia]].<ref>{{Cite journal|date=2009-05-01|title=Dissenting Opinion of Constitutional Court of Ukraine Justice P.M. Tkachuk Regarding the Decision of the Constitutional Court of Ukraine in the Matter of the Constitutional Petition of the Ministry of Justice of Ukraine Regarding the Official Interpretation of the Provisions of Article 11.6 of the Law of Ukraine "On Political Parties in Ukraine" (Case of the Creation and Registration of Party Organizations)|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.2753/rsd1061-0014440313|journal=Statutes and Decisions|volume=44|issue=3|pages=96–100|doi=10.2753/rsd1061-0014440313|issn=1061-0014|url-access=subscription}}</ref> The Constitutional Court rejected [[Vili Kovačič]]'s proposal to decide on constitutionality of [[The Left (Slovenia)|The Left]]'s program and actions of The Left and [[Social Democrats (Slovenia)|Social Democrats]] as groundless.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ustavno sodišče je zavrnilo pobudo za oceno protiustavnosti Levice in SD-ja |url=https://www.rtvslo.si/slovenija/ustavno-sodisce-je-zavrnilo-pobudo-za-oceno-protiustavnosti-levice-in-sd-ja/616814 |access-date=2022-03-24 |website=RTVSLO.si |language=sl}}</ref>

[[Aleksandra Pivec]] submitted 1500 signatures to support [[Our Country (Slovenia)|Our Country]]'s candidate lists. She also stated that MPs Branko Simonovič and Ivan Hršak of [[Democratic Party of Pensioners of Slovenia|DeSUS]] may join her party.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Naša dežela s 1500 podpisi volivcev vstopa v volilno tekmo|url=https://www.rtvslo.si/slovenija/nasa-dezela-s-1500-podpisi-volivcev-vstopa-v-volilno-tekmo/612534|access-date=2022-02-15|website=RTVSLO.si|language=sl}}</ref> DeSUS and [[Liberal Democrats (Slovenia)|LIDE]] decided to form a joint candidate lists for the election.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Uradno: DeSUS in LIDE gresta na volitve s skupno kandidatno listo|url=https://www.rtvslo.si/slovenija/uradno-desus-in-lide-gresta-na-volitve-s-skupno-kandidatno-listo/612520|access-date=2022-02-15|website=RTVSLO.si|language=sl}}</ref> [[Karl Erjavec]], former leader of DeSUS, said in an interview that DeSUS is a failed party and that connecting with LIDE will not have a positive effect in the election. He was critical of the DeSUS MPs and [[Igor Zorčič]], who did not support the vote of no confidence after which Erjavec would become prime minister. He added, that he might re-enter politics, but not through DeSUS, and that he has several offers from other parties.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Vsak dan prvi - 24ur.com|url=https://www.24ur.com/novice/slovenija/erjavec-desus-je-propadla-stranka-k-njej-se-ne-mislim-vrniti.html|access-date=2022-02-15|website=www.24ur.com}}</ref> The LIDE party authorized party president [[Igor Zorčič]] to form a joint list of candidates with DeSUS and the [[Liberal Democracy of Slovenia|LDS]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Svet stranke LIDE pooblastil Zorčiča za oblikovanje skupne liste kandidatov |url=https://www.rtvslo.si/slovenija/preberite-tudi/svet-stranke-lide-pooblastil-zorcica-za-oblikovanje-skupne-liste-kandidatov/612964 |access-date=2022-02-21 |website=RTVSLO.si |language=sl}}</ref> Later LIDE announced that it would not participate in the election. DeSUS did not want broader coalition with other parties and therefore rejected an agreement offered by LIDE. LIDE's leader [[Igor Zorčič]] stated that party will skip parliamentary election and focus on presidential and local elections, which will be held later this year.<ref>{{Cite web |title=LIDE ne bo šel na državnozborske volitve |url=https://www.rtvslo.si/slovenija/lide-ne-bo-sel-na-drzavnozborske-volitve/614043 |access-date=2022-02-28 |website=RTVSLO.si |language=sl}}</ref> DeSUS announced that it will run in the elections on its own after refusing to form a joint list with the LIDE.<ref>{{Cite web |title=DeSUS gre samostojno na volitve |url=https://www.rtvslo.si/slovenija/desus-gre-samostojno-na-volitve/614170 |access-date=2022-03-01 |website=RTVSLO.si |language=sl}}</ref>
 
[[The Commission for the Prevention of Corruption of the Republic of Slovenia|The Commission for the Prevention of Corruption]] announced that it had not found any violations regarding the vacations of [[Prime Minister of Slovenia|Prime Minister]] [[Janez Janša]] with some businessmen and stopped the investigation.<ref>{{Cite web|title=KPK ustavila postopek v zvezi z letovanji Janeza Janše|url=https://www.24ur.com/novice/slovenija/kpk-ustavila-postopek-v-zvezi-z-letovanji-janeza-janse.html|access-date=2022-02-21|website=www.24ur.com|language=sl}}</ref> After the investigation of the procurement of protective equipment in the initial phase of the COVID-19 pandemic, [[The Commission for the Prevention of Corruption of the Republic of Slovenia|the Commission for the Prevention of Corruption]] (KPK) found a violation of the integrity by the Minister of the Economy [[Zdravko Počivalšek]]. Počivalšek stated that he will not resign and that the KPK's opinion tells more about the KPK itself.<ref>{{Cite web|title=KPK: Minister Počivalšek pri nabavi ventilatorjev kršil integriteto. Počivalšek: Imam mirno vest|url=https://www.rtvslo.si/slovenija/kpk-minister-pocivalsek-pri-nabavi-ventilatorjev-krsil-integriteto-pocivalsek-imam-mirno-vest/613427|access-date=2022-02-23|website=RTVSLO.si|language=sl}}</ref> [[Robert Golob]] found himself under police investigation after he was accused of receiving too high a salary as a CEO of the state-owned GEN-I and therefore violating the so-called "Lahkovnik" Act, which regulates the salaries of management bodies of state-owned companies.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Predvolilno: Policija preverja plačo Roberta Goloba |url=https://siol.net/novice/slovenija/policija-preverja-placo-roberta-goloba-574225 |access-date=2022-03-03 |website=siol.net |language=sl}}</ref>

Speaker [[Igor Zorčič]], former member of the [[Modern Centre Party]], founded a new party called [[Liberal Democrats (Slovenia)|Liberal Democrats]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Na politični parket stopila stranka LIDE, na kongresu za člana predsedstva izvoljen Igor Zorčič |url=https://www.rtvslo.si/slovenija/na-politicni-parket-stopila-stranka-lide-na-kongresu-za-clana-predsedstva-izvoljen-igor-zorcic/608369 |access-date=2022-02-11 |website=RTVSLO.si |language=sl}}</ref> [[Robert Golob]], former State Secretary in the Ministry of Economy in Prime Minister [[Janez Drnovšek|Drnovšek]]'s cabinet and CEO of GEN-i, was elected president of the Green Actions Party, renaming it to the [[Freedom Movement (Slovenia)|Freedom Movement]]. [[Igor Zorčič]] announced that the Liberal Democrats will not form a coalition with the [[Freedom Movement (Slovenia)|Freedom Movement]], which was a mutual decision of both parties. Allegedly, Freedom Movement's leader Golob only offered Zorčič to be a candidate on his party's candidate list, and not a joint list.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Golob in Zorčič na volitvah ne bosta sodelovala |url=https://www.24ur.com/novice/slovenija/gibanje-svoboda-in-stranka-lide.html |access-date=2022-02-17 |website=www.24ur.com |language=sl}}</ref> Whistleblower Ivan Gale became president of the ''Our Future'' party, and former European Commissioner [[Violeta Bulc]] was elected vice president.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ivan Gale bo vodil stranko Naša prihodnost z ... |url=https://siol.net/novice/slovenija/ivan-gale-na-celo-stranke-nasa-prihodnost-574875 |access-date=2022-03-13 |website=siol.net |language=sl}}</ref> Smiljan Mekicar of ''Good Country'' party confirmed that they will form a joint list with Gale's Our Future party and some other parties and lists.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dobra država in Naša prihodnost gresta na volitve s skupno listo |url=https://www.rtvslo.si/slovenija/dobra-drzava-in-nasa-prihodnost-gresta-na-volitve-s-skupno-listo/616899 |access-date=2022-03-24 |website=RTVSLO.si |language=sl}}</ref>

RTV Slovenia, the public broadcaster, rejected [[Freedom Movement (Slovenia)|Freedom Movement]]'s request to recognize them as a parliamentary party.<ref>{{Cite web |title=RTVS Golobu: Niste parlamentarna stranka |url=https://siol.net/novice/slovenija/rtvs-golobu-niste-parlamentarna-stranka-575909 |access-date=2022-03-28 |website=siol.net |language=sl}}</ref> [[Radiotelevizija Slovenija|RTV Slovenia]] recognized [[Aleksandra Pivec]]'s [[Our Country (Slovenia)|Our Country]] party as a parliamentary party, which by law allows it to participate in electoral debates with other parliamentary parties. RTV Slovenia recognized Our Country as the successor to [[Democratic Party of Pensioners of Slovenia|DeSUS]], because Aleksandra Pivec was elected president of DeSUS, but then resigned and founded a new party, which was joined by several former members of DeSUS. According to RTV Slovenia, the situation was the same as in the case of the [[Alliance of Alenka Bratušek]] before the [[2014 Slovenian parliamentary election|2014 elections]]. [[Alenka Bratušek]] was elected president of [[Positive Slovenia]], then resigned and founded a new party, which included several members of Positive Slovenia. RTV Slovenia granted the Alliance of Alenka Bratušek parliamentary status.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Presenečenje: Pivčevi priznali status parlamentarne stranke, Golobu ne |url=https://siol.net/novice/slovenija/presenecenje-pivcevi-status-parlamentarne-stranke-576006 |access-date=2022-03-28 |website=siol.net |language=sl}}</ref> Freedom Movement was granted parliamentary status after it won a suit against RTV Slovenia for political discrimination.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2022-04-06 |title=Sodišče ugodilo Gibanju Svoboda, na RTVS bo obravnavano kot parlamentarna stranka |language=sl |work=Dnevnik |url=https://www.dnevnik.si/1042986699 |access-date=2022-04-25}}</ref>

== Aftermath ==
The [[Freedom Movement (Slovenia)|Freedom Movement]] led by [[Robert Golob]], a former executive of a state-owned energy company, won 41 seats. It had campaigned on a transition to green energy, an open society and the rule of law. The [[Slovenian Democratic Party]] of incumbent prime minister [[Janez Janša]] finished second and won 27 seats. [[New Slovenia – Christian Democrats]] finished third and won 8 seats, followed by the [[Social Democrats (Slovenia)|Social Democrats]] with 7 seats and [[The Left (Slovenia)|The Left]] with 5 seats. Golob, speaking to party headquarters via video link, declared victory and thanked his celebrating supporters for the historical turnout. On the other hand, prime minister Janša addressing his supporters conceded defeat and said: "The results are what they are. Congratulations to the relative winner."<ref name="Guardian">{{Cite web |title=Opposition Slovenian liberal party on course for landslide win, say exit polls |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2022/apr/24/opposition-slovenian-liberal-party-on-course-for-landslide-win-say-exit-polls |access-date=2022-04-24 |website=The Guardian |date=24 April 2022 |language=en}}</ref> [[Luka Mesec]], the coordinator of The Left, announced that he would offer to resign as the party coordinator.<ref name="MMCrezultat">{{Cite web |date=2022-04-24 |title=Velika zmaga Gibanja Svoboda, v državni zbor še SDS, NSi, SD in Levica |url=https://www.rtvslo.si/slovenija/parlamentarne-volitve-2022/velika-zmaga-gibanja-svoboda-v-drzavni-zbor-se-sds-nsi-sd-in-levica/621056 |access-date=2022-04-25 |website=RTVSlo.si |language=sl}}</ref>

In Slovenia, political analysts commented that many people voted for Golob because he was seen as the most likely candidate to win against Janša's government, and [[tactical voting]] took place. The result came at the expense of the two opposition parties, the [[List of Marjan Šarec]] and the [[Party of Alenka Bratušek]], both of which failed to secure seats in the National Assembly.<ref name="MMCkomentar">{{Cite web |date=2022-04-24 |title="Gibanje Svoboda je posrkalo večino volivcev, ki so glasovali proti vladi" |url=https://www.rtvslo.si/slovenija/parlamentarne-volitve-2022/gibanje-svoboda-je-posrkalo-vecino-volivcev-ki-so-glasovali-proti-vladi/621087 |access-date=2022-04-25 |website=RTVSlo.si |language=sl}}</ref> Freedom Movement won the highest number of seats for a single party in the elections since the independence of Slovenia. The number of parties that won seats (five) was the smallest elected to the legislature in the same time period; for comparison, nine parties were elected in 2018. Commentators mentioned that Golob, previously a successful businessman, is a newcomer to the office, and that there are still several unknowns about the party priorities. They also mentioned that he may lack qualified people to take the offices.<ref name="MMCkomentar"/><ref name="MMCtujina">{{Cite web |date=2022-04-25 |title=Odzivi iz tujine: Slovenija obrnila hrbet desnemu populizmu |url=https://www.rtvslo.si/svet/odzivi-iz-tujine-slovenija-obrnila-hrbet-desnemu-populizmu/624421 |access-date=2022-04-25 |website=RTVSlo.si |language=sl}}</ref> Luka Lisjak Gabrijelčič of ''[[Delo (newspaper)|Delo]]'' saw the result more like a defeat for Janša than a win for Golob, and added that the election in Slovenia would be internationally seen as a footnote in the fight against [[right-wing populism]], as the world was mostly focused on the bigger election of the day, the [[2022 French presidential election]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-04-25 |title=Kronika napovedanega poraza |url=https://www.delo.si/mnenja/kolumne/kronika-napovedanega-poraza/ |access-date=2022-04-25 |website=Delo |language=sl}}</ref>

International media saw the relative victory of the Freedom Movement as a defeat of right-wing populism of Janša's government, and commented that Janša was a supporter of the former US president [[Donald Trump]] and an ally of Hungary's Prime Minister [[Viktor Orbán]].<ref name="MMCtujina"/><ref name="Guardian"/> In Croatia, the news portal Index commented that Golob embodies the values of the late Prime Minister and President [[Janez Drnovšek]], and that a scenario where a political newcomer wins the election cannot happen in Croatia.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-04-25 |title=Zašto u Hrvatskoj nije moguća izborna pobjeda nekoga poput Goloba? |url=https://www.index.hr/vijesti/clanak/zasto-u-hrvatskoj-nije-moguca-izborna-pobjeda-nekoga-poput-goloba/2359032.aspx |access-date=2022-04-25 |website=Index.hr|language=hr}}</ref>

In order to form a government, ''[[Euronews]]'' reported that Freedom Movement is expected to form a coalition with "smaller centre-left groups".<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-04-24 |title=Slovenia's Janša defeated by opposition liberal Freedom Movement |url=https://www.euronews.com/2022/04/24/slovenians-out-to-vote-with-no-single-party-projected-to-rule-without-coalition |access-date=2022-04-25 |website=euronews |language=en}}</ref> Prior to election, Golob suggested that he could cooperate with the existing opposition parties. Both Social Democrats and The Left lost seats but were considered likely coalition partners, with possible collaboration with the List of Marjan Šarec and the Party of Alenka Bratušek discussed prior to the elections as well.<ref name="MMCkomentar"/> In early reactions, Golob stated that he does not exclude working with the Slovenian Democratic Party and New Slovenia on some projects, but added that the projects requiring a constitutional majority are not the top priority at the moment.<ref name="MMCrezultat"/> After meeting with Golob two days after the election, President [[Borut Pahor]] stated that he planned to appoint a new government led by Golob in late May, with coalition talks with the Social Democrats and The Left due to start the week after the meeting.<ref>{{Cite news |date=27 April 2022 |title=Pahor says PM-designate could be proposed around 23 May |work=[[The Slovenia Times]] |agency=[[Slovenian Press Agency]] |url=https://sloveniatimes.com/pahor-says-pm-designate-could-be-proposed-around-23-may/ |url-status=live |access-date=27 April 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220427030551/https://sloveniatimes.com/pahor-says-pm-designate-could-be-proposed-around-23-may/ |archive-date=27 April 2022}}</ref>

On 11 May, Robert Golob told reporters that the Freedom Movement had agreed to form a government with both the Social Democrats and The Left, with the goal of creating a cabinet of "experienced personalities and enthusiastic experts".<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-05-11|title=Slovenia's largest party says it has agreed to form coalition government |url=https://www.euronews.com/2022/05/11/slovenia-s-largest-party-says-it-has-agreed-to-form-coalition-government |access-date=2022-05-14 |website=euronews |language=en}}</ref> On 25 May, the National Assembly voted in Robert Golob as the new [[Prime Minister of Slovenia|prime minister]], heading the [[15th Government of Slovenia]]. His cabinet ministers were later sworn in on 1 June.

members of the [[National Council (Slovakia)|National Council]]. Regular elections were scheduled to be held in 2024. However, on 15 December 2022, the [[Cabinet of Eduard Heger|government]] lost a [[no-confidence]] vote.{{cite web |last1=Janiček |first1=Karel |title=Slovak coalition government collapses after losing no-confidence vote in parliament |url=https://www.pbs.org/newshour/world/slovak-coalition-government-collapses-after-losing-no-confidence-vote-in-parliament |website=PBS |access-date=28 January 2023 |date=15 December 2022 |archive-date=8 February 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230208084503/https://www.pbs.org/newshour/world/slovak-coalition-government-collapses-after-losing-no-confidence-vote-in-parliament |url-status=live }} Subsequently, the National Council amended the Constitution so that an early election could be held on 30 September 2023.{{Cite web |last=Kahn |first=Michael |date=22 January 2023 |editor-last=Lawson |editor-first=Hugh |title=Slovakia's former coalition heads agree to early parliamentary elections |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/slovakias-former-coalition-heads-agree-early-parliamentary-elections-2023-01-22/ |access-date=24 September 2023 |website=Reuters |archive-date=30 September 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230930234304/https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/slovakias-former-coalition-heads-agree-early-parliamentary-elections-2023-01-22/ |url-status=live }} This was the first snap election in the country since [[2012 Slovak parliamentary election|2012]]. The [[Left-wing populism|left-wing populist]] and [[Social conservatism|social conservative]] [[Direction – Social Democracy]] (Smer-SD), led by former [[Prime Minister of Slovakia|Prime Minister]] [[Robert Fico]], emerged as the largest party, winning 42 seats. The [[Social liberalism|social-liberal]] and [[Pro-Europeanism|pro-European]] [[Progressive Slovakia]] (PS) came in second, with 32 seats. Former Prime Minister [[Peter Pellegrini]]'s [[Social democracy|social-democratic]] [[Voice – Social Democracy]] (Hlas-SD), which split from Smer-SD in 2020, came in third with 27 seats. The [[Conservatism|conservative]] [[OĽaNO]] and its allies won 16 seats, less than a quarter of their total in the 2020 election. The [[Christian democracy|Christian-democratic]] [[Christian Democratic Movement]] (KDH) and the [[Right-wing populism|right-wing populist]] [[Slovak National Party]] (SNS) re-entered the National Council after failing to achieve the vote threshold in 2020, winning twelve and ten seats respectively. The [[Classical liberalism|classical liberal]] [[Freedom and Solidarity]] (SaS) won eleven seats, tying the 2012 election as their worst result since the party's founding.{{Cite web |date=2023-09-18 |title=Výsledky predčasných volieb 2023 |url=https://dennikn.sk/volby/vysledky/ |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=Denník N |language=sk-SK |archive-date=1 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231001061734/https://dennikn.sk/volby/vysledky/ |url-status=live}} As no single party or alliance reached the 76 seats needed for a majority, a coalition government was needed. A coalition government of [[Direction – Social Democracy|Smer-SD]], [[Voice – Social Democracy|Hlas-SD]], and [[Slovak National Party|SNS]] was formed. A [[Fico's Fourth Cabinet|new government]] with [[Robert Fico]] as prime minister was sworn in on 25 October 2023. ==Background== Prior to the [[2020 Slovak parliamentary election|previous election]], the [[Slovakia|Slovak Republic]] experienced a period of political turbulence, triggered by the murder of investigative journalist Ján Kuciak and his fiancée Martina Kušnírová in 2018. The incident led to widespread protests and the resignation of then-Prime Minister [[Robert Fico]].{{Cite web |date=2018-03-15 |title=Slovak PM Robert Fico resigns |url=https://www.politico.eu/article/slovakia-election-prime-minister-robert-fico-smer-hlas-patience-coalition/ |access-date=2023-10-16 |website=POLITICO |language=en |quote=Slovakia’s Prime Minister Robert Fico officially resigned Thursday, less than three weeks after the murder of an investigative reporter and his fiancée shocked the nation. |archive-date=15 March 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180315171933/https://www.politico.eu/article/robert-fico-resigns-slovakia-prime-minister/ |url-status=live }} The election itself was won by the movement of [[Ordinary People and Independent Personalities]] (OĽaNO) led by [[Igor Matovič]]. The party emerged as the victor, gaining over a quarter of the popular vote, which translated to 53 seats in the 150-seat National Council. OĽaNO formed a [[Matovič Cabinet|coalition government]] with several other parties, ending the long-standing dominance of [[Direction – Social Democracy]] (SMER–SD).{{Cite web |date=2020-02-29 |title=Výsledky parlamentných volieb 2020 |url=https://dennikn.sk/volby/vysledky/ |access-date=2023-10-16 |website=SME |language=sk-SK |archive-date=29 February 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200229175532/https://volby.sme.sk/parlamentne-volby/2020/vysledky |url-status=live }} ==Electoral system== The 150 members of the [[National Council (Slovakia)|National Council]] were elected by [[proportional representation]] in a [[At-large|single nationwide constituency]] with an [[electoral threshold]] of 5% for single parties, 7% for coalitions of two or three parties, and 10% for coalitions of four or more parties. The [[election]] used the [[open list]] system, with seats allocated using [[largest remainder method]] with [[Hagenbach-Bischoff quota]].[https://www.zakonypreludi.sk/zz/2014-180/znenie-20230604#p68 Slovak law 180/2014 § 68] Voters were able to cast up to four preferential votes for candidates of the selected party.{{cite web|title=Slovakia Národná rada (National Council) Electoral System|url=http://www.ipu.org/parline-e/reports/2285_B.htm|publisher=[[Inter-Parliamentary Union]]|access-date=8 March 2016}} All citizens of the [[Slovakia|Slovak Republic]] were allowed to vote except for citizens under 18 years of age, [[Prisoner|felons]] in prison convicted of serious offenses, and people declared ineligible to perform legal acts by court. Voters abroad on election day were allowed to vote by [[Postal voting|mail]].{{cite web |title=Voľba poštou, Ministerstvo vnútra SR - Verejná správa |url=http://www.minv.sk/?nr16-posta |language=sk |publisher=Ministry of the Interior |access-date=14 December 2015}} All citizens 21 years of age or older on the election day and are permanent residents of Slovakia, were allowed to run as candidates except for [[prisoner]]s, convicted felons, and those declared ineligible to perform legal acts by court.{{cite news |date=9 October 2015 |title=Prieskum: Voľby by vyhral Smer, OĽaNO-NOVA mimo parlamentu |url=http://spravy.pravda.sk/domace/clanok/370210-prieskum-volby-by-vyhral-smer-so-ziskom-40-olano-nova-mimo-parlamentu/ |language=sk |newspaper=[[Pravda (Slovakia)|Pravda]]|access-date=13 October 2015}} All participating parties must register 90 days before election day and pay a [[Election deposit|deposit]] of €17,000 which would be refunded to all parties gaining at least 3% of the votes. Voters not present in their electoral district at the time of the elections were allowed to request a [[Voter registration|voting certificate]] (voličský preukaz), which allowed them to vote in any district regardless of their residency. Voters abroad on [[election day]] were allowed to request a postal vote. According to the Central Election Committee, approximately 72,000 citizens of the [[Slovakia|Slovak Republic]] living abroad had requested a postal vote for the [[election]]. color:black; text-align:center;" |'''NI''' |} ==Opinion polls== {{excerpt|Opinion polling for the 2023 Slovak parliamentary election|section=Graphical summary}} ==Issues and developments== 2023 election issues included high inflation, Slovakia's position on the [[Russian invasion of Ukraine]] and the related [[2021–2023 global energy crisis|global energy crisis]], [[COVID-19]], internal fights within the previous government, corruption scandals and immigration;[https://www.cnn.com/2023/09/28/europe/slovakia-election-russia-supporter-intl-cmd/index.html "A NATO country could soon have a pro-Russian leader,"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230929121900/https://www.cnn.com/2023/09/28/europe/slovakia-election-russia-supporter-intl-cmd/index.html |date=29 September 2023 }} updated September 28, 2023, [[Cable News Network|CNN]], retrieved September 29, 2023[https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/9/27/slovakias-knife-edge-election-to-determine-stance-on-ukraine "Slovakia’s knife-edge election to determine stance on Ukraine,"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230929062251/https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/9/27/slovakias-knife-edge-election-to-determine-stance-on-ukraine |date=29 September 2023 }} September 27, 2023, [[Reuters]] in [[Al Jazeera Media Network|Al Jazeera]], retrieved September 29, 2023 questions of rights and values (particularly [[LGBTQ+]] issues) were covered during the campaign by [[Al Jazeera English]], [[BBC]][https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-66938694 "Ukraine war: Slovakia's Robert Fico eyes comeback in Saturday's election,"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230929155413/https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-66938694 |date=29 September 2023 }} September 29, 2023, [[British Broadcasting Corporation|BBC]], retrieved September 29, 2023 and [[Pravda (Slovakia)|Pravda]].{{cite news | last = Mogilevskaia | first = Anna | title = Sulík pre Pravdu: Pliagou Slovenska je silný štát, nie LGBTI. Po voľbách si viem predstaviť SaS vo vláde | work = Pravda | url = https://spravy.pravda.sk/domace/clanok/680830-sulik-pre-pravdu-pliagou-slovenska-je-silny-stat-nie-lgbt-vo-vlade-mame-zaujem-o-rezorty-ktore-sme-doteraz-mali-spolupracu-viem/ | issn = 1336-197X | publisher = Our Media SR | location = Bratislava | date = 2023-09-09 | access-date = 2023-09-23 | archive-date = 4 October 2023 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20231004232503/https://spravy.pravda.sk/domace/clanok/680830-sulik-pre-pravdu-pliagou-slovenska-je-silny-stat-nie-lgbt-vo-vlade-mame-zaujem-o-rezorty-ktore-sme-doteraz-mali-spolupracu-viem/ | url-status = live }} By the week of the election, popularity polls indicated that the two strongest parties were the [[Progressive Slovakia]] (led by pro-European [[Michal Šimečka]], a member of the [[European Parliament]] (EP) since 2019, and EP Vice-President since 2022, who has committed to maintaining support for Ukraine) and [[Direction – Social Democracy|Smer-SD]] (headed by [[Robert Fico]], three-time former prime minister, who has committed to ending Slovakia's support for Ukraine); however, neither appeared to be commanding a majority, and the [[British Broadcasting Corporation|BBC]] projected neither would top 20% of the vote, so each would have to attempt to build a coalition with other parties to achieve the majority needed to rule. Consequently, as many as 10 parties could wind up in the government. The third-largest party, which tipped the balance in favor of [[Robert Fico]], is [[Voice – Social Democracy|Hlas–SD]] (Voice), the moderate-left party of [[Peter Pellegrini]] (formerly of Smer-SD, Legislative elections were held in [[Taiwan]] on 13 January 2024 to elect members of the [[Legislative Yuan of the Republic of China|Legislative Yuan]]. The elections were held alongside [[2024 Taiwanese presidential election|presidential elections]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-03-10 |title=Taiwan sets Jan 13, 2024 for presidential, legislative elections |url=https://www.taiwannews.com.tw/en/news/4831353 |access-date=2023-08-08 |website=Taiwan News}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2024 presidential, legislative elections slated for Jan. 13: CEC |url=https://focustaiwan.tw/politics/202303100014 |access-date=2023-08-08 |website=Focus Taiwan - CNA English News |date=10 March 2023 |language=en-US}}</ref>

The results saw the ruling [[Democratic Progressive Party]] (DPP) lose its majority in the Legislative Yuan that it had held since [[2016 Taiwanese legislative election|2016]], losing 11 seats and retaining 51, while the [[Kuomintang]] (KMT) became the largest single party with 52 seats, and the [[Taiwan People's Party]] (TPP) won eight seats. The [[New Power Party]] lost all its three seats after failing to win a constituency seat or meet the 5% threshold for at-large representation. The election marked the first time under the current electoral system (introduced in 2008) that no party held an absolute majority in the Legislative Yuan,<ref name="nomajority"/> and the first in which the largest party in the legislature won neither the most constituency votes nor the most party votes. The term of the Legislative Yuan began on 1 February 2024.

==Electoral system==
{{Further|Legislative Yuan elections in Taiwan}}
The 113 seats of the [[Legislative Yuan]] are elected through [[parallel voting]]:<ref>{{Cite news |title=Election Types|url=https://web.cec.gov.tw/english/article/18|url-status=live |access-date=6 June 2026 |website=Central Election Commission |language=en}}</ref>
* 73 seats are elected through [[First-past-the-post]] voting in single member constituencies,
* 6 seats are reserved for [[taiwanese aboriginals]] elected through [[single non-transferable vote]] in two 3-member constituencies, [[Lowland Aborigine Constituency|Lowland]] and [[Highland Aborigine Constituency|Highland]],
* 34 seats are elected through [[party-list proportional representation]] in a single nationwide constituency with a 5% [[electoral threshold]], and 50% of list seats won must be women.

Taiwan's [[Central Election Commission (Taiwan)|Central Election Commission]] uses an active household registration system, therefore no citizen has to actively register. [[Electronic voting]] is not implemented in Taiwanese elections, nor is [[absentee voting]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Characteristics of Taiwan Elections|url=https://web.cec.gov.tw/english/article/23550|url-status=live |access-date=6 June 2026 |website=Central Election Commission |language=en}}</ref>

==Results==
The Kuomintang won 52 seats, making it the largest single party in the Legislative Yuan. The DPP, having won 51 seats, declined to the second largest party in the Legislative Yuan. The [[Taiwan People's Party]] (TPP) ranked the third with 8 seats under its control. The DPP lost 11 seats in the election, which also meant the loss of the parliamentary majority that it had held since [[2016 Taiwanese legislative election|2016]]. The election results also led to the removal of the [[New Power Party]], which previously held three seats, from the Legislative Yuan after it failed to win a constituency seat or meet the 5% threshold needed to win at-large seats. Two independents, namely [[Chen Chao-ming]] and [[Kao Chin Su-mei]], who were members of the Kuomintang caucus in the 10th Yuan, were also elected.<ref name="nomajority">{{cite news |title=No party gets majority in Legislature; KMT wins most seats |url=https://focustaiwan.tw/politics/202401130014 |access-date=13 January 2024 |agency=Focus Taiwan |date=13 January 2024}}</ref>

The election was the first in Taiwanese history in which the party that received the most votes did not win the most seats, and also marked the first time since [[2004 Taiwanese legislative election|2004]] that no party held an absolute majority in the Legislative Yuan.<ref name="nomajority"/> This put the TPP in a "kingmaker" position; it also meant that the TPP’s support was crucial in the selection of the [[President of the Legislative Yuan]] and the major policies.<ref>{{cite news |title=No party gets legislative majority; small TPP to play key role |url=https://focustaiwan.tw/politics/202401130019 |access-date=13 January 2024 |agency=Focus Taiwan |date=13 January 2024}}</ref>

The election was also the first time that an openly [[LGBT history in Taiwan|bisexual]] candidate,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Storm.mg |date=2021-01-24 |title=觀點投書：護航黃捷不要炫耀雙性戀-風傳媒 |url=https://www.storm.mg/article/3410687 |access-date=2024-02-01 |website=www.storm.mg |language=zh-TW}}</ref> [[Huang Jie (politician)|Huang Jie]] (DPP) of [[Kaohsiung]] city's sixth constituency, was elected to the Legislative Yuan.<ref>{{cite news |title=Huang Jie becomes Taiwan's first openly gay legislator |url=https://focustaiwan.tw/politics/202401130016 |work=Focus Taiwan |access-date=13 January 2024}}</ref> It was also the first time that an openly transgender person, Abbygail ET Wu of the [[Green Party Taiwan|Green Party]] (at-large), ran for the chamber, albeit unsuccessfully.<ref>{{cite news |title=Taiwan's 1st transgender legislative candidate vows to continue activism |url=https://focustaiwan.tw/society/202401190004 |work=Focus Taiwan |access-date=23 January 2024}}</ref>

=== By National-at-large ===
National-at-large legislators are apportioned by [[largest remainder method]]. Political parties will gain seats upon reaching the 5% threshold and allocated based on total votes. The quota remains as 2.9412%, each political party will be allocated a seat. The remainder will be allocated based on the largest remainder (Remainder: Democratic Progressive Party 0.7244%; Kuomintang 1.9683%; Taiwan People's Party 0.2496%).

==Aftermath==
At the opening of the new Legislative Yuan on 1 February 2024, [[Han Kuo-yu]] of the Kuomintang was elected as [[President of the Legislative Yuan]] following two rounds of voting in which all eight members of the TPP abstained in the second round. Han obtained the support of the KMT's 52 members in the Legislative Yuan as well as two independents<ref>{{cite news |title=Member of Taiwan's pro-unification Nationalists elected speaker in a consolation prize for China |url=https://apnews.com/article/taiwan-china-politics-legislature-fa2f05bf6bd89df5cdc3163f9336b18b |work=Associated Press |access-date=1 February 2024}}</ref> and defeated the DPP's [[You Si-kun]] and the TPP's [[Huang Shan-shan]]. The KMT's [[Johnny Chiang]] was also elected as deputy speaker, defeating the DPP's [[Tsai Chi-chang]] and the TPP's [[Chang Chi-kai]].<ref>{{cite news |title=KMT wins speakership, deputy speakership in newly sworn-in Legislature |url=https://focustaiwan.tw/politics/202402010020 |agency=Central News Agency |access-date=1 February 2024}}</ref>

The first round of the election also coincided with two [[2024 Uruguayan constitutional referendum|constitutional referendums]] on reforms to the social security system that would lower the retirement age, increase payouts and transfer privately managed savings to a state-run trust,{{Cite web |title=Uruguay election: Voters in one of Latin America's strongest democracies pick between 2 centrists |url=https://apnews.com/article/uruguay-election-politics-leftwing-president-rightwing-86984f87bb0607d9c061c293ec11fe71 |access-date=2024-10-27 |website=Associated Press |language=en}} and allowing for nighttime police raids in homes.{{cite web |url=https://apnews.com/article/uruguay-election-politics-leftwing-president-rightwing-86984f87bb0607d9c061c293ec11fe71 |title=Polls open in stable Uruguay in a vote free of political hostility seen elsewhere in the region |work=[[Associated Press]] |date=27 October 2024 |access-date=27 October 2024 |last1=Batschke |first1=Nayara |last2=Debre |first2=Isabel |language=en }} ==Background== {{Main|Presidency of Luis Lacalle Pou}} Incumbent president [[Luis Lacalle Pou]], who won the [[2019 Uruguayan general election|2019 elections]], cannot run again as the constitution bars a president from immediate re-election. As a result, the governing [[National Party (Uruguay)|National Party]] has to nominate a new candidate. Lacalle Pou took office in 2020, heading the [[Republican Coalition|Multicolor Coalition]], a big tent political alliance formed after October 2019 first round that remains active in the 2024 elections under the name ''Republican Coalition''. His cabinet is composed of leaders from the member parties of the coalition, which holds a majority in both chambers of Parliament, allowing it to push through various legislative initiatives despite the Broad Front opposition. During the period from 2020 to 2024, the government of Luis Lacalle Pou has faced various controversies and challenges. These have included issues related to the handling of the COVID-19 pandemic, economic policies, corruption scandals and social issues such as education reform and security. ==Electoral system== Voting in Uruguay is compulsory and extends to all citizens aged 18 and over. Those who cannot vote without a valid reason will face a fine or be sanctioned with the inability to carry out various public procedures. According to the [[Constitution of Uruguay]], voting is not only a right of the citizen but above all, it is a duty as a citizen, as well as an obligation. The [[President of Uruguay]] is elected using the [[two-round system]], with a run-off held between the two most-voted candidates if no candidate receives 50% of the vote in the first round. The 30 members of the [[Senate of Uruguay|Senate]] are elected by proportional representation in a single nationwide constituency. The vice president, elected on the same ballot as the president, becomes president of the Senate, with his vote being determinant in case of tie.[http://www.ipu.org/parline-e/reports/2342_B.htm Electoral system] IPU The 99 members of the [[Chamber of Representatives of Uruguay|Chamber of Representatives]] are elected by proportional representation in 19 multi-member constituencies based on the 19 [[Departments of Uruguay|departments]]. Seats are allocated using the [[highest averages method]].[http://www.ipu.org/parline-e/reports/2341_B.htm Electoral system] IPU The elections are held using the [[Ley de Lemas|double simultaneous vote method]], whereby voters cast a single vote for the party of their choice for all three seats of Presidency, Senate and Chamber of Representatives. ==Parties and candidates== [[2024 Uruguayan presidential primaries|Presidential primaries]] were held on 30 June 2024 to nominate the presidential candidate for every [[List of political parties in Uruguay|political party]]. Fourteen political parties surpassed the minimum of 500 valid votes in the internal elections required by the Electoral Court to participate in the general elections. Of these fourteen, only eleven ultimately participated in these elections (the same number of parties as in the previous elections of 2019, but with different parties). Following the results of the second round, Delgado conceded defeat to Orsi, who pledged to be a president "who calls again and again for national dialogue to find the best solutions".{{Cite web|url=https://www.france24.com/en/americas/20241125-leftist-candidate-in-the-lead-in-uruguay-s-presidential-election |title=Leftist candidate Orsi wins Uruguay's presidential election |date=25 November 2024|access-date=25 November 2024|website=[[France 24]] |language=en}} Outgoing president [[Luis Lacalle Pou]] congratulated Orsi, who pledged to begin the presidential transition "as soon as I deem it appropriate".{{Cite web|url=https://apnews.com/article/uruguay-yamadu-orsi-elected-president-ab071b5afb2f94bcba8877d5e47c91cf |title=Uruguay’s leftist opposition candidate Yamandú Orsi becomes country’s new president |date=25 November 2024|access-date=25 November 2024|website=[[Associated Press]] |language=en}} === International === * {{Flag|Argentina}}: The [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs, International Trade and Worship|Ministry of Foreign Affairs]] issued a statement congratulating Orsi on his victory, as well as wishes to strengthen the ties between Argentina and Uruguay. * {{Flag|Brazil}}: President [[Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva]] congratulated Orsi on his victory, as well as the electoral process. * {{Flag|Colombia}}: President [[Gustavo Petro]] congratulated Orsi on his victory, who stated that "this victory reflects the will of the Latin American people for unity and change". * {{Flag|Guatemala}}: President [[Bernardo Arévalo]] (who was born in [[Montevideo]]) congratulated Orsi on his victory, who stated that: "May the success of your government translate into the improvement of the material and spiritual conditions of the beloved Uruguayan people". * {{Flag|Honduras}}: President [[Xiomara Castro]] congratulated Orsi on his victory, who said that "a clear victory that reaffirms the progressive and democratic trend in Latin America". * {{Flag|Mexico}}: President [[Claudia Sheinbaum]] congratulated both Orsi and Cosse on their victories, as well as saying that the Uruguayan people "once again demonstrates its democratic and ([[Zhelyazkov Government]]) }}{{Politics of Bulgaria}} Snap parliamentary elections were held in [[Bulgaria]] on 27 October 2024,{{cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/bulgaria-hold-another-snap-parliamentary-election-oct-27-says-president-2024-08-26/|title=Bulgaria to hold another snap parliamentary election on Oct. 27, says president|website=[[Reuters]]|date=26 August 2024}}{{Cite web |title=Central Election Commission Adopts Schedule for October 27 Snap Parliamentary Elections |url=https://www.bta.bg/en/news/bulgaria/732377-central-election-commission-adopts-schedule-for-october-27-snap-parliamentary-el |access-date=2024-08-27 |website=www.bta.bg |language=en}} after all [[June 2024 Bulgarian parliamentary election#Coalition negotiations|three attempts to form a government]] following the latest [[June 2024 Bulgarian parliamentary election|June 2024 elections]] failed. This was the country's sixth snap election since 2021. This series of snap elections is the result of [[Bulgarian political crisis (2021–2026)|a political crisis affecting the country]]. Eight parties passed the [[electoral threshold]] to win representation in the National Assembly, while [[Velichie]] came just 21 votes short to win representation. [[GERB–SDS]] had the best results by winning 25.5% of the vote, but were required to form an alliance with at least two other elected parties in order to achieve a voting majority in the National Assembly. The new elected [[51st National Assembly of Bulgaria|51st Parliament]] replaced the [[50th National Assembly of Bulgaria|50th Parliament]] when all elected members were sworn in on 11 November.{{Cite web|title=The Members of the 51th National Assembly officially took the oath of office|url=https://parliament.bg/en/news/ID/6132|website=National Assembly of the Republic of Bulgaria (parliament.bg)|date=11 November 2024|access-date=11 November 2024}} After 11 voting rounds, [[Natalia Kiselova]] ([[BSP – United Left|BSP–OL]]) was elected as speaker of the National Assembly on 6 December.{{Cite web|title=ОБНОВЕНА: Наталия Киселова е избрана за председател на 51-вото Народно събрание|trans-title=UPDATED: Natalia Kiselova elected as Speaker of the 51st National Assembly|url=https://www.bta.bg/bg/news/bulgaria/794888-nataliya-kiselova-e-izbrana-za-predsedatel-na-51-voto-narodno-sabranie|date=6 December 2024|access-date=6 December 2024|author=Desislava Antova|website=BTA|language=bg}} President [[Rumen Radev]] granted the [[#First negotiation mandate|first negotiation mandate]] to the largest party GERB-SDS on 15 January,{{Cite web|title=Wrap-up: GERB-UDF Mandated to Form Cabinet, Unveil Proposed Lineup|url=https://www.bta.bg/en/news/bulgaria/815213-gerb-udf-mandated-to-form-cabinet-unveil-proposed-lineup|author=Dimitrina Solakova|date=15 January 2025|access-date=15 January 2025|website=BTA|language=en}} which formed a minority government alongside [[Bulgarian Socialist Party|BSP]] and [[There is Such a People|ITN]], with support from [[Alliance for Rights and Freedoms|APS (Dogan)]]. The government was led by GERB politician Rosen Zhelyazkov.{{Cite web|title=Хората на Доган ще подкрепят кабинет на ГЕРБ, БСП и ИТН|trans-title=Dogan's people will support a cabinet of GERB, BSP and ITN|url=https://www.mediapool.bg/horata-na-dogan-shte-podkrepyat-kabinet-na-gerb-bsp-i-itn-news367038.html|date=14 January 2025|access-date=14 January 2025|website=Mediapool|language=bg}}{{Cite web|title=Movement for Rights and Freedoms' Operations Bureau Confirms Support for Zhelyazkov's Cabinet|url=https://www.bta.bg/en/news/bulgaria/815272-movement-for-rights-and-freedoms-operations-bureau-confirms-support-for-zhelyaz|author=Yoana Vodenicharova|date=15 January 2025|access-date=15 January 2025|website=BTA|language=en}} Velichie and all elected parties except [[DPS – A New Beginning|DPS–NN (Peevski)]] [[#Contestation of the results and election conduct|contested the results and conduct of the parliamentary election]] by submitting complaint cases to the [[Constitutional Court of Bulgaria|Constitutional Court]]; and the court subsequently appointed an independent expert panel to investigate all complaints. Following a recalculation of the results, the Constitutional Court ruled in March 2025 that 16 of the 240 MPs were elected illegally, and that Velichie had passed the threshold.{{Cite web |title=Constitutional Court Outlaws Election of 16 MPs in 51st National Assembly |url=https://www.bta.bg/en/news/bulgaria/851141-|website=Bulgarian News Agency}} ==Background== {{See also|Bulgarian political crisis (2021–2026)}} ===Elections and government breakdown=== The [[June 2024 Bulgarian parliamentary election|June 2024 elections]], held at the same time as the [[2024 European Parliament election in Bulgaria|European Parliament elections]], had the lowest turnout (33%) since the [[End of Communism in Bulgaria (1989)|end of communist rule in 1989]].{{Cite web |date=22 June 2022 |title=Bulgaria's Petkov points finger at mafia and Russia as government collapses |url=https://www.politico.eu/article/bulgarian-pm-petkov-government-lose-no-confidence-vote/ |access-date=10 April |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230410183652/https://www.politico.eu/article/bulgarian-pm-petkov-government-lose-no-confidence-vote/ |url-status=live }} It resulted in [[GERB–SDS]] winning 25% of the votes and 68 seats, with no party or alliance obtaining enough seats to form a majority in the National Assembly.{{Cite web |date=2024-06-10 |title=Centre right bags victory in Bulgaria national and EU elections |url=https://www.euronews.com/my-europe/2024/06/10/centre-right-bags-victory-in-bulgaria-national-and-eu-elections |access-date=2024-08-04 |website=euronews |language=en}} The new elected [[50th National Assembly of Bulgaria|50th Parliament]] replaced the [[49th National Assembly of Bulgaria|49th Parliament]],{{Cite web|url=https://www.bta.bg/en/news/bulgaria/692888-new-parliament-opens|title=New Parliament Opens|author=Petya Petrova|publisher=Bulgarian News Agency|date=19 June 2024|access-date=21 June 2024}} when all elected members were sworn in on 19 June.{{Cite web|url=https://www.bta.bg/en/news/bulgaria/692940-new-mps-are-sworn-in|title=New MPs Are Sworn In|author=Petya Petrova|publisher=Bulgarian Change – Democratic Bulgaria|PP–DB]] and [[There is Such a People]] (ITN), with the final attempt failing on 5 August.{{Cite web |date=2024-08-04 |title=Bulgaria appears set for early elections as populist ITN says it will abandon bid for government |url=https://sofiaglobe.com/2024/08/04/bulgaria-appears-set-for-early-elections-as-populist-itn-says-it-will-abandon-bid-for-government/ 2024|access-date=5 August 2024|website=BTA|language=en|archive-url=|archive-date=|url-status=}} As a consequence, [[President of Bulgaria|President]] [[Rumen Radev]] instead appointed the Vice Radev rejected the government proposal, delaying the upcoming election.{{Cite web |date=2024-08-19 |title=Bulgaria elections postponed as political crisis deepens |url=https://www.politico.eu/article/bulgaria-elections-postponed-president-rumen-radev-kalin-stoyanov-political-crisis/ |access-date=2024-08-22 |website=Politico |language=en-GB}} Following the rejection of Grancharova-Kozhareva, Radev re-appointed [[Dimitar Glavchev]] as the caretaker prime minister,{{Cite web |title=Bulgaria: Glavchev to Lead Interim Government Again, October Elections Confirmed - Novinite.com - Sofia News Agency |url=https://www.novinite.com/articles/227900/Bulgaria:+Glavchev+to+Lead+Interim+Government+Again,+October+Elections+Confirmed |access-date=2024-08-28 |website=www.novinite.com}} and his [[Second Glavchev Government|government proposal]] was sworn in on 27 August, and the elections were set for 27 October.{{Cite web |date=2024-08-27 |title=New Bulgarian caretaker government sworn in |url=https://www.euronews.com/2024/08/27/new-bulgarian-caretaker-government-sworn-in-ahead-of-october-election |access-date=2024-08-28 |website=euronews |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2024-08-26 |title=Bulgaria to hold another snap parliamentary election on Oct. 27, says president |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/bulgaria-hold-another-snap-parliamentary-election-oct-27-says-president-2024-08-26/ |work=[[Reuters]]}} === Changes in the Assembly's composition prior to the election === One MP was expelled from the BSP by its national council on 18 June, before being sworn in. The [[Velichie]] parliamentary group comprised 13 MPs after the election. News |url=https://www.transparency.org/en/news/the-price-of-a-vote-in-a-bulgarian-pub |access-date=2024-09-30 |website=Transparency.org |language=en}} During the election campaign, a deputy, [[Ivaylo Mirchev]], from [[PP–DB]], claimed that there was widespread vote buying being conducted by [[DPS – A New Beginning|DPS–Peevski]], claiming people were being paid up to 500 BGN (US$286) per vote.{{Cite web |last=Мирчев |first=Ивайло |date=2024-09-28 |title=Статус на деня: Пеевски купува гласове чрез Цайса, Дънката, Сандокана, Шарана и Данчо Пръча |url=https://www.dnevnik.bg/analizi/2024/09/28/4681836_status_na_denia_peevski_kupuva_glasove_chrez_caisa/ |access-date=2024-09-30 |website=Dnevnik |language=bg}} One of the leaders of the list for DPS–Peevski appeared to admit to vote buying in a social media poll.{{Cite web |date=2024-10-10 |title=Водач на листа на ДПС-Пеевски леко се изпусна: Призна, че коалицията купува гласове |url=https://gospodari.com/novini/2024/10/10/vodach-na-lista-na-dps-peevski-leko-se-izpusna-prizna-che-koalitsiyata-kupuva-glasove |access-date=2024-10-18 |website=Gospodari.com |language=bg}} The [[Ministry of Interior (Bulgaria)|interior minister]], [[Atanas Ilkov]], told a parliamentary hearing that he had received two alerts of vote buying by 25 September.{{Cite web |title=Interior Ministry Has Received Two Alerts of Alleged Vote Buying Regarding Oct. 27 Elections |url=https://www.bta.bg/en/news/bulgaria/748574-interior-ministry-has-received-two-alerts-of-alleged-vote-buying-regarding-oct- |access-date=2024-09-30 |website=www.bta.bg |language=en}} A national police operation that was set up to target the practice began operating two days later.{{Cite web |title=Bulgaria: Interior Ministry Launches Nationwide Operation to Combat Vote-Buying - Novinite.com - Sofia News Agency |url=https://www.novinite.com/articles/228525/Bulgaria:+Interior+Ministry+Launches+Nationwide+Operation+to+Combat+Vote-Buying |access-date=2024-09-30 |website=www.novinite.com}} On 18 October, Ilkov said his ministry had received 259 allegations of vote buying.{{Cite web |date=2024-10-18 |title=Бързи новини (18 октомври) |url=https://www.dnevnik.bg/burzi-novini/2024/10/18/4690061_burzi_novini_18_oktomvri/#4690454 |access-date=2024-10-18 |website=Dnevnik |language=bg}} [[Deutsche Welle]] received reports, especially in [[Kardzhali Province]], that DPS–Peevski was pressuring people to vote for the party in fear of losing their jobs, with already 60 jobs lost in the municipal administration. They also reported that Peevski personally was paying for various small-scale public repairs.{{Cite web |title=Кърджали: Натиск да се гласува "правилно" |url=https://www.dw.com/bg/krdzali-natisk-da-se-glasuva-pravilno/a-70598054 |access-date=2024-10-26 |website=dw.com |language=bg}} === Dzheyhan Ibryamov case === On 2 October, the lead candidate of [[Alliance for Rights and Freedoms|DPS–Dogan]] in Shumen, [[Dzheyhan Ibryamov]], was arrested by the Prosecutors Office on the charge of attempting to buy vote and [[influence peddling]].{{Cite web |title=Арестуван е депутатът Джейхан Ибрямов от ДПС-Доган. Антикорупционната комисия влезе в дома му |url=https://www.svobodnaevropa.bg/a/dzheyhan-ibryamov-arestuvan-dps-dogan/33144346.html |access-date=2024-10-06 |website=www.svobodnaevropa.com|date=3 October 2024 }} Following a request by the Prosecutors Office, the CEC and Chairwoman of the National Assembly, [[Raya Nazaryan]], agreed to lift Ibryamov's immunity as a candidate in the elections.{{Cite web |title=Решено: Джейхан Ибрямов остана без имунитет |url=https://tribune.bg/bg/politika/resheno-dzheyhan-ibryamov-osta/ |access-date=2024-10-06 |website=www.trinune.bg}} Despite the criminal case against him and his arrest, Ibryamov was still authorised to participate in the elections.{{Cite web |title=И със свален имунитет Джейхан Ибрямов продължава да участва в изборите, увери Матева |url=https://banker.bg/2024/10/06/i-sas-svalen-imunitet-dzhejhan-ibryamov-prodalzhava-da-uchastva-v-izborite-uveri-mateva/ |access-date=2024-10-06 |website=www.banker.bg|date=6 October 2024 }} The arrest and criminal prosecution of Ibryamov provoked negative reactions from key DPS–Dogan figures, with the coalition ''de facto'' leader, [[Dzhevdet Chakarov]], calling for the cancellation of the upcoming elections.{{Cite web |title=Джевдет Чакъров за арестите на членове на ДПС: Ще предложим отмяна на изборите |url=https://btvnovinite.bg/bulgaria/dzhevdet-chakarov-za-arestite-na-chlenove-na-dps-shte-predlozhim-otmjana-na-izborite.html?p=1&utm_source=article_page_break&utm_medium=article&utm_campaign=page_break_reload#page_break_1 |access-date=2024-10-06 |website=www.BTV.bg}} === Post-result reports === In identified polling stations with a risk of high levels of controlled or bought votes, GERB and DPS–Peevski were the leading parties.{{Cite web |last=Друмева |first=Ина |date=2024-10-29 |title=В рисковите секции Пеевски обра гласовете за ДПС от юни |url=https://m.dnevnik.bg/izbori-2024/2024/10/29/4694908_v_riskovite_sekcii_peevski_obra_glasovete_za_dps_ot/ |access-date=2024-10-29 |website=Dnevnik |language=bg}} According to the Institute for the Development of the Public Environment, there were 827 polling stations with this risk, and [[BTV (Bulgaria)|bTV]] reported some voters in [[Blagoevgrad Municipality|Blagoevgrad]] did not deny that there was vote buying occurring.{{Cite web |title=827 рискови секции в страната: В една от тях не отричат за изборна търговия |url=https://btvnovinite.bg/bulgaria/827-riskovi-sekcii-v-stranata-v-edna-ot-tjah-ne-otrichat-za-izborna-targovija.html |access-date=2024-10-29 |website=bTV Новините |language=bg}} The coordinator of the 'You Count' organisation, which asks voters to report election misconduct, claimed that there were entire municipalities at risk of high levels of bought and controlled votes. He claimed the results did not reflect the will of the Bulgarian citizens because the results were so skewed.{{Cite web |title=Тодор Петров: Вече няма рискови секции, има рискови общини |url=https://bnr.bg/horizont/post/102066434 |access-date=2024-10-29 }} An investigation was released on the state broadcaster, BNT, claimed to show that discrepancies of up to 100 votes in one electoral district, as well as other malpractices elsewhere.{{Cite web |title=БНТ с ново разкритие: 100 гласа разлика между видеонаблюдението и протокол от СИК в Гърмен by abroad countries ==Aftermath== {{too detailed|date=December 2024}} {{split section|date=January 2025}} The new elected [[51st National Assembly of Bulgaria|51st Parliament]] replaced the [[50th National Assembly of Bulgaria|50th Parliament]], when all elected members were sworn in on 11 November. The official start of the process for exploring the [[#First negotiation mandate|first negotiation mandate]] in order to form a new government, awaited a prior election of the speaker for the 51st National Assembly. After 11 voting rounds, [[Natalia Kiselova]] ([[BSP – United Left|BSP–OL]]) was elected as speaker of the National Assembly on 6 December. The [[Electoral threshold|unelected]] party [[Velichie]] and all elected parties, except [[DPS – A New Beginning|DPS–NN (Peevski)]], [[#Contestation of the results and election conduct|contested the results and conduct of the parliamentary election]] by submitting [[complaint]] cases to the [[Constitutional Court of Bulgaria|Constitutional Court]]; and the court subsequently appointed an independent expert panel with a given deadline on 10 January 2025 to investigate all complaints. === Election of the speaker === {{main|51st National Assembly of Bulgaria#National Assembly Speaker and Deputy-Speakers}} The election of a [[Chairperson of the National Assembly of Bulgaria|speaker for the 51st National Assembly]] is required before it can begin its work, which include conducting upcoming votes on potential government formation proposals. The Bulgarian President will only start the process of handing out the exploring [[#Government formation|government forming mandates]], once a speaker of the Parliament has been elected.{{Cite web|title=Ако бъде избран председател на парламента, поне две много съществени процедури ще бъдат отпушени, каза вицепрезидентът Илияна Йотова|trans-title=If the Speaker of the Parliament is elected, at least two very important procedures will be unblocked, said Vice President Iliana Yotova|url=https://www.bta.bg/bg/news/bulgaria/790322-ako-bade-izbran-predsedatel-na-parlamenta-pone-dve-mnogo-sashtestveni-protsedur|author=Konstantin Kostov|date=29 November 2024|access-date=29 November 2024|website=BTA|language=bg}} The election of the speaker of the National Assembly was previously used by GERB as a key part of coalition negotiations. GERB again declared that as the largest party, they should elect the speaker and his party would not partake in coalition talks if this was not to be the case.{{Cite web |last=Веселинова |first=Йорданка |date=2024-11-04 |title=Борисов отново постави избора на председател на парламента като условие за преговорите за кабинет |url=https://www.dnevnik.bg/politika/2024/11/04/4697860_borisov_otnovo_postavi_izbora_na_predsedatel_na/?ref=home_mainStory |access-date=2024-11-04 |website=Dnevnik |language=bg}} PP–DB had previously stated they would not vote to elect a GERB speaker.{{Cite news |date=2024-11-03 |title=ПП-ДБ няма да подкрепят председател на НС от ГЕРБ |url=https://offnews.bg/politika/pp-db-niama-da-podkrepiat-predsedatel-na-ns-ot-gerb-833405.html |access-date=2024-11-04 |work=OFFNews}} Initially, the GERB and PP–DB candidates, [[Raya Nazaryan]] and [[Andrey Tsekov]] respectively, made it into the run-off vote, but neither could get a majority of the votes. The conflict between the involved institutions led to an emergency session of the National Assembly.{{Cite web |date=2025-03-11 |title=Парламентът вика на изслушване и експертите, броили повторно бюлетините от вота |url=https://www.24chasa.bg/bulgaria/article/20087874 |access-date=2025-03-11 |website=24Chasa |language=bg}} Following the testimonies of representatives of the institutions, GERB called for an open session of the Constitutional Court in order to determine how the recount was conducted.{{Cite web |date=2025-03-11 |title=Лично шефът на "Информационно обслужване" сезирал прокуратурата за липсващи гласове от вота |url=https://www.24chasa.bg/bulgaria/article/20088681 |access-date=2025-03-11 |website=24Chasa |language=bg}} ITN supported this, and called for a hearing of the experts who had conducted the recount.{{Cite web |date=2025-03-11 |title=От ИТН искат изслушване на вещите лица от Конституционния съд|url=https://www.24chasa.bg/bulgaria/article/20090154|access-date=2025-03-11 |website=24Chasa |language=bg}} Revival called for the resignation of the CEC, the head of the Information Services agency and the Constitutional Court. Thousands, including senior PP–DB figures, protested the process.{{Cite web |date=2025-03-12 |title=Протест "Кой открадна изборите" събра хиляди в големите градове (Обновена) |url=https://www.mediapool.bg/protest-koi-otkradna-izborite-sabra-hilyadi-v-golemite-gradove-obnovena-news369097.html |access-date=2025-03-13 |website=Mediapool.bg |language=bg-BG}} On 12 March, the National Assembly approved a declaration requesting that the Constitutional Court provide greater transparency about the recount and undertake further steps to establish the validity of the preceding elections.{{Cite web |date=2025-03-12 |title=Управляващите и "Ново начало" срещу Конституционния съд: втори рунд |url=https://www.mediapool.bg/upravlyavashtite-i-novo-nachalo-sreshtu-konstitutsionniya-sad-vtori-rund-news369057.html |access-date=2025-03-13 |website=Mediapool.bg |language=bg-BG}} They further heard testimonies from some of the experts involved in the recount, who described some of the discrepancies found by the recount and confirmed that they had received empty boxes from certain electoral sections. The testimony of the experts led to accusations by ITN MP, Toshko Yordanov, that the Constitutional Court was potentially responsible for the disappearance of the ballots. The Constitutional Court in turn claimed that they had requested the missing ballots from the CEC, but didn't receive them.{{Cite web |date=2025-03-12 |title=КС 2 пъти изискал изборни книжа по делото за оспорване на законността на вота |url=https://www.24chasa.bg/bulgaria/article/20096755|access-date=2025-03-13 |website=24chasa.bg |language=bg-BG}} On 13 March, the Constitutional Court declared that 16 sitting deputies in the National Assembly were illegally elected, and instructed the CEC to present a new composition of the Assembly. The court's decision resulted in the following changes:{{Cite web |date=2025-03-13 |title=Конституционният съд обяви за незаконен избора на 16 депутати, "Величие" влиза в НС |url=https://www.mediapool.bg/konstitutsionniyat-sad-obyavi-za-nezakonen-izbora-na-16-deputati-velichie-vliza-v-ns-news369132.html |access-date=2025-03-13 |website=Mediapool.bg |language=bg-BG}}{{Cite news |last=BNT |date=2025-03-13 |title=КС обяви за незаконен избора на 16 народни представители, "Величие" влиза в парламента |url=https://bntnews.bg/news/ks-obyavi-za-nezakonen-izbora-na-16-narodni-predstaviteli-velichie-vliza-v-parlamenta-1330644news.html |work=[[Bulgarian National Television]]}} * The threshold to pass the 4% barrier was raised to 97,391 votes, something which Velichie passed. * All parties' votes shifted, including DPS–Peevski receiving 1,110 fewer votes. * ITN, MECh and GERB had 3 illegally elected MPs, DPS–Peevski and Vaz. had 2 each, and DPS–Dogan, PP–DB, and BSP–OL had 1 each. The court suggested that there was more electoral fraud than had been found, but that it did not have the power to recognize it.{{Cite web |date=2025-03-13 |title=Изборните измами са много по-големи, но КС няма власт да ги признае |url=https://www.mediapool.bg/izbornite-izmami-sa-mnogo-po-golemi-no-ks-nyama-vlast-da-gi-priznae-news369149.html |access-date=2025-03-14 |website=Mediapool.bg |language=bg-BG}} Following the ruling, the Organisation for Fair Elections presented its analysis of the results, and suggested 238,000 votes could have been at risk of manipulation, the highest for the last five elections.{{Cite web |title=238 хил. гласа дадени в секции, за които подозират, че може да са манипулирани |url=https://www.24chasa.bg/bulgaria/article/20113726 |access-date=2025-03-15 |website=www.24chasa.bg |language=en}} === Government instability === With the Constitutional Court determining Velichie had passed the threshold and gained 10 seats in the National Assembly, the government's support was bought down to 121 out of 240 deputies. However, Borisov said that, because one government deputy was sick, the government [[de facto]] had a majority of 1 (120 to 119).{{Cite web |title=Борисов: Заговорът на президента и Конституционния съд успя и ни ограбиха |url=https://nova.bg/news/view/2025/03/14/490763/%D0%B1%D0%BE%D1%80%D0%B8%D1%81%D0%BE%D0%B2-%D0%B7%D0%B0%D0%B3%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%BE%D1%80%D1%8A%D1%82-%D0%BD%D0%B0-%D0%BF%D1%80%D0%B5%D0%B7%D0%B8%D0%B4%D0%B5%D0%BD%D1%82%D0%B0-%D0%B8-%D0%BA%D0%BE%D0%BD%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B8%D1%82%D1%83%D1%86%D0%B8%D0%BE%D0%BD%D0%BD%D0%B8%D1%8F-%D1%81%D1%8A%D0%B4-%D1%83%D1%81%D0%BF%D1%8F-%D0%B8-%D0%BD%D0%B8-%D0%BE%D0%B3%D1%80%D0%B0%D0%B1%D0%B8%D1%85%D0%B0/ |access-date=2025-03-14 |website=nova.bg |language=bulgarian}} Prior to the Constitutional Court decision, Peevski alluded that his group in the National Assembly may provide support for the incumbent government if they were to lose their majority in the recalculation.{{Cite web |date=2025-03-13 |title=Пеевски обяви, че е готов да крепи кабинета |url=https://www.mediapool.bg/peevski-obyavi-che-e-gotov-da-krepi-kabineta-news369128.html|access-date=2025-03-13 |website=Mediapool.bg |language=bg-BG}} After the decision, Borisov declared that the government would fall if Peevski did not support its budget.{{Cite web |title=Peevski Asserts Right to Lead in Bulgaria, Borissov Backs Him: 'Without Peevski, No Budget or Decisions' - Novinite.com - Sofia News Agency |url=https://www.novinite.com/articles/231300/Peevski+Asserts+Right+to+Lead+in+Bulgaria,+Borissov+Backs+Him:+%E2%80%98Without+Peevski,+No+Budget+or+Decisions%E2%80%99 |access-date=2025-03-14 |website=www.novinite.com}} As DPS–Dogan had previously said they would refuse to support a government which included Peevski, they sought clarity on what the parliamentary majority of the government was.{{Cite web |last=Маринова |first=Даяна |date=2025-03-14 |title=ДПС-ДПС иска яснота за парламентарното мнозинство |url=https://news.bg/politics/dps-dps-iska-yasnota-za-parlamentarnoto-mnozinstvo.html |access-date=2025-03-14 |website=News.bg |language=bulgarian}} On 17 March, Prime Minister [[Rosen Zhelyazkov|Zhelyazkov]] insisted that the government was stable, and there was no alternative majority that could be formed.{{Cite news |date=2025-03-17 |title=Правителството е стабилно и няма алтернатива, заяви премиерът |url=https://bntnews.bg/news/pravitelstvoto-e-stabilno-i-nyama-alternativa-zayavi-premierat-1331140news.html |work=[[Bulgarian National Television]]}} Regardless, Peevski said that the government would be forced to work with him, and said his party would support the budget.{{Cite web |title=Оттук нататък ще работят с Пеевски, защото хората решават така, коментира Делян Пеевски |url=https://www.bta.bg/bg/news/bulgaria/854465-ottuk-natatak-shte-rabotyat-s-peevski-zashtoto-horata-reshavat-taka-komentira- |access-date=2025-03-19 |website=www.bta.bg |language=bg}} On 20 March, DPS–Peevski and the government, without DPS–Dogan, elected a member of the Constitutional Court.{{Cite web |date=2025-03-20 |title="За тяснопартийни цели". ГЕРБ, БСП, ИТН и ДПС-Пеевски избраха Орлин Колев за конституционен съдия |url=https://www.svobodnaevropa.bg/a/orlin-kolev-gerb-bsp-itn-peevski-jonko-grozev-konstitucionen-sadia/33354113.html |access-date=2025-03-20 |website=Свободна Европа |language=bg}} Following the disputes, on 1 April, the top figures of DPS–Dogan met to reconsider their position supporting the government.{{Cite web |date=2025-04-01 |title="Не сме по крайните действия". ДПС-Доган решава дали да остане част от мнозинството (обновена) |url=https://www.mediapool.bg/ne-sme-po-krainite-deistviya-dps-dogan-reshava-dali-da-ostane-chast-ot-mnozinstvoto-obnovena-news369773.html |access-date=2025-04-01 |website=Mediapool.bg |language=bg-BG}} They decided to continue the support for the cabinet until Bulgaria joined the [[Eurozone]], but said they would set conditions on their support for the government.{{Cite web |title=ДПС-ДПС с решение: Продължават подкрепата за кабинета до конвергентния доклад за eврото |url=https://btvnovinite.bg/bulgaria/dps-dps-s-reshenie-prodalzhavat-podkrepata-za-kabineta-do-konvergentnija-doklad-za-evroto.html |access-date=2025-04-01 |website=bTV Новините |language=bg}} On 15 April, DPS–Dogan announced they would withdraw their support for the government. The government said it would continue to govern.{{Cite web |date=2025-04-15 |title=ДПС-Доган реши: Напуска управляващото мнозинство |url=https://www.mediapool.bg/dps-dogan-reshi-napuska-upravlyavashtoto-mnozinstvo-news370294.html |access-date=2025-04-16 |website=Mediapool.bg |language=bg-BG}} The government was set to face a vote of no confidence on 16 April, but it survived as Peevski said he would support the government, while PP–DB declared they would abstain.{{Cite web |title=Това правителство ще оцелее, според лидера на "Величие" Ивелин Михайлов |url=https://www.bta.bg/bg/news/bulgaria/873237-tova-pravitelstvo-shte-otselee-spored-lidera-na-velichie-ivelin-mihaylov |access-date=2025-04-16 |website=www.bta.bg |language=bg}} ==References== {{reflist}} {{Bulgarian elections}} [[Category:2024 elections in Europe|Bulgaria]] [[Category:2024 elections in Bulgaria|Parliamentary]] [[Category:October 2024 in Bulgaria|Parliamentary election]] [[Category:Parliamentary elections in Bulgaria|2024 10]]
