Snap parliamentary elections were held in [[Greece]] on 25 June 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/may/24/greece-to-hold-fresh-elections-on-25-june |title=Senior judge to lead Greek caretaker government until fresh June election |work=The Guardian |date=24 May 2023 |access-date=28 May 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://tvxs.gr/news/ellada/oristika-se-nees-ekloges-stis-25-ioynioy-odigeitai-i-xora |title=Οριστικά σε νέες εκλογές στις 25 Ιουνίου οδηγείται η χώρα |publisher=Tvxs.gr |date=22 February 2016 |accessdate=23 May 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ieidiseis.gr/politiki/198985/stin-ptd-me-ta-apotelesmata-ton-eklogon-o-tasoulas-ksekinoyn-oi-dierevnitikes|title=Ολοταχώς για νέες εκλογές στις 25 Ιουνίου – Ο Μητσοτάκης θα επιστρέψει το απόγευμα τη διερευνητική εντολή|website=www.ieidiseis.gr |date=22 May 2023 }}</ref> All 300 seats in the [[Hellenic Parliament]] were contested. Prime Minister [[Kyriakos Mitsotakis]] called for the snap vote after the [[May 2023 Greek parliamentary election|May 2023 elections]] did not result in any party gaining a majority, although his centre-right [[New Democracy (Greece)|New Democracy]] made unanticipated gains and increased its share of the vote. As a result, no coalition government was formed by any of the parties eligible to do so.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://abcnews.go.com/Business/wireStory/greeces-center-landslide-election-victory-new-vote-form-99500712|title=Greece faces new election in weeks, after center right triumphs but falls short of majority|first=Nicholas|last=Paphitis|website=ABC News}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.euronews.com/2023/05/21/greek-election-live-blog-mitsotakis-takes-the-lead-headed-to-second-vote|title=Greek voters face new election in June as New Democracy seeks majority|date=21 May 2023|website=euronews}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=22 May 2023 |title=Mitsotakis calls for second Greek election, possibly on June 25 |url=https://www.politico.eu/article/kyriakos-mitsotakis-new-democracy-greece-election-june-25/ |access-date=22 May 2023 |website=POLITICO |language=en}}</ref>

In contrast to the May elections, the June vote used a [[majority bonus system]], making a [[majority government]] more likely.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Greece's prime minister wins an election, but lacks a majority |newspaper=The Economist |url=https://www.economist.com/europe/2023/05/21/greeces-prime-minister-wins-an-election-but-lacks-a-majority |access-date=2023-06-07 |issn=0013-0613}}</ref> On 25 May 2023, as required by Greece's constitution, President [[Katerina Sakellaropoulou]] appointed [[Ioannis Sarmas]] as [[caretaker prime minister]] until the formation of the next government following the elections.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Papadimas |first1=Lefteris |title=Greece appoints caretaker PM ahead of June repeat election |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/greek-party-leaders-meet-coalition-talks-open-way-new-elections-2023-05-24/ |access-date=25 May 2023 |work=Reuters |date=25 May 2023}}</ref>

New Democracy increased their number of seats in parliament, achieving a majority, while the main opposition [[Syriza]] lost seats. Minor parties [[Spartans (Greek political party)|Spartans]], [[Victory (Greek political party)|Victory]], and [[Course of Freedom]] entered parliament for the first time.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boutri |first=Alexandra |date=2023-06-30 |title=Greek Left Leaders Betrayed the Working Class. Conservatives Won a Landslide. |url=https://truthout.org/articles/greek-left-leaders-betrayed-the-working-class-conservatives-won-a-landslide/ |access-date=2023-07-02 |website=Truthout |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Electoral system==
[[File:June 2023 Greek election - ballots.jpg|thumb|180px|The ballots in a polling station in Argos]]
[[File:Polling booth in Greece (June 2023 election).jpg|thumb|The polling booth in a polling station in Argos]]
[[New Democracy (Greece)|New Democracy]] has been a proponent of [[majority bonus system|majority bonuses]] since 1974.  Soon after returning to power in the [[2019 Greek parliamentary election|2019 parliamentary election]], they passed a new electoral law to reinstate the bonus that had been eliminated by the [[SYRIZA]]-[[Independent Greeks|ANEL]] coalition government's 2016 law (which established a [[Proportional representation|purely proportional system]] with a 3% electoral threshold), albeit under a very different formula. The party list coming first with at least 25% of the votes would receive 20 extra seats, with one more seat for every half percentage point above 25%, to a maximum of 50 extra seats at 40% (or more) of the votes. Once this bonus has been attributed, the proper proportional distribution begins for the remaining seats, which can range from 250 if one party gathered at least 40%, to 300 if no party reached 25%.<ref>{{cite web |date=24 January 2020 |title=Parliament votes to change election law |url=http://www.ekathimerini.com/248820/article/ekathimerini/news/parliament-votes-to-change-election-law |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200125025345/http://www.ekathimerini.com/248820/article/ekathimerini/news/parliament-votes-to-change-election-law |archive-date=25 January 2020 |access-date=25 January 2020 |website=www.ekathimerini.com}}</ref> This 2020 law would take effect starting from the next Greek election after the May 2023 election.

A 2019 law granted the right to vote for Greeks abroad who have lived for two years in Greece during the previous 35 years and who have submitted a [[tax return]] during the year of the election or the previous year. Voters from abroad choose the national-wide ballot of their desired party without choosing candidates, and their vote is counted equally in final results.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Με συντριπτική πλειοψηφία το νομοσχέδιο για την ψήφο των αποδήμων |date=12 December 2019 |url=https://www.kathimerini.gr/politics/1055771/me-syntriptiki-pleiopsifia-to-nomoschedio-gia-tin-psifo-ton-apodimon/ |website=kathimerini.gr |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221222211932/https://www.kathimerini.gr/politics/1055771/me-syntriptiki-pleiopsifia-to-nomoschedio-gia-tin-psifo-ton-apodimon/ |archive-date=22 December 2022 |access-date=21 May 2023}}</ref> [[Compulsory voting|Voting is theoretically compulsory]], with voter registration being automatic,<ref>{{cite web |title=Constitution of Greece |url=http://www.hellenicparliament.gr/UserFiles/f3c70a23-7696-49db-9148-f24dce6a27c8/001-156%20aggliko.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171114142907/http://www.hellenicparliament.gr/UserFiles/f3c70a23-7696-49db-9148-f24dce6a27c8/001-156%20aggliko.pdf |archive-date=14 November 2017 |access-date=5 November 2011 |work=[[Hellenic Parliament]] |quote=Article 51, Clause 5: The exercise of the right to vote is compulsory.}}</ref> but the penalties and sanctions in place for those who do not vote are unenforced.<ref>{{cite web |script-title=el:Υποχρεωτική η ψήφος αλλά "παγωμένες" οι κυρώσεις |trans-title=Voting is mandatory, but penalties "frozen" |url=http://archive.enet.gr/online/online_text/c=112,dt=12.06.2004,id=20721500 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130217164234/http://archive.enet.gr/online/online_text/c=112,dt=12.06.2004,id=20721500 |archive-date=17 February 2013 |access-date=7 November 2011 |work=[[Eleftherotypia]] |language=el}}</ref>

==Opinion polls==
{{Main|Opinion polling for the June 2023 Greek parliamentary election}}
[[File:OpinionPollingGreeceLegislativeElectionJune2023.svg|center|thumb|700x700px|[[Local regression]] trend line of poll results from 21 May 2023 to the present day, with each line corresponding to a political party and a 7-day average compared to the May election]]

==Results==
New Democracy won 41% of the vote, which allowed it to gain 50 bonus seats. This led to New Democracy winning a majority of seats. Syriza won nearly 18% of the vote. The newly created Spartans party won 4.7% of the vote, which allowed it to enter Parliament.<ref>{{cite web | last=Smith | first=Helena | title=Greek voters propel new far-right Spartans group into parliament | website=the Guardian | date=26 June 2023 | url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/jun/26/greek-voters-propel-new-far-right-spartans-group-into-parliament | access-date=16 August 2023}}</ref> Overall, eight parties crossed the 3% threshold to enter Parliament. The turnout was at 54%, which was 7 [[Percentage point|pp]] lower than the turnout in the May election. Reacting to his party's victory, Mitsotakis said, "The people have given us a safe majority. Major reforms will go ahead quickly." According to political analyst Nick Malkoutzis, "Mitsotakis has been rewarded by voters as the leader who has led Greece out of a [[Greek debt crisis|severe debt crisis]] and three international bailouts back into a growth path. Someone who has kept, at least some, of his pledges which is more than many in Greece had previously done."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-65997486|title=Greek elections: Mitsotakis hails conservative win as mandate for reform|last=Kirby|first=Paul|date=25 June 2023|via=www.bbc.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cnn.com/2023/06/25/europe/kyriakos-mitsotakis-elections-victory-intl/index.html|title=Greek prime minister earns resounding electoral win, as far right makes gains|first=Elinda|last=Labropoulou|date=25 June 2023|website=CNN}}</ref>
